title: After Spate of Deaths, MP Deploys Medical Teams Outside Liquor Shops
description: National | Medical teams in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar district have begun screening regular liquor consumers outside liquor outlets to identify people.
author: PratidinTime News Desk
content:
Medical teams in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar district have begun screening regular liquor consumers outside liquor outlets to identify people at risk of health complications due to prolonged alcohol consumption.
The initiative follows a series of deaths in the district, including 20 fatalities in a suspected spurious liquor tragedy in September. The campaign involves doctors conducting health check-ups, collecting blood samples and providing medical advice to customers.
According to district authorities, liquor shop operators have been asked to identify their most frequent customers, including those who arrive before outlets open at 8 am. These lists are being used to identify chronic drinkers for medical examinations.
Over the first two days of the campaign, medical teams screened 147 people and collected 144 blood samples for liver and kidney function tests. The screenings were conducted across Sagar, Deori, Rahli, Khurai and Bina.
Chief Medical and Health Officer Dr Devesh Pateria said the exercise had identified several cases of chronic alcoholism and possible liver damage. Medical teams are also providing Vitamin B1 and multivitamin supplements to address nutritional deficiencies.
Collector Dilip Kumar Yadav said the initiative aims to create awareness about the health risks associated with excessive alcohol consumption and encourage people to seek timely medical care.
The administration is also reaching out to habitual drinkers through health centres and village-level visits to expand the screening exercise.

title: Mumbai Police Deploys Drug Testing Van At Concerts, 12 Test Positive In First Screening
description: National | Mumbai police has introduced a mobile Anti-Narcotics Investigation and Forensic Van to detect suspected drug consumption and identify narcotic substances at concerts and large public gatherings.
author: PratidinTime News Desk
content:
Mumbai police have introduced a mobile Anti-Narcotics Investigation and Forensic Van to detect suspected drug consumption and identify narcotic substances at concerts and large public gatherings.
The van made its first deployment at a concert at Mahalaxmi Race Course on Sunday, where 55 people were screened. Of them, 12 tested positive for drug consumption, including 11 for cannabis and one for cocaine.
The vehicle is equipped with a Dräger DrugTest device, which uses oral fluid samples to screen individuals for drug consumption. A swab is collected from the person's mouth and analysed, with the process taking around five minutes.
It also carries two handheld devices, TruNarc and Gemini, which use laser-based technology to identify suspected narcotic substances without opening their packaging. The devices have databases covering thousands of narcotics and other chemicals.
The van also features 360-degree cameras and facilities for crime scene photography and videography. Its evidence management system uses blockchain technology to make digital records difficult to alter or tamper with.
The 12 people who tested positive during the first deployment were booked under the NDPS Act and served notices under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), police said.
Inaugurated by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on November 21, the unit will be deployed at concerts and other large public gatherings as part of Mumbai Police's Mega City Policing initiative.

title: Indian Railways May Scrap RAC Ticket System Amid Digital Changes
description: Indian Railways may scrap the 40-year-old RAC system, which allows two passengers to share a single berth at full fare, citing advancements in digital ticketing. |National | Top Stories|
author: DY365
content:
Indian Railways May Scrap RAC Ticket System Amid Digital Changes
Indian Railways may scrap the 40-year-old RAC system, which allows two passengers to share a single berth at full fare, citing advancements in digital ticketing.
New Delhi: The Indian Railways may discontinue its Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) facility as senior railway officials believe that digital technology has made the system less important.
Introduced in 1983-84, the RAC system allows two passengers to share a single berth while paying the full ticket fare. It was originally introduced to help waiting-list passengers get accommodation if confirmed ticket holders failed to board their trains.
However, railway officials now believe that digital ticketing systems can manage vacant berths more efficiently without the need for RAC.
According to officials, Train Ticket Examiners (TTEs) use Hand Held Terminals (HHTs), which are directly connected to the railway reservation system. If a passenger does not board the train, the TTE can update the status digitally, making the vacant berth available for another passenger from the next station.
Officials also believe that removing RAC could reduce the chances of irregularities in berth allocation by TTEs. They would be required to complete ticket verification within a fixed time and update the system about passengers who fail to turn up.
The Railways also does not lose revenue when confirmed passengers fail to board, as such passengers are not eligible for refunds under the rules introduced in 2015. The vacant berth can then be offered to another passenger at the full fare.
The Railway Ministry is reportedly examining the proposal. The Parliamentary Public Accounts Committee had earlier recommended giving partial refunds to RAC passengers.

title: Rahul Gandhi Alleges Rajiv Gandhi’s Security Was Withdrawn to Get Him Killed
description: Rahul Gandhi has alleged that his father, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s security was deliberately withdrawn to facilitate his assassination, during a discussion with Sonia and Priyanka Gandhi.|  Top Stories | Politics|
author: DY365
content:
Rahul Gandhi Alleges Rajiv Gandhi’s Security Was Withdrawn to Get Him Killed
Rahul Gandhi has alleged that his father, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s security was deliberately withdrawn to facilitate his assassination, during a discussion with Sonia and Priyanka Gandhi about Sonia’s memoir.
New Delhi: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has alleged that security was deliberately withdrawn from his father, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, which he believes was intentional to get him killed.
Rahul made the statement during a family discussion with his mother, Sonia Gandhi along with sister, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. They were talking about Sonia Gandhi’s recently released memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which shares personal experiences and important moments from her life.
During the conversation, Sonia Gandhi recalled an incident from Rajiv Gandhi’s visit to Bihar when he was the Leader of the Opposition. She said Rajiv travelled in an open jeep and faced protests, stone-pelting and angry crowds during the tour.
Rahul was with his father during the visit and became very worried about his father's safety. Sonia recalled that after returning home, Rahul warned her that something terrible could happen to his father if his security was not upgraded. He even feared that he might soon have to return home for his father's funeral.
Speaking about the incident, Rahul said he had been concerned about his father's security even before the Bihar visit. He had repeatedly raised the issue and also argued with his father Rajiv Gandhi about it.
Rahul described the Bihar tour as the final warning sign and alleged that the withdrawal of his father's security was a deliberate decision, not an accident.

title: BJP and SAD Renew Alliance After Six-Year Break Ahead of Punjab Elections
description: Politics | National | Top Stories| Ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal have reunited after a six-year break over the Centre's farm laws.
author: DY365
content:
BJP and SAD Renew Alliance After Six-Year Break Ahead of Punjab Elections
Ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal have reunited after a six-year break over the Centre's farm laws.
New Delhi: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have renewed their political partnership after six years, as the two parties have come together again ahead of the next Punjab Assembly elections.
The decision was announced at a joint press conference in New Delhi on Tuesday. Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal attended the event on the 556th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev.
Amit Shah welcomed the SAD back into the National Democratic Alliance (NDA). He said the alliance would work for Punjab and strengthen Hindu-Sikh unity. He also said that removing drugs from Punjab would be a top priority, with a target to make the state drug-free by December 31, 2029.
Sukhbir Singh Badal described the reunion as an emotional bond rather than just a political partnership. He said the alliance would work for the people of Punjab, the Sikh community and the country.
Badal also credited his late father, former Chief Minister Prakash Singh Badal, for building ties between the two parties. He announced that Prime Minister Narendra Modi would attend a rally in Moga on December 8 to mark his father's birth anniversary.
The BJP and SAD first joined hands in November 1996 and formed governments in Punjab in 1997, 2007 and 2012. However, their partnership ended in September 2020 as the SAD left the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws. The laws were later withdrawn after a year-long farmers' protest.
The reunion marks the end of their six-year seperation.
|Punjab News |

title: 9 Jun 2026 · 1 min read Freedom 250 memorial motorcycle rally honours US-India security cooperation KOLKATA, 8 Jun: US Consul General Kathy Giles-Diaz and West Bengal Cabinet minister Dilip Ghosh on Monday took to the streets of Kolkata to honour a security partnership between India and the United States. The leaders…
description: KOLKATA, 8 Jun: US Consul General Kathy Giles-Diaz and West Bengal Cabinet minister Dilip Ghosh on Monday took to the streets of Kolkata to honour a security partnership between India and the United States. The leaders…
content:
KOLKATA, 8 Jun: US Consul General Kathy Giles-Diaz and West Bengal Cabinet minister Dilip Ghosh on Monday took to the streets of Kolkata to honour a security partnership between India and the United States.
The leaders celebrated the first Joy-Freedom Ride motorcycle rally, followed by a wreath-laying ceremony at the American Centre. The event, part of the Freedom 250 campaign, celebrated decades of partnership built on mutual trust and shared values, and the memory of five Kolkata Police officers killed defending the American Centre from a terrorist attack in 2002: Pijush Sarker, Ujjal Burman, Suresh Hembram, Anup Mondal, and Sheikh Ashraf Ali.
“Just as a motorcycle needs two wheels to move forward, the US-India partnership relies on our nations working together,” Consul General Giles-Diaz said. “Our shared vision for a free, open, and secure Indo-Pacific drives us forward. This vision requires resilience and vigilance, and dedicated people like the Kolkata police. What grew out of the 2002 attack is the network of partners who help us protect the ideas of freedom and peace every day.”
The rally brought together more than 250 riders representing American diplomats, Indian police officers, motorcycle enthusiasts, and business partners in an early morning city tour starting at the American Centre and passing the Victoria Memorial, Princep Ghat, and Laal Bazar, home to the Kolkata police headquarters.
The rally was organised in partnership with US Consulate Kolkata’s Overseas Security Advisory Council, which fosters security cooperation between US diplomatic missions and the American private sector abroad.

title: 10 Apr 2026 · 1 min read VIT Chennai celebrates university day CHENNAI, 8 Apr: The Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) here in Tamil Nadu celebrated its University Day on Tuesday. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Indian Bank, Binod Kumar, in his address,…
description: CHENNAI, 8 Apr: The Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) here in Tamil Nadu celebrated its University Day on Tuesday. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Indian Bank, Binod Kumar, in his address,…
content:
CHENNAI, 8 Apr: The Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) here in Tamil Nadu celebrated its University Day on Tuesday.
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Indian Bank, Binod Kumar, in his address, encouraged students to prepare themselves for a rapidly changing world.
He stressed the importance of continuous effort and adaptability to overcome challenges and seize opportunities. He also highlighted the need for innovation with a focus on improving the end-user experience.
Emphasizing the role of knowledge and character, Kumar said that knowledge is one thing which will help you in shaping yourself. Knowledge can take you up to a stage, beyond that, it is your characteristics which will shape you,” he noted.
Alumnus of VIT Chennai, Major Vaibhav Chaurasia urged students to draw inspiration from their surroundings and focus on positive influences. He urged them to remain resilient, maintain self-belief. “Never give up, never have a doubt in yourself. Things will not work out and things will go wrong, but you have to keep working hard and always do things right,” he added.
In his presidential address, Founder and Chancellor of VIT Dr. G. Viswanathan underscored the transformative power of education. He stated that education uplifts not only individuals and families but also society, the state, and the nation as a whole.
He emphasized that achieving the vision of a developed nation depends on universal access to quality education and economic growth driven by knowledge.
Medals and certificates were distributed to meritorious and outstanding students in recognition of their academic and overall excellence during the celebration.
VIT’s Vice President Dr. G. V. Selvam, VIT’s Pro-Vice Chancellor Prof. T. Thyagarajan, Director Prof. K. Sathiyanarayanan and Additional Registrar Prof. P.K.Manoharan were also present in the function.

title: "UP has shed 'Bimaru' tag to become revenue-surplus": Brajesh Pathak rallies communities for 3rd BJP term
description: According to Pathak, detailed deliberations were held on how Uttar Pradesh shed the stigma of being a 'bimaru' state to emerge as a revenue-surplus economy. He highlighted that over the last 10 years, criminals were jailed, law and order improved significantly, and both the state's budget and per capita income tripled, boosting the self-confidence of the state's residents.
content:
Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh) [India], November 25 (ANI): Stepping up outreach ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak convened a 'Samajik Sampark' (social outreach) meeting in Lucknow on Wednesday.
The meeting brought together community leaders from across the state to build consensus for a third consecutive Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government.
Addressing representatives drawn from various communities representing Uttar Pradesh's 25 crore population, Pathak said the gathering — held at his official residence under the theme of fostering 'Samajik Samrasta' (social harmony) — focused on the state's governance record over the past decade.
According to Pathak, detailed deliberations were held on how Uttar Pradesh shed the stigma of being a 'bimaru' state to emerge as a revenue-surplus economy.
He highlighted that over the last 10 years, criminals were jailed, law and order improved significantly, and both the state's budget and per capita income tripled, boosting the self-confidence of the state's residents.
Pathak added that the discussions centred on securing an overwhelming mandate for the BJP to form the government for a third straight term. He noted that community leaders present at the platform resolved to work together in unity across the state to ensure the party returns to power with a massive majority.
"The BJP in Uttar Pradesh has organised a 'Samajik Sampark' meeting. Leaders from various communities, representing the 25 crore people who make up the state's population, were brought together on a single platform to foster 'Samajik Samrasta' and engage in discussions. A detailed discussion was held on the state's transformation over the last 10 years: how it shed the stigma of being a 'bimaru' state to become a revenue-surplus state; how criminals were sent to jail; how law and order improved; how per capita income tripled; and how the state's budget also tripled. The self-confidence of the people of Uttar Pradesh has grown. There was an in-depth deliberation on how the BJP could secure a massive mandate to form the government in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term. Leaders from all these communities have resolved that, by working together with a sense of unity across the state, they will ensure that the BJP forms the government once again with an overwhelming majority," he said.
The BJP-led NDA is aiming for a third consecutive term in 2027 in Uttar Pradesh after winning the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections. In the 2017 polls, the BJP had won 312 seats, which shrank to 255 in 2022. Even with a reduced number of seats, the BJP-led NDA comfortably crossed the majority mark of 202.
During the event, the Deputy Chief Minister also accused the Samajwadi Party (SP) of practising appeasement politics and neglecting broader social representation.
The BJP's social consolidation drive comes at a time when the opposition INDIA bloc partners — the Samajwadi Party and the Congress — are engaged in tense seat-sharing negotiations for the 403-member Assembly.
Ahead of their second round of talks in New Delhi on Tuesday, SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav announced that his party had formally offered 26 seats to the Congress.
The offer comprises two constituencies won by the Congress in 2022, four where it finished runner-up, and 20 seats where the SP had polled substantial votes.
It falls significantly short of the Congress's reported demand for 120 to 130 constituencies.
Adding to the friction within the opposition camp, the Samajwadi Party on Tuesday unilaterally released its first list of five candidates — naming four sitting MLAs — even as alliance talks remained unresolved.
Responding to the developments on Wednesday, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav urged the Congress to prioritise winnability over seat numbers, stating that "winning seats brings respect".
He proposed that joint candidates contest under the banner of the INDIA bloc and his party's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) formula to challenge the ruling NDA in 2027. (ANI)

title: Cabinet approves continuation of Postal Operations Scheme with outlay of Rs 1,141 Crore
description: The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme “Postal Operations” during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with a proposed outlay of Rs 1,141 crore. The scheme seeks to strengthen postal infrastructure, improve operational efficiency and support the growing requirements of logistics, e-commerce and digital service delivery across the country.
content:
New Delhi [India], November 25 (ANI): The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme “Postal Operations” during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with a proposed outlay of Rs 1,141 crore. The scheme seeks to strengthen postal infrastructure, improve operational efficiency and support the growing requirements of logistics, e-commerce and digital service delivery across the country. 
With one of the world’s largest postal networks comprising 1.65 lakh post offices, including 1,49,655 post offices in rural areas, India Post continues to serve as an important platform for delivery of mail, parcels, banking, insurance and other citizen-centric services, particularly in remote and underserved regions. 
Apart from its core postal operations, India Post provides a wide range of public services through initiatives such as Post Office Savings Bank (POSB), India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), Postal Life Insurance (PLI), Aadhaar enrolment and updation, Passport Services through Post Office Passport Seva Kendras, KYC verification services and support to rural artisans through Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs). 
The scheme would support modernisation of postal infrastructure, strengthen last-mile delivery, improve logistics efficiency, promote financial inclusion and enhance customer-centric service delivery across the country. The proposal also aligns with the broader objectives of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. 
The scheme is intended to be implemented over a period of five years from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. 
The Postal Operations Scheme comprises six sub-schemes.
Rural Business and Access to Postal Network, with Rs. 120 crore, is focused on infrastructure upgrades, standardised branding and better resource utilisation to transform post offices, particularly in rural areas, into efficient and citizen-centric service hubs. The component aims to strengthen financial inclusion, digital connectivity and local economic development while improving last-mile delivery and enhancing access to postal and citizen-centric services in underserved regions. 
Mail Network Optimisation with Rs. 575 crore envisages modernisation of mail operations through centralised delivery systems, mechanisation, advanced IT solutions under Advanced Postal Technology (APT 2.0), GIS-based services and upgraded infrastructure. The initiative also includes strengthening delivery post offices, mail handling systems, Mail Motor Service (MMS) workshops, Road Transport Network and modern smart 24x7 letter boxes to improve operational efficiency, transparency, service quality and logistical reliability across the network. 
Parcel Network Optimisation with Rs. 278 crore includes construction of Parcel Hubs and expansion of Parcel Packaging Units (PPUs) aligned with the redesigned sorting framework to streamline parcel movement, reduce handling points, ease capacity constraints and improve transit times. The component also aims to support growing parcel volumes from e-commerce and rural markets through purpose-built facilities, standardised secure packaging and enhanced operational flexibility while improving customer trust and strengthening India Post’s competitiveness in the logistics sector.  
Infrastructure Upgrade and Augmentation of Infrastructure for International Mail with Rs 8 crore aims to strengthen international mail services by upgrading Foreign Post Offices (FPOs) and Sub Foreign Post Offices (SFPOs) to improve infrastructure and expedite processing of international consignments. The initiative also includes marketing and advertising through Postal / RMS Division and positions India Post as a reliable international logistics provider while improving compliance, technology integration and export logistics support. 
Marketing functions, including Quality of Service, with Rs 100 crore, are focused on promotion, branding, outreach and customer engagement through multi-channel campaigns across television, digital, radio, print and outdoor platforms. The component also includes participation in events and exhibitions, social media campaigns, direct marketing and expansion of Dak Chaupal activities to deepen grassroots engagement, especially in rural and underserved areas. In addition, it envisages infrastructure upgrades, studio facilities, ICT enhancements, market research, influencer engagement and third-party evaluation mechanisms to improve quality of service and strengthen a customer-centric approach.  
Philately Operations with Rs. 60 crore proposes initiatives to promote philately through exhibitions, seminars, quizzes, school philatelic clubs and innovative stamp designs including scented, holographic and 3D stamps. The component also includes digital outreach activities, programmes such as the Dhai Akhar letter-writing competition and SPARSH scholarship, modernisation of production and fulfilment centres, market research and international collaboration, with the objective of revitalising philately as an engaging educational and cultural activity while also improving operational efficiency and revenue potential.
The cabinet also approved the proposal of the Department of Posts for the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme, the Estates Management Scheme, during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme carries a total financial outlay of Rs.1,491 crores over a five-year period.
The scheme aims to comprehensively transform and modernise the estates infrastructure of the Department of Posts. It focuses heavily on the construction, reconstruction, renovation, and uniform branding of post offices and residential colonies, along with the preservation of India’s heritage postal buildings. This modernisation strategy directly supports first-mile delivery, fosters financial inclusion and enhances citizen-centric service delivery nationwide, aligning with the broader visions of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.
As one of the world's largest postal networks with 1.65 lakh post offices (including 1,49,385 in rural areas), India Post remains a critical vehicle for mail, banking (POSB/IPPB), insurance (PLI), Aadhaar services, Post Office Passport Seva Kendras and rural artisan support via Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs).
The scheme is scheduled for phased implementation over a five-year horizon, starting from FY 2026-27 through FY 2030-31.
New Construction with Rs. 280 Crore will focus on building 190 departmental postal buildings on vacant departmental plots to replace currently rented spaces and eliminate rental liabilities.
Reconstruction with Rs. 108 Crore will be used for demolishing and rebuilding 50 dilapidated departmental postal structures to ensure long-term structural safety.
Renovation & Branding with Rs 318 Crore will focus on upgrading and establishing uniform branding across 2,550 departmental SubPost Offices as per SPA guidelines.
Rented Post Office Upgrades with Rs 37.50 crore will focus on upgrading and uniformly branding 2,500 post offices operating out of rented premises
Heritage Preservation with Rs. 180 Crore will focus on restoring and preserving 20 landmark heritage postal buildings to safeguard the historical legacy of the department.
Colony Renovation Rs 357.50 crore will revamp 150 high-demand postal residential colonies to elevate employee welfare and satisfaction.
Allied & Inclusive Activities with Rs. 100 Crore will implement sustainable features (Solar power, Rainwater Harvesting) and universal accessibility infrastructure (ramps, Braille signage) under the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, alongwith gender-focused additions like ladies' toilets and feeding rooms.
Integrated Technology Centre with Rs. 100 Crore will set up a permanent physical infrastructure for the Centre for Excellence in Postal Technology (CEPT) in Bengaluru to drive Advanced Postal Technology (APT) services and support the indigenous open-source tech stack. (ANI)

title: Maharashtra awards Adani company a contract to supply power using power from another Adani company
description: The government overruled objections from competitors that the group’s company would have access to advantageous information.
author: Shreegireesh Jalihal
content:
In March 2026, the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited, or MSEDCL, invited bids for the supply of 2,500 MW of electricity from companies willing to supply uninterrupted power, with a minimum of 51% drawn from traceable green energy.
On the surface, this appeared to be a routine tender. Uninterrupted, or round-the-clock, power packages are becoming increasingly popular in India because, rather than only focus on power generation, they ensure that end users receive a reliable electricity supply.
But documents accessed by Scroll reveal that several competing bidders raised concerns over a possible conflict of interest in the Maharashtra tender.
One of the companies in the fray was Adani Power. Other competing bidders objected to a clause in the tender that said that the winning bidder, as part of its round-the-clock supply package, would be bound to use solar power generated by another Adani-owned firm – Adani Renewable Energy Fifty-Five, which had an existing power-supply contract with MSEDCL.
In a pre-bid meeting that MSEDCL held with interested companies, one of the bidders stated: “We request not to allow the participation of any affiliate or Group company of M/s Adani Renewable Energy Fifty-Five Ltd… as it will create conflict of interest towards bidding in this tender and would provide an unfair advantage to their Affiliate and Group companies.”
Rather than lay out an argument for why this concern was unfounded, MSEDCL merely asserted that “no preferential treatment is provided to Adani Renewable Energy Fifty Five Ltd., or its Affiliate or Group Companies, under the bid documents. Therefore, there is no conflict of interest or unfair advantage to such companies, in case they participate in the bid process.”
It added that “there is no bid related information which is solely available to Adani Renewable Energy Fifty Five Ltd, or its Affiliate or Group Companies”.
Adani Power won the bid. This led to a tripartite agreement between two Adani Group companies and the Maharashtra state-owned firm.
Independent observers echoed concerns raised by the other firms. “When one of the competitors of the auction is responsible for supplying solar power which is part of the auction, then it raises questions about how fair the auction is,” said Dr Priyanshu Gupta, a researcher on coal and energy.
However, an Adani Power spokesperson dismissed these concerns, noting that they “were raised during the pre-bid discussions and were duly clarified by the competent authorities at that stage”.
The spokesperson stated that “Any suggestion that Adani enjoyed an advantageous position vis-à-vis other competing bidders is entirely misconceived and unsupported by the facts. Neither the solar generation profile nor the source of input power from an already-contracted solar project, merely because it happened to be associated with an Adani entity, conferred any advantage to Adani or disadvantage to competitors.”
Calculations by Scroll show that the cost of power to MSEDCL under the triangular arrangement is significantly higher than the cost under a conventional round-the-clock contract awarded earlier this year by a central government-run company to several bidders. It is also significantly higher than a cost estimate for uninterrupted solar power published by the State Bank of India.
MSEDCL did not respond to a request for comment.
The Adani spokesperson stated that the tendering and contracting process were “subject to adjudication by” the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission, “an independent quasi-judicial regulatory body”. The commission’s “assessment of the process is publicly available and open to scrutiny and challenge through the appropriate legal and regulatory mechanisms”, it added.
Tender-on-tender
The contract to which the March 2026 tender was linked dates back to October 2024. Under that deal, MSEDCL contracted the Adani Group to supply 5,000 MW solar power and 1,600 MW coal-powered electricity to Maharashtra for 25 years.
The solar power component was signed by Adani Renewables Energy Fifty-Five Limited. This firm, wholly owned by Adani Energy Solutions, was incorporated in December 2023, just four months before MSEDCL issued this tender.
Around a year-and-a-half later, MSEDCL issued a fresh tender. This one was for supplying a “round-the-clock” electricity package of 2,500 MW. When a company is contracted to provide such power, even if they rely on solar power, they are obligated to ensure that supply is continuous even when the weather is not sunny.
In this instance, while the deal would bind the winning bidder to supply 51% of the electricity from traceable green energy, the company was free to decide on the source for the remaining 49%. It could, for instance, use a renewable source, battery-stored power, or even thermal power.
Ahead of the bidding, MSEDCL held a meeting with interested companies, at which they could seek clarifications on the process and recommend changes to it. The details of these discussions were published online, with company names redacted – thus concealing information about which companies raised specific queries and concerns.
“The problem with this tripartite tender is that it potentially creates a vexed loop on a tender from two years ago,” Gupta said. “It also raises the question: did companies participating in the 2024 tender know that there will be another tender on top of that one? By issuing another tender on top of that one, the government runs the risk of vitiating the original auction as well.”
Competitors’ objections
MSEDCL’s 2026 tender specified that it would “make available” to the winning bidder 5,000 MW of solar power generated by Adani Renewable Energy Fifty-Five under an earlier contract, which the winning bidder would have to use to put together its round-the-clock supply package.
Overruling concerns about the participation of Adani group companies in the bid, the distributor stated, “the ability to source power under the Executed PPA is available to all bidders and there is no bid related information which is solely available to Adani Renewable Energy Fifty Five Ltd., or its Affiliate or Group Companies that would give rise to a conflict of interest”.
In the pre-bid meeting, some companies specifically asked whether they could use solar power from their own plants instead of Adani’s to fulfill the tender. The distributor overruled this request, making the use of Adani’s solar power supply mandatory for the winning bidder.
Companies also asked for more information about the “generation profile” of the Adani solar power plant that they would be tied down to under the tender. Such a profile comprises data about the amount of power that a plant produces over specific time periods. The information allows competitors to tailor their bids based on cost estimates and other factors dependent on the nature of the supply available to them.
MSEDCL turned down all such requests. It only stated that the Adani company had issued the “relevant consent/no objection” for the use of its power supply.
“How does a company bid without basic information like generation profile?” said Gupta. “If a company does not have access to data like generation profile, then it would not be an open tender anymore. Which will raise questions on whether a truly competitive price was discovered.”
No liability for Adani
Apart from questions about being tied down to Adani’s power supply, competing companies also raised a range of other concerns pertaining to the deal with Adani.
Many noted objections about a clause in the tender that appeared to free the Adani company of any liability if it did not supply the solar power to which the tender was linked. “As per the tender, bidders are permitted to enter into a tripartite agreement with Adani and MSEDCL for the supply of solar power,” one company stated. “However, Clause 5.1.6 absolves the solar supplier (Adani) of any liability on account of non-supply of solar power.”
This clause of the tender document states that “the bidder shall unconditionally commence power supply” from the determined date – but it adds, “In case Solar Power … from MSEDCL is not available due to any transmission constraints by such SSD,” referring to the scheduled supply date, “bidder shall still ensure supply of power under this PPA from the above SSD.”
Many companies pointed out that this was patently unfair – and that, on the one hand, the distributor was tying the companies down to using Adani’s solar power, but on the other hand, not guaranteeing that supply.
The companies demanded that the distributor “allow back-to-back liability sharing with the solar generator for its respective scope” – that is, that if they were obligated to use that supply, the Adani company bear liability for providing the solar power to the winning bidder, who would then bear the responsibility of providing the final supply to MSEDCL.
This was shot down with no explanation, and the line, “Tender conditions will prevail.” Driving this point home, the distributor noted that the bidding company would bear “complete responsibility for meeting RTC supply obligations as per Tender conditions, irrespective of the input solar power availability (5 GW)”.
Battery supply also linked to Adani
This was not the only clause of the tender document that tied bidders to the Adani group. In fact, the highest number of queries pertained to another condition – that if any bidder chose to supply part of the round-the-clock package through a “battery energy storage system”, this system would have to be located “at the same location as the Solar plant” which provided the allocated 5,000 MW of power, Adani’s plant in the village of Khavda, in Gujarat’s Kachchh district.
One company sought to know whether the distributor would provide land for such a plant under the contract if they needed it, “or if the developer is required to arrange the land”.
Another sought to know, “If land at the Adani site is not available, whether BESS” – a battery energy storage system – “installation at an alternate location on the Selected Bidder’s land is permissible while charging from the Adani solar plant, subject to applicable regulations.”
Here too, the power distributor stuck to its terms. It noted that such a storage system would have to be located at Adani’s Gujarat-based plant, and that procuring land to install this technology was “under Supplier’s scope”.
The cost
A closer analysis of the round-the-clock power deal also raises questions about the price that the state distributor agreed to pay for the electricity.
After winning the 2026 tender, Adani Power passed on contractual obligations to Powerpulse Trading Solutions – this was a subsidiary incorporated in February 2024, two months before MSEDCL issued the original tender, to which the 2026 tender was linked.
The resulting 2026 tripartite contract is between MSEDCL, Adani Renewable Energy Fifty-Five Limited and the Adani-owned Powerpulse Trading Solutions.
Under this contract, Adani Renewable Energy Fifty-Five supplies solar power to Adani Power. MSEDCL pays for this power, at Rs 2.7 per kWH, a price discovered from the 2024 auction.
Adani Power’s subsidiary, Powerpulse Trading Solutions, then delivers a round-the-clock package to MSEDCL. This supply is priced at Rs 5.9 per kWH, discovered in the 2026 auction – but since MSEDCL has already paid for the solar component to Adani Power, it subtracts Rs 2.7 per kWH from this payment.
The total cost to MSEDCL, then, is the same contracted rate of Rs 5.9 per kWH. Powerpulse is bound under the deal to guarantee a minimum of 80% of the contracted supply each year.
In June 2026, the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission issued an order approving of this tariff. The regulator noted that the tender in question was “unique and bespoke” and that “there are no recent tenders of similar construct, scale, risk allocation and performance obligations that have been awarded through tariff‑based competitive bidding”.
It compared the discovered tariff of Rs 5.90/kWh with one earlier Adani Group round-the-clock renewable energy tariff, of Rs 6.38 Rs/kWh, as well as numerous other thermal power supply tariffs. Referring to the latter, the regulator noted, “The discovered tariff of Rs. 5.90/kWh under the subject tender compares favorably with the above approved thermal levelized tariffs ranging from Rs 6.31/kWh to Rs 8.90/kWh, despite higher risk obligations on the supplier.” Thus, the regular granted its approval to the tariff.
But another recent round-the-clock tender resulted in a significantly lower price, even compared to the round-the-clock tariff the regulator considered. This tender was issued by the central government company the Solar Energy Corporation of India, for 1,000 MW of round-the-clock solar power – the price discovered in the process was between Rs 5.25 and Rs 5.26 per unit.
After that tender, contracts were awarded to seven developers. Juniper Green Energy and Hexa Climate Solutions were contracted to supply 230 MW and 150 MW respectively at Rs 5.26 per unit. Five other companies – Kengeri Prime Solar Power, Resolven Four Energy, Hero Solar Energy, EMIF II Holding and Purvah Green Power – were contracted for the remaining 620 MW at Rs 5.25 per unit. Under this tender, companies have to specifically use battery storage systems to ensure round-the-clock supply, and are bound to guarantee that they will supply at least 90% of the contracted energy each year.
The rate of Rs 5.9 per kWH under the tripartite agreement is 12.38% higher than the Rs 5.25 tariff discovered in SECI’s tender.
Using the 80% annual supply requirement in the MSEDCL contract as a basis for comparison, 2,500 MW would correspond to around 17.52 billion units of electricity a year. At MSEDCL’s Rs 5.90 tariff, that would amount to roughly Rs 2,58,400 crore over 25 years – the duration of the contract. At SECI’s Rs 5.25-Rs 5.26 tariff, the same quantity of electricity would cost around Rs 2,30,000 crore – approximately Rs 28,400 crore less.
An April 2026 analysis by the State Bank of India’s Centre of Excellence provides another figure for comparison. The analysis examines the economics of supplying renewable electricity around the clock using combinations of solar, wind and storage. The report presents such systems as an emerging way of providing reliable renewable power, rather than simply selling intermittent solar or wind electricity.
The SBI analysis provides an even lower benchmark under one of the round-the-clock configurations it examines, of Rs 4.70 per unit. At that price, the same 2,500 MW contract and assumed volume would cost roughly Rs 2,06,000 crore over 25 years – around Rs 52,000 crore less than the cost at the Rs 5.90 tariff approved for MSEDCL.
Gupta argued that the SBI calculations provided a reasonable estimate of the cost of round-the-clock power supply. “Costs for generating solar round-the-clock have fallen considerably,” he said. “I agree with the price estimate that SBI Centre for Excellence calculated.”
Power for data centres
In its order approving the tender, the electricity regulator noted that a key factor that MSEDCL cited in support of its request was that the state was “promoting data centres and other sunshine industries to support economic growth”. It noted, “Data centers, cloud computing, and AI have a massive energy footprint.”
It also explicitly singled out data centres as the intended consumers of this renewable power. “Expected end consumers of this RTC power are Data Centres for which the Traceable Green Power supply is mandatory for sustainability reporting and/or public disclosure,” it said.
The Adani Group has emerged as India’s largest player in setting up data centres. These include centres in Maharashtra – in 2024 and 2026, the group signed deals with the government to set up large renewable-energy-powered data centres in the state.
Adani Group’s disclosures to stock markets record electricity purchases by the group data centre arm from Powerpulse Trading Solutions, the Adani Power subsidiary that is fulfilling the Maharashtra round-the-clock tender. Scroll was unable to independently verify if these power purchases are from the tripartite agreement or from other Adani Group contracts.

title: Andhra Pradesh villages give a reality check to India’s 2030 malaria elimination target
description: In Adivasi hamlets, it is difficult to get a diagnosis for the mosquito-borne disease and even then patients are not treated properly due to low drug supplies.
author: Rohith Meesaraganda
content:
On May 2, a violent storm hit Peddaporlu, a hamlet surrounded by hills in the heart of Andhra Pradesh’s Eastern Ghats. Seetha, the village’s health volunteer, told me about a 14-year-old girl named Vaishnavi who had developed a severe headache, apparently after witnessing lightning strike the ground.
The nearest government Primary Health Centre ruled out lightning-related illness. Some medicines were prescribed. Vaishnavi’s headache worsened, she developed a fever and started shivering. Could it be what is locally called “chali-jwaram” (chills-fever)?
As a doctor with an NGO called the Rural Development Service Society who regularly visits Peddaporlu and other hamlets in the region, I realised that specialised attention was needed. But it was only available at the district hospital in Paderu, 45 kilometres away. When Seetha proposed this to Vaishnavi’s family, they remained silent.
Perhaps they were thinking of all the hills and valleys they would have to traverse. Torrential downpours frequently wash away the mud roads that connect hamlets like Peddaporlu to the outside world. No road means no medical services.
The district hospital odyssey
Eventually, Vaishnavi’s family agreed to take her to Paderu, the headquarters of Alluri Sitharamaraju district. We spent most of the next seven days standing in queues at the district hospital, carrying around blood samples for testing.
Vaishnavi was not admitted to the ward. The hospital does not have facilities for overnight stays. The very weak Vaishnavi and her family travelled back and forth between Peddaporlu and Paderu three times on a two-wheeler.
Around 270 kilometres later and after over Rs 1,000 had been spent on fuel, the doctors – realising that Vaishnavi had become very frail and her platelet count was dropping rapidly – urged us to take her to King George Hospital in Visakhapatnam, 106 kilometres away.
“Few who go up to KGH actually come back”, is a sentiment I have heard too often from health volunteers. Vaishnavi’s mother declared that she would rather take her daughter to a guru-guniya – a local faith healer – than send her to King George Hospital. The guru-guniya would sacrifice a goat or a pig to free Vaishnavi from a demon or a curse.
Confused and overwhelmed, we finally decided to try our luck at a private hospital in Paderu. There, Vaishnavi was diagnosed with malaria and treatment began.
Vaishnavi’s family earns a living by selling its agricultural produce to private contractors, who buy at far below market rates. Total monthly spending averages Rs 7,500; the family and our NGO spent around Rs 15,000 for a single day’s stay at this hospital. Later, we got Vaishnavi admitted to the district hospital, where – after three days of treatment – she was discharged, cured of malaria.
‘Adivasis are ignorant’
Despite multi-stage barriers to accessing healthcare, 3,513 malaria cases were identified in 2025 in Alluri Sitharamaraju district alone – 49.3% of the total number of cases in Andhra Pradesh, in a district that is home to less than 2% of its population.
Public health officials attribute the high incidence of malaria in this region to its forested and hilly terrain. They explain the disproportionately low access to treatment by claiming that “Adivasis are ignorant”.
Adivasis constitute over 80% of the district’s population, with a literacy rate that is about half the state average. But when Adivasis such as Vaishnavi do seek treatment, the public health system does not record the systemic roadblocks they encounter and the long ordeals of having to travel from one hospital to the other, that incapacitate entire families in the process.
Unrecorded deaths
Vaishnavi’s case is an outlier. Not everyone like her survives or even gets a proper diagnosis.
In August, a four-old-girl from a remote Adivasi village of seven houses, not far from Peddaporlu, developed chali-jwaram. Chandrasekar Rao, the health volunteer, suspected this could be malaria. He tried to convince her parents to take her to the nearest health centre. They took her to a guru-guniya instead. After five days of illness, she died.
Many deaths in this region go unrecorded, and chali-jwaram is often the answer. But why do people persist in seeking a cure from a guru-guniya instead of a doctor?
The science of malaria
Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite, transmitted by the bite of the female anopheles mosquito. An easy-to-perform, widely available, rapid diagnostic test on a single drop of blood can detect the variant of plasmodium causing the disease.
The falciparum variant of the parasite is widely prevalent in Alluri Sitharamaraju district and is known to be resistant to an anti-malarial medicine called chloroquine. The government’s own guidelines stipulate that falciparum malaria should be treated by Artemisinin-based Combination Therapies (ACT), a combination of medicines.
Right ailment, wrong cure
A government medical officer told me that his primary health centre receives less than 20% of the total number of ACT doses they ask for in a month.
When I asked a community health officer why chloroquine – which is ineffective against falciparum malaria – is the only medicine prescribed for any type of malaria, he explained that the number of ACTs received at the centre is very low, and that he has to “make do with whatever is available”.
As a result people may think they have been treated even when they have not. When the prescriptions fail repeatedly, people lose trust in the public health system. “Very few Adivasis believe their disease can actually be treated by going to a doctor,” said Chandrasekar Rao, the health volunteer.
The implementation of even the most basic measures for malaria prevention remains inadequate.
I asked Sanjiv Rao, a Kondh Adivasi from the hills, if he remembered when the government had last distributed insecticide-treated mosquito nets, or deployed indoor residual spraying as a measure to control mosquitoes. “I have never seen indoor spraying and no mosquito nets have been distributed, or awareness campaigns conducted in my village since 2019,” he said.
“Technically, insecticide-treated bednets must be refilled every year, and indoor residual spraying must cover at least 80% of households in a village,” said Praful Chandel, a malaria program coordinator at Jan Swasthya Sahyog, a healthcare organisation that has worked with tribal and rural communities of Chattisgarh since 2000.
Four years to malaria elimination?
In September, a seven-year-old Adivasi girl died, and over 50 people from the same village in Andhra Pradesh’s Polavaram district were admitted to hospital on the same day, after being administered a dose of choloroquine as a preventive measure. Twelve of them tested positive for malaria.
In February, the state government claimed that malaria cases are on the decline in Andhra Pradesh, and the state has achieved 71.57% reduction as part of the goal to eliminate malaria by 2030. The waves of chali-jwaram in Alluri Sitharamaraju and many such Adivasi pockets of the country, speak of a different reality.
Dr Rohith Meesaraganda is a doctor-facilitator with the Rural Development Service Society. He regularly visits remote hamlets like Peddaporlu, assesses health conditions, and trains local volunteers in basic health knowledge to help communities deal with their medical problems.
The names of residents mentioned in this article have been changed to protect their identities.

title: Tiger relocated to Bengal reserve, residents of forest villages oppose tourism curbs
description: Residents say they are losing out on livelihood in peak season. Forest officials say the restrictions are temporary and for the big cat to acclimatise.
author: Nabarun Guha
content:
A three year old tigress, T138 was released in Buxa Tiger Reserve in West Bengal on October 2. While the translocation has been lauded as an important step in wildlife conservation, people living in forest villages have protested restrictions on tourism activities imposed to minimise disturbance and allow the tigress to acclimatise.
The translocation was the result of a joint initiative of the West Bengal Forest Department and National Tiger Conservation Authority. The tigress which was brought from the Valmiki Tiger Reserve in Bihar was soft released into an enclosure on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. Two days later, it reportedly stepped out of the enclosure and walked into the wild.
Bhupender Yadav, Union Cabinet Minister for Forest, Environment and Climate Change celebrated the tiger reintroduction to Buxa on his social media.
Why Buxa, declared a tiger reserve in 1983 under Project Tiger, needed a translocated tiger to repopulate it, points to decades of poaching, habitat degradation, poor prey base and biotic pressures, among others that wiped out the apex predators from the landscape. All India tiger estimation in 2018 recorded no tigers in Buxa which continued until late 2021 when camera traps showed one male tiger.
Chief Wildlife Warden of West Bengal, Pradeep Vyas shared that the gradual disappearance of tigers in Buxa Tiger Reserve started from 1970 onwards. “I think tigers mainly disappeared due to biotic interference in the park and poaching of their prey base. This led to their habitat getting disturbed. Unlike leopards, tigers won’t stay in disturbed forests.”
Forest villagers protest
While the big cat release has been touted as a milestone in tiger conservation in West Bengal, the decision sparked tension among residents of 18 forest villages. They took out a sit-in dharna at Rajabhatkhawa range, the entry point to the park, alleging loss of livelihood due to the restrictions imposed on tourism by the forest department. Initially the restrictions were to be from September 30 to October 3 but later, it was extended.
Buxa Tiger Reserve has 14 forest ranges. It also has 46 fringe villages, 37 forest villages, 34 tea gardens and four fixed demand holdings, according to a tiger management evaluation report released in 2023.
Deputy Field Director of BTR, PJ Harikrishnan, told Mongabay-India that the restriction has been imposed as a part of a standard protocol to provide an undisturbed habitat to the reintroduced tiger to get acclimatised to the new environment. “We have radio-collared the tigress and are giving it time to get acclimatised to its new environment. We have restricted tourism so that it doesn’t get disturbed and venture outside the forest,” he said.
Ayan Naidu, executive member of Maha Gram Sabha Joutha Sangram Committee, the organisation leading the protest said that while they were happy about the reintroduction since Buxa has not had a tiger in two decades, they were worried about loss of livelihood due to restrictions. “I live in Jayanti village and there is no scope for any other employment except tourism. Agriculture is not possible here because of the terrain. So this restriction is affecting the livelihood of more than 10,000 people here.”
“October is the earning season for us. Tourists book two to three months in advance for Dooars. Due to the park closure, hotel/homestay bookings got cancelled and they (the owners) had to refund advance payments,” he added.
Villagers raise demands
One of the protesters, Kurbaan Khan claimed that the villagers have several demands and that the protest was not only for lifting restrictions on tourism. “We want the removal of Rajabhatkhawa toll gate where we have to pay Rs 480 per vehicle plus Rs 150 per person on a PWD road. This is harassment as we have to go to the nearest town, Alipurduar, 30 km away, for everything. We also seek implementation of Forest Rights Act, 2006 and declaration of forest settlements as revenue villages.”
Buxa once witnessed rampant dolomite mining inside the forest since colonial times. Protesters such as Khan wondered if the villagers would be relocated for tiger reintroduction which could make mining easier.
More tigers are slated to be released in Buxa in the coming months though no official details are available. Mongabay India contacted senior forest officials who refused to comment.
The translocation process started a decade back, according to Vyas, when, as the Chief Wildlife Warden in West Bengal, he prepared a plan with the Wildlife Institute of India which NTCA later approved. “NTCA put forth certain conditions such as improving the prey base. As per the directive, sambar deers were brought from Jaldapara and a captive breeding programme was done before releasing them in BTR [Buxa Tiger Reserve]. The process needs very strong coordination between the state and central government,” he shared.
Regarding the choice of Valmiki as the source site for the translocation, he said, “Both Valmiki and Buxa share the Terai landscape so it won’t be a problem for the tiger to get acclimatised here.”
Tiger translocation has been used as a recovery tool in India, with successes in Rajasthan’s Sariska and Madhya Pradesh’s Panna, but failure in Odisha’s Satkosia Tiger Reserve. Translocations have also helped strengthen tiger populations in Uttarakhand’s Rajaji and Rajasthan’s Ramgarh Vishdhari tiger reserves.
Buxa with an area of 760.87 sq km falls in Alipurduar district has landscape connectivity to Bhutan forests in the north, Kochugaon and Manas Tiger Reserve (Assam) in the east, and Jaldapara in the west.
The tigress is currently at Chuniajhora area of Hathipota range, according to forest officials.
This article was first published on Mongabay.

title: MP के रीवा में जमीन, जल और भविष्य की लड़ाई के बीच ग्रामीणों ने नहीं मनाई दीपावली, घरों में नहीं जले दीये!
description: प्रस्तावित न्यूक्लियर प्लांट के विरोध में रोझौही और सरई कला के ग्रामीणों का अनोखा विरोध; विमला कोल की मौत के बाद परिवार की पहली दीपावली रही सूनी, ग्रामीण बोले- जमीन और आने वाली पीढ़ियों का भविष्य ज्यादा अहम
author: Ankit Pachauri
content:
भोपाल। दीपावली पर जहां हर घर रोशनी से जगमगा रहा था, बच्चे पटाखे चला रहे थे और परिवार त्योहार की खुशियां बांट रहे थे, वहीं मध्य प्रदेश के रीवा जिले के रोझौही और सरई कला क्षेत्र में इस बार दीपावली का माहौल बिल्कुल अलग रहा। यहां कई घरों में न तो दीपावली की तैयारियां हुईं और न ही दीये जलाकर त्योहार मनाया गया। प्रस्तावित न्यूक्लियर प्लांट के विरोध में आंदोलन कर रहे ग्रामीणों ने अपनी जमीन, पानी और आने वाली पीढ़ियों के भविष्य की चिंता को त्योहार से ऊपर रखा और दीपावली नहीं मनाने का फैसला किया।
ग्रामीणों का यह विरोध सिर्फ प्रस्तावित परियोजना के खिलाफ नहीं, बल्कि अपने जल, जंगल, जमीन और पर्यावरण को बचाने की चिंता से भी जुड़ा है। इस बीच विमला कोल की मौत ने आंदोलन के दर्द को और गहरा कर दिया। परिवार के लिए यह पहली दीपावली थी, जब घर में विमला मौजूद नहीं थीं।
पत्नी की यादों के बीच जमुना कोल की सूनी दीपावली
विमला कोल के पति जमुना कोल के लिए इस बार दीपावली का त्योहार बेहद दुखद रहा। जिस घर में पत्नी के साथ त्योहार की खुशियां बांटनी थीं, वहां इस बार उनकी यादें ही रह गईं। आंदोलन के दौरान विमला की तबीयत बिगड़ने के बाद अस्पताल में मौत हो गई थी।
परिवार और ग्रामीणों का दावा था कि विमला जल सत्याग्रह में शामिल थीं और कई दिनों से तालाब में उतरकर प्रस्तावित परियोजना का विरोध कर रही थीं। हालांकि, उनकी मौत की परिस्थितियों को लेकर प्रशासन और परिवार के अलग-अलग दावे सामने आए थे।
तत्कालीन कलेक्टर नरेंद्र सूर्यवंशी ने कहा था कि विमला जल सत्याग्रह में शामिल नहीं थीं और नित्यकर्म के दौरान गिरने से उनकी मौत हुई थी। वहीं, परिवार और ग्रामीणों ने उनकी मौत को आंदोलन के दौरान हुई परेशानियों से जोड़कर देखा। विमला की मौत के बाद नेता प्रतिपक्ष उमंग सिंघार ने परिवार से मुलाकात कर एक लाख रुपये की आर्थिक सहायता भी दी थी।
बच्चों के भविष्य की चिंता
आंदोलन में शामिल संदीप कोल ने कहा कि दीपावली ऐसा त्योहार है, जिसे हर परिवार अपने घर में खुशियों के साथ मनाना चाहता है। लेकिन जब अपनी जमीन और भविष्य को लेकर चिंता हो, तो त्योहार मनाने का मन नहीं होता। हमारी आजीविका जमीन से जुड़ी है। हम चाहते हैं कि आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए यह जमीन सुरक्षित रहे।
रावेंद्र कोल ने कहा कि गांव के लोगों के लिए जमीन और पानी सबसे जरूरी हैं। प्रस्तावित प्लांट से इन पर क्या असर पड़ेगा, इसकी स्पष्ट जानकारी ग्रामीणों को नहीं दी गई है। जब तक लोगों की आशंकाओं का समाधान नहीं होता, तब तक विरोध जारी रहेगा।
वहीं, बबली कोल ने कहा कि दीपावली बच्चों के लिए खुशियों का त्योहार है, लेकिन इस बार गांव के लोगों ने अपने भविष्य की चिंता को प्राथमिकता दी है। हम नहीं चाहते कि आने वाली पीढ़ियों को अपनी जमीन और अधिकार बचाने के लिए संघर्ष करना पड़े।
440 मेगावाट की प्रस्तावित परियोजना
रोझौही और सरई कला क्षेत्र में टाटा पावर से जुड़ी 2×220 मेगावाट क्षमता की प्रस्तावित न्यूक्लियर परियोजना को लेकर ग्रामीणों में नाराजगी है। परियोजना की शुरुआती तकनीकी जांच के लिए एमएस फुग्रो की दो बोरिंग मशीनें क्षेत्र में पहुंची थीं।
योजना के तहत कुल आठ बोरहोल किए जाने थे। इनमें से चार बोरहोल करीब 100 मीटर गहराई तक प्रस्तावित थे। हालांकि, ग्रामीणों ने सर्वे का विरोध करते हुए काम रुकवा दिया था।
9 अक्टूबर को कंपनी, प्रशासन और ग्रामीणों के बीच हुई बैठक भी बेनतीजा रही थी। ग्रामसभा में भी परियोजना के प्रस्ताव पर ग्रामीणों ने असहमति जताई थी। ग्रामीणों का कहना है कि परियोजना को लेकर उनकी आशंकाओं और सवालों का जवाब दिए बिना आगे की प्रक्रिया नहीं बढ़ाई जानी चाहिए।
कोटी जलप्रपात को बचाने की मांग, आंदोलन जारी
सामाजिक कार्यकर्ता और आंदोलनकारी शिवानंद द्विवेदी ने बताया कि ग्रामीणों का विरोध किसी भी विकास कार्य के खिलाफ नहीं है। उनकी चिंता जल, जंगल, जमीन और पर्यावरण को लेकर है। ग्रामीण चाहते हैं कि परियोजना से होने वाले संभावित प्रभावों की जानकारी सार्वजनिक की जाए और उनकी आपत्तियों का समाधान किया जाए।
उन्होंने कहा कि ग्रामीण अपने अधिकारों और आने वाली पीढ़ियों के भविष्य को लेकर चिंतित हैं। प्रस्तावित न्यूक्लियर प्लांट को निरस्त करने और क्षेत्र के प्राकृतिक महत्व वाले कोटी जलप्रपात को बचाने की मांग के साथ आंदोलन जारी है।
द मूकनायक की प्रीमियम और चुनिंदा खबरें अब द मूकनायक के न्यूज़ एप्प पर पढ़ें। Google Play Store से न्यूज़ एप्प इंस्टाल करने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें.
'द मूकनायक' जनवादी पत्रकारिता करता है. यह संविधान, लोकतंत्र और सामाजिक न्याय पर चलने वाला मीडिया समूह है। अगर आप भी चाहते हैं कि 'द मूकनायक' हमेशा हाशिए पर खड़े लोगों की आवाज बुलंद करता रहे, बेजुबानों की पीड़ा दिखाते रहें तो सब्सक्राइब करें।

title: MP हाईकोर्ट की दीपावली पर विशेष सुनवाई: 14 साल की दुष्कर्म पीड़िता को 26 सप्ताह का गर्भ समाप्त करने की अनुमति
description: जस्टिस मिलिंद रमेश फड़के की विशेष बेंच ने शनिवार को की सुनवाई, उसी दिन शाम 4 बजे तक प्रक्रिया पूरी करने के दिए निर्देश; मेडिकल बोर्ड की रिपोर्ट के लिए हाईकोर्ट ने प्रदेश की सभी अदालतों को जारी की नई गाइडलाइन
author: Ankit Pachauri
content:
भोपाल। मध्य प्रदेश हाईकोर्ट ने दीपावली की छुट्टी के दिन शनिवार को विशेष सुनवाई करते हुए 14 साल की दुष्कर्म पीड़िता को 26 सप्ताह का गर्भ समाप्त करने की अनुमति दी। शिवपुरी जिले की पीड़िता के मामले की गंभीरता को देखते हुए जस्टिस मिलिंद रमेश फड़के की विशेष बेंच ने 7 नवंबर को सुनवाई की। कोर्ट ने वरिष्ठ डॉक्टरों को उसी दिन शाम 4 बजे तक गर्भपात की प्रक्रिया पूरी करने के निर्देश दिए।
हाईकोर्ट ने मामले की गंभीरता को रेखांकित करते हुए कहा कि ऐसे मामलों में हर दिन बेहद कीमती होता है। एक दिन की देरी भी पीड़िता के स्वास्थ्य और जीवन के लिए ऐसे गंभीर परिणाम पैदा कर सकती है, जिनकी भरपाई संभव नहीं है।
मेडिकल बोर्ड की पहली रिपोर्ट स्पष्ट नहीं होने पर दोबारा मांगी जानकारी
यह मामला शिवपुरी जिले की करैरा स्पेशल कोर्ट से हाईकोर्ट पहुंचा था। पीड़िता के गर्भ की अवधि 26 सप्ताह होने के कारण मेडिकल स्थिति और गर्भ समाप्त करने की सुरक्षा को लेकर चिकित्सकीय राय मांगी गई थी।
जीआर मेडिकल कॉलेज और कमलाराजा अस्पताल के मेडिकल बोर्ड की पहली रिपोर्ट स्पष्ट नहीं थी। इस पर हाईकोर्ट ने दोबारा रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करने के निर्देश दिए। मेडिकल बोर्ड ने अपनी दूसरी रिपोर्ट में खून की उपलब्धता और जरूरी चिकित्सकीय सावधानियों को ध्यान में रखते हुए गर्भपात की प्रक्रिया को सुरक्षित बताया।
मेडिकल बोर्ड की रिपोर्ट मिलने के बाद हाईकोर्ट ने गर्भ समाप्त करने की अनुमति दे दी और डॉक्टरों को निर्धारित समयसीमा में प्रक्रिया पूरी करने के निर्देश दिए।
प्रदेश की सभी अदालतों के लिए जारी की नई गाइडलाइन
इस मामले में सुनवाई के दौरान हाईकोर्ट ने एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम उठाते हुए दुष्कर्म पीड़िताओं और अन्य विशेष परिस्थितियों में गर्भपात की अनुमति से जुड़ी याचिकाओं के निपटारे के लिए प्रदेश की सभी अदालतों को नई गाइडलाइन जारी की है।
हाईकोर्ट ने निर्देश दिया है कि ऐसे मामलों में मेडिकल बोर्ड की रिपोर्ट स्पष्ट और पूरी होनी चाहिए, ताकि अधूरी जानकारी के कारण न्यायिक प्रक्रिया में अनावश्यक देरी न हो। कोर्ट ने आदेश की प्रति जबलपुर मुख्यपीठ, इंदौर और ग्वालियर खंडपीठ के साथ प्रदेश के सभी जिला न्यायालयों को भेजने के निर्देश भी दिए हैं।
मेडिकल बोर्ड की रिपोर्ट में इन तीन बिंदुओं का होना अनिवार्य
हाईकोर्ट की गाइडलाइन के मुताबिक, ऐसे मामलों को आगे भेजने से पहले निचली अदालतों को मेडिकल बोर्ड की स्पष्ट रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करनी होगी। रिपोर्ट में तीन महत्वपूर्ण बिंदुओं का उल्लेख अनिवार्य होगा।
पीड़िता की वर्तमान शारीरिक स्थिति: मेडिकल बोर्ड पीड़िता के स्वास्थ्य और उसकी मौजूदा चिकित्सकीय स्थिति की स्पष्ट जानकारी देगा।
गर्भ की सटीक अवधि: रिपोर्ट में यह स्पष्ट रूप से दर्ज करना होगा कि गर्भ कितने सप्ताह का है।
गर्भपात की चिकित्सकीय संभावना और सुरक्षा: डॉक्टरों को स्पष्ट बताना होगा कि चिकित्सकीय दृष्टि से गर्भ समाप्त करना संभव और सुरक्षित है या नहीं।
देरी रोकने की दिशा में महत्वपूर्ण कदम
हाईकोर्ट की यह पहल दुष्कर्म पीड़िताओं और विशेष परिस्थितियों में गर्भपात की अनुमति से जुड़े मामलों में समय पर निर्णय सुनिश्चित करने की दिशा में महत्वपूर्ण मानी जा रही है। अदालत का जोर इस बात पर है कि मेडिकल बोर्ड की अस्पष्ट रिपोर्ट या प्रक्रियागत देरी के कारण पीड़िता को अतिरिक्त शारीरिक और मानसिक परेशानी का सामना न करना पड़े।
इस मामले में दीपावली की छुट्टी के दिन विशेष सुनवाई कर हाईकोर्ट ने यह स्पष्ट किया कि संवेदनशील मामलों में पीड़िता के स्वास्थ्य और जीवन की सुरक्षा सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता होनी चाहिए।
द मूकनायक की प्रीमियम और चुनिंदा खबरें अब द मूकनायक के न्यूज़ एप्प पर पढ़ें। Google Play Store से न्यूज़ एप्प इंस्टाल करने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें.
'द मूकनायक' जनवादी पत्रकारिता करता है. यह संविधान, लोकतंत्र और सामाजिक न्याय पर चलने वाला मीडिया समूह है। अगर आप भी चाहते हैं कि 'द मूकनायक' हमेशा हाशिए पर खड़े लोगों की आवाज बुलंद करता रहे, बेजुबानों की पीड़ा दिखाते रहें तो सब्सक्राइब करें।

title: 35 दिन बाद दिव्या अहिरवार को हाईकोर्ट से मिली जमानत, पुलिस की कार्रवाई पर उठाए सवाल
description: केन-बेतवा लिंक परियोजना से प्रभावित परिवारों के विस्थापन और पुनर्वास की मांग को लेकर कर रही थीं आंदोलन; धारा 307 के तहत हुई थी गिरफ्तारी, पूर्व राज्यसभा सांसद वृंदा करात ने संभाली थी आंदोलन की कमान
author: Ankit Pachauri
content:
भोपाल। मध्य प्रदेश के पन्ना और छतरपुर जिले में केन-बेतवा लिंक परियोजना सहित अन्य विकास योजनाओं से प्रभावित परिवारों के विस्थापन, उचित मुआवजे और पुनर्वास की मांग को लेकर आंदोलन कर रहीं 25 वर्षीय दिव्या अहिरवार को आखिरकार 35 दिन बाद मध्य प्रदेश हाईकोर्ट से जमानत मिल गई है। शुक्रवार को जस्टिस विवेक अग्रवाल की अदालत में उनकी जमानत याचिका पर सुनवाई हुई। सुनवाई के दौरान अदालत ने पुलिस की कार्रवाई पर सवाल उठाए और मामले में पुलिस की कार्रवाई को संदेह के घेरे में माना। इसके बाद दिव्या को जमानत दे दी गई।
दिव्या अहिरवार की गिरफ्तारी के बाद से ही इस आंदोलन को लेकर प्रदेश की राजनीति और सामाजिक संगठनों के बीच चर्चा तेज हो गई थी। दिव्या ने सैकड़ों महिलाओं के साथ मिलकर विस्थापन और पुनर्वास के सवाल पर आंदोलन खड़ा किया था। उनका आंदोलन केवल मुआवजे तक सीमित नहीं था, बल्कि प्रभावित परिवारों के अधिकारों, उनकी आजीविका और भविष्य की सुरक्षा से भी जुड़ा था। गिरफ्तारी के बाद पूर्व राज्यसभा सांसद वृंदा करात ने आंदोलन की कमान संभालते हुए प्रभावित लोगों के समर्थन में आवाज उठाई थी।
ऐसे शुरू हुआ विस्थापन के खिलाफ आंदोलन
दिव्या अहिरवार लंबे समय से सामाजिक कार्यकर्ता अमित भटनागर के साथ केन-बेतवा लिंक परियोजना और अन्य विकास योजनाओं से प्रभावित परिवारों के अधिकारों के लिए संघर्ष कर रही हैं। पन्ना-छतरपुर क्षेत्र में प्रस्तावित और निर्माणाधीन परियोजनाओं के कारण विस्थापन की आशंका झेल रहे परिवार उचित मुआवजे, पुनर्वास और अपने अधिकारों की मांग कर रहे हैं।
इसी क्रम में मझगांय डैम क्षेत्र में दिव्या के नेतृत्व में अलग-अलग तरीके से विरोध प्रदर्शन किए जा रहे थे। आंदोलनकारियों ने अपनी मांगों को प्रशासन तक पहुंचाने के लिए चिता सत्याग्रह, फांसी आंदोलन और जल सत्याग्रह जैसे विरोध के तरीके अपनाए। इन प्रदर्शनों में बड़ी संख्या में महिलाएं शामिल हुईं।
आंदोलन के दौरान महिलाओं का 'न्याय दो या फिर मार दो' का नारा चर्चा में रहा। प्रदर्शनकारियों का कहना था कि विकास परियोजनाओं के नाम पर उनकी जमीन, घर और आजीविका प्रभावित हो रही है, लेकिन उन्हें उनकी मांगों के अनुरूप मुआवजा और पुनर्वास नहीं मिल रहा है।
धीरे-धीरे यह आंदोलन प्रशासन के लिए बड़ी चुनौती बनता गया। प्रभावित परिवारों की बढ़ती भागीदारी और महिलाओं की सक्रिय भूमिका के बीच जिला प्रशासन और आंदोलनकारियों के बीच टकराव की स्थिति बनने लगी। इसके बाद प्रशासन ने पुलिस के जरिए सख्ती शुरू कर दी।
धारा 307 के तहत दिव्या समेत चार लोगों की गिरफ्तारी
आंदोलन के दौरान पुलिस कार्रवाई और गिरफ्तारियों को लेकर अधिवक्ता अंजना कुरारिया ने गंभीर सवाल उठाए हैं। उनके मुताबिक, 28 से 30 सितंबर के बीच पन्ना जिले में भारी पुलिस बल के साथ सीआरपीएफ की तैनाती की गई थी। इस दौरान आंदोलनकारियों के खिलाफ सख्ती बरती गई और दर्जनों लोगों पर अलग-अलग मुकदमे दर्ज किए गए।
अधिवक्ता अंजना कुरारिया के अनुसार, 28 सितंबर की रात पन्ना पुलिस ने दिव्या अहिरवार, हिसाबी राजपूत, इंद्रपाल और कमलेश प्रजापति को भारतीय दंड संहिता की धारा 307 (हत्या के प्रयास) के तहत गिरफ्तार किया था। गिरफ्तारी के बाद पुलिस उन्हें हनुमतगंज चौकी लेकर गई।
इसके अगले दिन यानी 29 सितंबर को दिव्या अहिरवार को जिला न्यायालय में पेश किया गया, जहां से उन्हें जेल भेज दिया गया। वहीं, उनके तीन अन्य साथियों को छतरपुर न्यायालय में पेश किया गया। इन तीनों को 12 अक्टूबर को जमानत मिल गई थी, लेकिन दिव्या को जेल में ही रहना पड़ा।
दिव्या की गिरफ्तारी के बाद आंदोलन से जुड़े लोगों और सामाजिक संगठनों ने उनकी रिहाई की मांग उठाई। उनका कहना था कि विस्थापन, मुआवजे और पुनर्वास जैसे बुनियादी सवालों को लेकर आवाज उठाने वाले आंदोलनकारियों के खिलाफ आपराधिक मुकदमे दर्ज करना लोकतांत्रिक विरोध को दबाने जैसा है।
हाईकोर्ट ने पुलिस की कार्रवाई पर उठाए सवाल
शुक्रवार को मध्य प्रदेश हाईकोर्ट में दिव्या अहिरवार की जमानत याचिका पर सुनवाई हुई। जस्टिस विवेक अग्रवाल की अदालत ने मामले में पुलिस की कार्रवाई को संदेहास्पद माना। अधिवक्ता अंजना कुरारिया के मुताबिक, अदालत ने पुलिस की कार्रवाई पर सवाल उठाते हुए दिव्या को जमानत दे दी।
35 दिनों तक जेल में रहने के बाद दिव्या को मिली इस राहत को आंदोलन से जुड़े लोगों के लिए महत्वपूर्ण माना जा रहा है। हालांकि, जमानत मिलने के बाद भी विस्थापन, मुआवजे और पुनर्वास से जुड़े मूल सवाल बने हुए हैं। प्रभावित परिवारों की मांग है कि सरकार उनकी समस्याओं का समाधान करे और विकास परियोजनाओं से प्रभावित लोगों के अधिकारों की रक्षा सुनिश्चित करे।
दिव्या की गिरफ्तारी के बाद वृंदा करात ने संभाली आंदोलन की कमान
दिव्या अहिरवार की गिरफ्तारी के बाद आंदोलन को राजनीतिक और सामाजिक स्तर पर समर्थन मिलने लगा था। पूर्व राज्यसभा सांसद वृंदा करात ने आंदोलन की कमान संभाली और प्रभावित परिवारों के मुद्दे को प्रमुखता से उठाया। उनके समर्थन से आंदोलन को राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर भी चर्चा मिली।
इसके अलावा मध्य प्रदेश विधानसभा में नेता प्रतिपक्ष उमंग सिंघार, आदिवासी कांग्रेस के राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष डॉ. विक्रांत भूरिया, प्रदेश कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष जीतू पटवारी और आम आदमी पार्टी की प्रदेश अध्यक्ष रानी अग्रवाल भी आंदोलन के समर्थन में पन्ना पहुंच चुके हैं।
इन नेताओं ने प्रभावित परिवारों की मांगों और आंदोलनकारियों के साथ हुई पुलिस कार्रवाई को लेकर अपनी चिंता जाहिर की थी। राजनीतिक दलों और सामाजिक संगठनों के प्रतिनिधियों की मौजूदगी ने इस आंदोलन को और व्यापक बना दिया।
द मूकनायक की प्रीमियम और चुनिंदा खबरें अब द मूकनायक के न्यूज़ एप्प पर पढ़ें। Google Play Store से न्यूज़ एप्प इंस्टाल करने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें.
'द मूकनायक' जनवादी पत्रकारिता करता है. यह संविधान, लोकतंत्र और सामाजिक न्याय पर चलने वाला मीडिया समूह है। अगर आप भी चाहते हैं कि 'द मूकनायक' हमेशा हाशिए पर खड़े लोगों की आवाज बुलंद करता रहे, बेजुबानों की पीड़ा दिखाते रहें तो सब्सक्राइब करें।

title: PM Modi may have considered Sharad Pawar for President had he joined NDA in 2019, claims Ramdas Athawale
description: Union Minister Ramdas Athawale has claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi could have considered Sharad Pawar for the 2022 presidential election had the NCP (SP) chief joined the NDA in 2019. He said he had repeatedly urged Pawar to join the alliance.
author: India TV News Desk
content:
Union Minister of State Ramdas Athawale has claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi could have considered NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar for the 2022 presidential election had the veteran politician joined the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in 2019. Athawale said he had repeatedly urged Pawar to join the alliance, proposing that the two sides work together on the basis of a common minimum programme.
Speaking to news agency IANS on Wednesday, Athawale also commented on the ongoing seat-sharing discussions between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. He said the two INDIA bloc partners might find it difficult to reach an agreement and could even contest the polls separately. He also welcomed the BJP's renewed alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in Punjab, saying it would strengthen the NDA's prospects in the state.
Athawale says Modi could have considered Pawar for President
Athawale said he had personally encouraged Pawar to join the NDA in 2019 and had repeatedly proposed bringing the two sides together through a common minimum programme.
"I was the one who had suggested that Sharad Pawar should join the NDA in 2019. I repeatedly told him that we should come together on the basis of a Common Minimum Programme. From 2014 to 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi accelerated the country's development, and significant progress was made across several sectors," he said.
The Union minister claimed that Modi had always held Pawar in high regard. He also recalled that when Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat, he had described the NCP (SP) chief as his ideal.
"Prime Minister Narendra Modi believes in development, and our mission is to make India the world's number one economy by 2047. He has always held Sharad Pawar in high regard. When Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat, he used to say that he considered Pawar his ideal," Athawale said.
He further suggested that Pawar could have been considered for the country's highest constitutional office if he had joined the NDA.
"Therefore, I believe Sharad Pawar should have joined the NDA. Had he joined in 2019, perhaps Prime Minister Narendra Modi would have considered him for the 2022 presidential election," he told IANS.
Athawale doubts SP-Congress seat-sharing agreement for UP polls
Commenting on the seat-sharing discussions between the Samajwadi Party and Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Athawale expressed doubt that the two parties would reach a compromise.
"I do not know what compromise will be reached between the two parties, but I do not think the Samajwadi Party will offer them so many seats," he said.
He added that the two INDIA bloc allies could decide to contest the elections separately, although the final decision would rest with the parties.
"It is also possible that the SP and Congress may contest the elections separately. However, the decision rests with them," Athawale said.
Athawale welcomes BJP-SAD alliance in Punjab
On the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal renewing their alliance ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections, Athawale said the move would improve the NDA's electoral prospects in the state.
He pointed to the earlier partnership between the two parties under former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal, saying they had remained in power together for several years.
Athawale also claimed that people in Punjab were becoming increasingly dissatisfied with the Aam Aadmi Party government. He cited concerns over drug trafficking, the condition of young people and issues affecting farmers as reasons for the alleged discontent.

title: Tamil Nadu govt apologises in SC for failure to light lamp at Deepathoon, blames temple board
description: The annual Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary Uchipillayar mandapam at Thirupparankundram, and not at the stone pillar on the hill as directed by the Supreme Court on Tuesday.
author: Arushi Jaiswal
content:
New Delhi:
The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday apologised to the Supreme Court over the failure to light the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon on Thirupparankundram Hill on November 24. The state government claimed that the temple's Board of Trustees had not authorised the team proposed to carry out the exercise.
Tamil Nadu government files status report
In a status report submitted by Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna, the state government told a bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi that the district administration had completed all arrangements to implement the Supreme Court's November 20 order permitting the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon through a restricted team authorised by the temple administration.
However, the order of the apex court could not be complied with because the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed for carrying out the exercise and instead resolved to follow the customary practice of lighting the Karthigai Mahadeepam at its traditional location, the state government claimed in the report.
On Tuesday, the annual Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary Uchipillayar mandapam at Thirupparankundram and not at the stone pillar on the hill as directed by the top court.
Deepathoon is a stone pillar atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.
'I sincerely apologise...'
"I submit that I took all the steps to comply with the order in good faith. There has been no wilful, deliberate disobedience on my part of any directions of this Hon'ble Court. I hold the orders of the Hon'ble Court in the highest respect and remain committed to comply with every direction this Hon'ble Court may issue," District Collector Nishant Krishna said in a status report.
"I sincerely apologise for the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon. The district administration made every effort to secure the authorisation of the Devasthanam and the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon," Krishna said.
However, the Board of Trustees, by its resolution dated November 24, resolved to light the lamp at the customary place.
The report added that the collector would submit a supplementary status report along with all supporting documents. "I submit that I will submit an additional status report with all supporting documents along with the same," the status report said.
The district collector also said the administration had made every effort to obtain the temple administration's authorisation to conduct the lighting ceremony at the Deepathoon.
The Supreme Court scheduled the main petition challenging the Madras High Court order permitting the lighting of the ceremonial lamp for final hearing in January next year.
The bench may also take up any contempt petition filed in connection with the matter.
(With PTI inputs)
