title: ‘A day off means job loss’: One year on, Surat’s loom workers say labour codes yet to reach them
description: Many migrants who run Surat’s power looms still work 14-hour days on piece rates, with no contracts and no safe way to complain.
author: Satish Bhartiya
content:
Many migrants who run Surat’s power looms still work 14-hour days on piece rates, with no contracts and no safe way to complain.
Amit Raut* has been caught in a Catch-22 for nearly two decades. The only work that pays enough to keep his family going is the work that is wearing him down.
Raut, about 50, first came to Surat 19 years ago from Ganjam district in Odisha, some 1,600 kilometres away, to work in the city’s power loom factories. Within four years, the pressure and the insecurity amid the clatter of dozens of machines became unbearable. He quit and went home.
In Ganjam, he spent nearly 10 years trying to make ends meet as a labourer. Daily wages there could not run a household, and the work was never certain. Three years ago, he came back to Surat, and to the looms.
Today he operates power looms in the Katargam area for 14 to 15 hours a day, paid by the metre of fabric he weaves. “I don’t receive any benefits like a labour card, PF (provident fund), or ESI,” he says.
Raut’s situation may seem to be an aberration, but it is how a significant portion of Surat’s weaving economy works. The city’s textile trade turns over an estimated Rs 1.5 lakh crore a year, and its looms are run by several lakh migrant workers from Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. Few of them have any official record of their employment.
On November 21, 2025, the Union government brought four labour codes into force, replacing 29 older laws and promising appointment letters, provident fund, health insurance and leave. As the codes complete their first anniversary, our reporting across Surat’s loom clusters found that little of that promise has reached the factory floor.
It is because of various reasons. The codes’ own headcount thresholds leave many small weaving units outside their strictest provisions. Workers say the rules, such as double pay for overtime, are barely enforced, and that they are too afraid of losing their jobs to ask.
Inside the sheds
Inside a factory in Katargam, more than 50 power looms roared at once, minded by just three workers, roughly 17 machines each. Two of them, drenched in sweat, had plugged in earphones to cut out the din. The third was peeling off a soaked vest.
Many factories we visited looked like ruins (except that ruins are quiet): broken windows, walls unpainted for years, and tin sheds, put up in the name of repairs, that make the interiors even hotter. Workers laboured in shorts and undershirts. The passages between machines were so narrow that one misstep could cause a serious accident. Drinking water was scarce, and emergency exits were hard to find.
What was easy to find were CCTV cameras. They were mounted in most factories, including those with no restrooms or water coolers.
Raut’s own factory, also in Katargam, runs about 66 looms.
“I operate power loom machines for about 14–15 hours every day just to earn Rs 500-800,” Raut says. That works out to between Rs 33 and Rs 57 an hour.
Though he is paid by output, not time, which shifts the cost of every flaw onto him. “My income fluctuates because sometimes the fabric gets damaged in the machine, resulting in lower pay,” he says. “The factories pay between two to five rupees per meter. I get paid three rupees per metre of fabric produced. Under these conditions, my monthly income comes out to between 15,000 and 25,000 rupees.”
Rent takes Rs 6,000 a month and food for the family another Rs 10,000. He also buys his own drinking water. “I spend anywhere between 60-100 rupees on water,” he says. Even the factory’s toilets and rest areas are off limits to him, he claims.
In a good month, Raut saves about Rs 5,000. That is nowhere near enough to educate his children or cover a medical emergency, and he claims getting a day off is difficult. So why stay? “There are six members in my family. My wife, myself, three daughters, and one son,” he says.
An industry that doesn’t count its workers?
Since its first textile ancillary unit opened in 1925, Surat has grown into a network of more than 70,000 traders. The city alone is estimated to have around 7 to 8 lakh weaving units, which employ between 7 lakh and 12 lakh migrant workers.
Naishadh Desai, chairman of the labour organisation Shramjivi Sevalaya, says around 30 lakh workers are employed in Surat’s textile industry, with 95 percent coming from states like Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh.
The government’s last baseline survey of the powerloom sector, conducted in 2013, counted roughly 24 lakh power looms across India supporting about 44 lakh jobs. For all of Gujarat, it recorded 5,24,102 looms and 6,63,068 jobs, fewer looms than Surat is now estimated to run on its own. The Ministry of Textiles told Parliament in 2024 that it was framing a new survey. Until one is published, the 2013 count remains the only official baseline.
A worker who does not exist on paper cannot claim provident fund, insurance or gratuity, and in some of the factories we visited, there was no official record of the people at the looms.
Little change
The labour codes were meant to fix some of these issues. Between them, the Code on Wages, the Industrial Relations Code, the Code on Social Security and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code promised appointment letters, ESIC insurance, free health check-ups, and gratuity, based on certain eligibility conditions.
Workers say they have seen little of it. Asim Sheikh*, 25, a migrant from Birbhum district in West Bengal, says his work conditions and pay have not changed in the year since the codes took effect. “We remain unorganised labour contracted on a temporary basis, which means we can’t demand rights under labour laws,” he says.
A study based on group discussions, by a labour organisation that requested anonymity, earlier claimed that most workers are unaware of overtime. No factory registers workers for ESIC or EPF or pays gratuity, and grievance committees and basic safety measures are virtually absent, it claimed.
Part of the explanation lies in some of the codes. The OSH Code covers establishments with 10 or more workers, and treats a unit as a “factory” only if 20 or more people work there with power. Under the old Factories Act, that threshold was 10. Provident fund is compulsory only for establishments with 20 or more employees, and ESIC is mandatory from 10, voluntary below that. Weaving units with four to 10 workers, a common size in Surat, can slip under most of these lines.
Though the Code on Wages has no such restrictions. It applies to every employee in every establishment, organised or unorganised, and guarantees minimum wage and overtime at no less than twice the normal rate. Even Gujarat’s 2025 amendment to its factory law, which allowed shifts to stretch to 12 hours, kept a 48-hour weekly ceiling and required overtime pay beyond nine hours a day.
Raut works 14 to 15 hours a day and earns the same three rupees a metre in his 14th hour as in his first.
A climate of fear
Shramjivi Sevalaya’s four-storey, 35,000-square-foot building seems deserted. Founded in 1940 to fight for workers’ rights, the organisation registered about 100,000 workers between 1960 and around 2000. Today, barely two to five workers visit in a day.
Its chairman Naishadh Desai says more than 80 union leaders work on labour rights in Surat. “However, even today, more than 90 percent of textile workers here, including those in power looms, are not provided their rights under labour laws,” he said.
The offices of five labour rights organisations we visited were just as empty, with at most one to four workers present.
Sheikh claims, “If a worker attempts to form a union or demand labour law protections, they are fired and blacklisted from finding work elsewhere.”
The same allegation surfaced this autumn, when Surat’s embroidery workers went on strike for shorter shifts and a weekly day off. As per reports, labour leader Malkhan Singh Verma alleged that 300 to 400 workers were dismissed, and that photographs of some were circulated on social media to warn other units off hiring them. Verma, who heads Majdoor Sena Surat, says the pattern is old. “In my experience working on labour rights from 2010 to the present, whenever an organisation, worker, or social activist raises the issue of workers’ rights, they are assaulted, jailed, threatened, and framed in false cases,” he says.
This reporter tried to speak to about 100 power loom workers. Some felt nothing would change; others believed speaking out would cost them their jobs. Not one agreed to be recorded on camera, and many would not even name their factory or its owner.
In Surat’s Parvat Patiya area, a group of people earlier surrounded a reporter who was filming workers. One of them snatched the phone, deleted several videos and issued a warning: “Get out of Surat, and don’t let us catch you filming anywhere again.”
The quiet exit
Bhimadhar Samudra, 59, has run Santoshi Restaurant in Katargam for 26 years. A power loom operator himself some 40 years ago, he has watched his customers dwindle.
“Until 2017–18, around 600 power loom workers used to come to my restaurant for meals in the morning and evening,” he says. “Now only about 100 workers eat here. They no longer have the money to feed themselves properly.”
He has also noticed more workers quitting the looms to look for something else. Rukmini Ben* is about to be one of them. The 45-year-old came to Surat from Jalgaon in Maharashtra 20 years ago and spent nearly 15 of them on power looms, with no job security, provident fund, bonus or safety provisions.
“Our hands make the cloth that goes out to the entire world,” she says, “but no rules or laws are followed in the factory to ensure our hands remain safe.”
Having “wasted” 15 years, she now wants out. “When a worker does not get their rights even after working for years, continuing the job makes no sense,” she says.
For now, she cooks in the evenings after her shift at the loom, and is looking for less physical work such as cooking, gardening or domestic help. “The power loom work makes me weak and fragile,” she says.
‘Sector hasn’t recovered from Covid’
Ramesh Bhai Prajapati, who owns a small weaving unit in Surat, admits that labour laws are disregarded in the city’s factories.
“We are unable to provide facilities like PF or labour cards to workers,” he says. “This is private, informal work, so workers are paid on a daily wage basis. Providing any additional benefits beyond this is beyond our capacity.”
Ramesh employs eight workers and pays them by output. His monthly wage bill is about Rs 1.5 lakh, or Rs 18,000 to 20,000 a worker. Maintenance, cleaning, electricity and materials cost another Rs 30,000 to 50,000. “My monthly net profit ranges from Rs. 1.5-2 lakh,” he says. “Before Covid, it was almost twice as much. The textile sector hasn’t recovered from the lockdown period.”
With eight employees, his unit falls below the thresholds for compulsory provident fund and ESIC, though the Code on Wages’ minimum-wage and overtime rules still bind him.
Ramesh says “we sometimes have to lay off workers” because the textile industry is “currently experiencing a slowdown”. This year has given some owners reasons for strain. In March, amid a gas shortage linked to the West Asia conflict, labour shortages and weak demand, Surat’s power loom units suspended night shifts. By April, industry bodies said nearly 2.5 lakh migrant workers had left the city. In August, a 25–30 percent jump in polyester yarn prices pushed about 1.5 lakh looms to drop a shift or close two days a week.
Larger owners, Ramesh says, have more capital and are in a much better position. “They are better equipped to look after their workers.”
Ashok Jirawala, president of the All Gujarat Textile Federation in Surat, says factory owners help out workers if they face any work-related or other difficulties, and that they are paid their wages on time. He argues that one of the reasons powerloom workers in Surat do not receive certain work-related benefits is that they do not stay with one factory for a long period.
We could not reach the factory owners whose units employed the workers quoted in this report. The workers were afraid that raising concerns about their rights could cost them their jobs, and spoke to us outside factory premises.
A movement tries again
“To enforce workers’ legal rights, the government and factory owners themselves must step forward with a clear policy,” says Mohan Bhai Dabbuwala, secretary of the Surat Textile Labour Union. “But the intent is clearly missing.”
Sandeep Patel, a Surat activist, is among the leaders of a textile labour movement that began a few months ago. “To demand ground-level enforcement of these laws, we held a sit-in protest on August 10 this year,” he says. “On August 24, we submitted a memorandum to the Collector. But there was no response. So we were forced to protest with nearly 2,000 workers on September 12.”
His demands are basic. “We are driving this movement so that statutory provisions under labour laws — such as 8-hour workdays, fair wages, Sunday off, ESI, and worker safety — are actually enforced on the ground.”
Patel says the Surat administration asked his team for a list of companies that were flouting the labour laws. The team’s worker-led survey covered more than 200 companies across textiles and other sectors. “None of them complied with the labour laws,” he claims.
His campaign ran alongside a wider agitation by Surat’s embroidery workers, who struck in mid-August and also protested at the collector’s office on September 12. In late September, the Deputy Labour Commissioner told the embroidery owners’ association, TEJAS, to comply with the four codes. On October 15, police detained around 70 workers and labour leaders before a planned satyagraha, citing a lack of permission.
The owners made a counter-offer: Rs 14,300 a month for an eight-hour shift with a weekly holiday, against the Rs 25,000 to 30,000 workers now earn for 12-hour days. Unions rejected it, along with a Rs 35,000 offer to stay on 12-hour shifts.
“If workers are denied their rights, this struggle will inevitably evolve into a much larger movement,” Patel says.
This reporter reached out to Surat’s labour assistant commissioner on the phone, email and WhatsApp to seek the department’s response to the allegations mentioned in the copy. This report will be updated if a response is received.
For Amit Raut, nothing about the codes’ first anniversary changes his life. “Taking a day off means losing your job.”
*Names of workers changed to protect identity

title: India and Nepal hit reset, but the reset has limits
description: Balendra Shah’s Delhi visit ended months of strain. Making the thaw last means building ties with Nepal’s institutions, not just its leader.
author: Anand Vardhan
content:
Balendra Shah’s Delhi visit ended months of strain. Making the thaw last means building ties with Nepal’s institutions, not just its leader.
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s choice of New Delhi for his first bilateral visit since assuming office in March was significant, though not unexpected. The visit followed a period when relations between the two neighbours had entered uncertainty after the political upheaval in Nepal and Shah’s initial reservations about India’s approach to several bilateral issues.
In essence, his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 23, followed by a series of agreements and a ten-pillar joint vision, appears to have given the relationship fresh diplomatic momentum. In terms of more visible outcomes, India announced development assistance worth Rs 15,000 crore, while the two sides advanced cooperation in railway and road connectivity, energy, transit, trade and institutional development. At the same time, however, the visit also exposed the limits of the current rapprochement. Several of the issues that have complicated relations for decades remain unresolved. The more consequential question is whether the new political engagement can translate into a more durable understanding between the two countries.
Shah’s emergence as a leader from the violent protests of September 2025, which overthrew the previous KP Oli regime, makes this visit particularly important. The parliamentary elections in March 2026 brought Shah’s Rastriya Swatantra Party to power with a decisive mandate, transforming the domestic political landscape. The party now faces pressure to deliver on expectations of accountable government, job creation, and a more assertive articulation of national interests.
For New Delhi, this presented a diplomatic challenge. Its relationship with Oli had deteriorated amid disagreements over the boundary dispute and his engagement with Beijing. Shah also made pointed remarks about Nepal’s territorial claims and India’s position on the disputed areas. His proposed visit to India in May was cancelled after he declined to meet Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri. The eventual decision to make New Delhi his first bilateral destination abroad suggested that both governments recognised the importance of restoring a working relationship, even where differences persisted. The visit followed Misri’s preparatory discussions in Kathmandu earlier in November.
Money, rails and pipelines
The devastating floods and debris flows in the Rasuwa-Trishuli basin and other parts of Nepal in August had added urgency to the engagement. The disaster caused extensive loss of life and destroyed homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure. Shah acknowledged India’s prompt humanitarian and technical assistance during his visit. Reconstruction also figured prominently in the discussions with Modi. India announced assistance worth Rs 15,000 crore, comprising Rs 3,500 crore in grants for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure projects and Rs 11,500 crore through a rupee-denominated line of credit for energy projects—the distinction between the two components matters. The total amount is not a grant and specific projects and disbursement arrangements will be finalised through mutual discussion. It’s a significant announcement but the value of it will be in the nature of the assistance and how quickly the projects get to implementation.
The economic package has to be viewed in the context of the wider connectivity agenda. Nepal’s continued reliance on Indian routes as the means to access overseas markets has been a classic example of both economic interdependence and a politically sensitive issue. The announcement of transit access through Deendayal Port at Kandla, with access to Paradip in Odisha to follow once the necessary infrastructure is in place, offers Nepal additional options. The importance of these arrangements will depend on whether they reduce transport costs and make Nepali exports more competitive. Additional port access has limited practical value unless the rail and road connections linking Nepal to these facilities are developed alongside it. The absence of an agreement on access to Mundra, which Nepal had also sought, reminds us that diversification of transit facilities remains a matter of negotiation.
In more immediate terms, railway cooperation is one of the more significant aspects of the visit. The inauguration of the Sarayu-Kamala Express between Ayodhya and Janakpur provides a tangible element to the religious and cultural links between the two countries and will be of enormous benefit to pilgrimage and tourism on the Ramayana circuit. The larger economic implications, however, lie in the proposed expansion of cross-border rail networks. The two governments have agreed to expedite the remaining sections of the Jayanagar-Bardibas and Jogbani-Biratnagar railway lines. They have also welcomed the finalisation of the Final Location Survey for the proposed electrified broad-gauge Raxaul-Kathmandu railway. Cooperation on Nepal's East-West Railway, with priority to the Bardibas-Nijgadh and Birgunj-Nijgadh sections, is another important commitment. These projects could improve Nepal’s access to Indian markets and ports, strengthen trade links and reduce the cost of movement. Their eventual impact will depend on financing, construction schedules and coordination between the two railway systems.
In some ways, the same practical considerations apply to road and border infrastructure. A motorable bridge across the Mahakali connecting Dharchula in India with Darchula in Nepal was inaugurated, while work on integrated check posts at Bhairahawa, Sunauli, Banbasa and Dodhara Chandani is to be expedited. In the energy and petroleum sectors, Phase II of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj pipeline was dedicated, the foundation stone of a petroleum terminal at Jhapa was laid, and the two governments agreed to advance a pipeline connecting Siliguri with Jhapa. They will also explore the possibility of a gas pipeline. These initiatives are about integrating the two countries’ supply chains and making cross-border trade more efficient. Their success will depend on whether simpler procedures and reliable movement of goods go hand in hand with the infrastructure.
Of the various areas of mutual interest, energy is undoubtedly one of the most significant from an economic point of view. Nepal has enormous hydropower potential, and India has a rapidly growing requirement for power as well as a very large market in which to sell it. This creates a clear opportunity for a more integrated regional energy system.
The foundation stone for the 669 MW Lower Arun project and the commitment to accelerate work on the Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project, as well as the Saptakoshi and Sunkoshi schemes, are important developments. The two sides also noted progress towards joint ventures for high-capacity transmission lines connecting Inaruwa with New Purnea and Dododhara with Bareilly. The 2024 long-term power trade agreement, which envisages Indian purchases of up to 10,000 MW of Nepali electricity over ten years, provides a framework for expanding this relationship. Yet the obstacles are familiar, particularly differences over project financing, water-sharing, transmission infrastructure, and the conditions governing electricity purchases, which continue to affect cooperation. The Pancheshwar project, in particular, has remained stalled for years despite its considerable potential for power generation, irrigation and flood management.
The eight memoranda of understanding exchanged during the visit extend cooperation into forensic science, police training, civil-service capacity building, traditional medicine, satellite communications, sustainable urban development, healthcare, livestock and fisheries. The joint vision also envisages collaboration in digital payments, artificial intelligence, start-ups, space technology and education. India's commitment to establishing an offshore IIT campus in Nepal and the proposed Agro-Industrial Park in Chitwan are intended to give the partnership a wider developmental base. Cooperation in sports, including support for a national cricket training academy, and the development of Ramayana, Buddhist, and Shiv-Shakti tourism circuits are further examples of efforts to broaden the relationship.
Where the reset stops
The positive atmosphere in New Delhi should not obscure the limited movement on the more contentious questions. The territorial dispute involving Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura remains unresolved. The joint statement records progress in maintaining and repairing boundary pillars and directs the foreign secretaries to work on outstanding boundary issues. This keeps the diplomatic door open, but technical discussions in themselves won't resolve a dispute over competing claims of sovereignty. Nepal’s request for further international air entry routes is still only partially met. The existing one-way B345 route from Kathmandu via Bhairahawa to Lucknow is to be made two-way as a result of the technical discussions. That’s a sensible thing to do, particularly in terms of the operation of Bhairahawa airport, but again it doesn’t go any way towards meeting Nepal’s wider request for additional routes (including through the western sector).
The historical strands continue to pose questions. The 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship is still a sensitive issue. The joint vision recognises the need for an updated legal framework and states that existing bilateral agreements, including the treaty, may be reviewed by mutual consent. This is an acknowledgement of Nepal's longstanding demand, but no specific mechanism or timetable for renegotiation has been announced. The Eminent Persons Group report, submitted in 2018 after examining the treaty and the wider relationship, remains a point of disagreement. Nepal has regarded its recommendations as an important basis for reconsidering bilateral arrangements, but India has not accepted the report as a basis for the present exercise and has indicated a preference for a forward-looking approach. The difference reflects contrasting understandings of how historical grievances should be addressed. Other concerns, including the trade deficit, non-tariff barriers affecting Nepali exports and the suspension of recruitment of Nepali citizens into the Indian Army under the Agnipath scheme, also remain. The visit did not produce a breakthrough on these questions.
The gap between economic cooperation and political accommodation is a recurring feature of India-Nepal relations. Successive governments have announced infrastructure projects, promised progress on water resources and agreed to discuss the treaty and boundary questions, but implementation has often been slow, and politically sensitive matters have remained at the level of official discussions. Nepalese concerns about the unequal nature of the relationship cannot be addressed simply by adding more development projects to the bilateral agenda. Geography has made India Nepal’s principal trading partner, transit route and supplier of essential goods. The open border and extensive social, cultural and religious connections have created a relationship that reaches well beyond government-to-government engagement. But economic interdependence is unequal. Nepal’s reliance on Indian markets, ports, fuel supplies and transport routes has often raised concerns about its bargaining position and freedom of action. The experience of the 2015 blockade remains an important part of Nepali political memory, reinforcing the perception that economic dependence can become a source of political vulnerability.
Policies, not persons
The observations of former Indian foreign Secretary Shyam Saran, who once also served as India’s ambassador to Nepal, remain relevant in this context. For years, he has argued that India should advocate policies rather than persons, and engage with the widest possible political spectrum in Nepal, which speaks directly to the challenge presented by Shah’s government. India’s interests cannot rest on its relationship with particular leaders or parties. Political change in Kathmandu has repeatedly altered the terms of engagement, and New Delhi has sometimes allowed its assessment of individual leaders to influence its broader approach. A more durable policy would be built around institutions, long-term economic interests and sustained engagement across Nepal’s political spectrum. Shah’s emergence from a movement challenging the established political order makes this lesson particularly pertinent. His government will have to respond to domestic expectations that may not always coincide with India's preferences.
In this context, a longtime Nepal watcher and former special envoy to Nepal SD Muni offers a complementary perspective on India-Nepal relations, particularly his attention to India’s popular profile in Nepal and the consequences of overlooking Nepalese political sensitivities. India’s geographical proximity, cultural links and economic importance give it considerable advantages. But historical affinity doesn’t necessarily translate into public goodwill. Perceptions of interference, of unequal treatment and of a disregard for Nepal’s sovereignty can all erode the social bedrock of the relationship even if the economic cooperation is very substantial. Experience from previous periods of diplomatic friction shows that public opinion in Nepal is a key factor in the durability of India's influence. The emphasis on development and people-to-people ties during the November visit will only have real meaning if the benefits are demonstrable beyond speeches and official events.
The geopolitical setting makes this task more complex. Nepal’s position between India and China has long shaped New Delhi’s security calculations. The idea of Nepal as a buffer state has influenced Indian thinking since the colonial period and continued after independence. The security of the Himalayan frontier, cross-border networks and the presence of an external power close to India's northern borders are legitimate strategic concerns. China’s expanding economic and infrastructure engagement in Nepal, including through the Belt and Road Initiative, has consequently attracted attention in New Delhi. But Nepal’s ties with China cannot be understood only as a challenge to India. Kathmandu has its own reasons for seeking diversified partnerships, including access to infrastructure finance, trade routes and investment. Its political leadership must also respond to domestic expectations about sovereignty and strategic autonomy. An Indian policy driven principally by anxiety over Chinese influence risks strengthening the very resentment that it seeks to contain.
Making the advantage count
India’s advantages in Nepal are substantial, but they require careful use. Its proximity, integrated markets, employment links, open border and cultural connections offer a basis for cooperation that no external partner can easily replicate. The task is to turn these advantages into a relationship that Nepal sees as mutually beneficial. This requires greater attention to trade facilitation, investment conditions, timely completion of infrastructure projects and the removal of practical obstacles faced by Nepali exporters. It also means recognising that Nepal will maintain relations with other countries and that this is an expression of its sovereign choice. India’s security interests can be pursued through consultation and predictable cooperation rather than pressure.
Climate and environmental cooperation should become a more prominent part of this partnership. The August floods demonstrated the vulnerability of both countries to disasters originating in the Himalayan region. Rivers cross national boundaries, while floods, landslides and glacial lake outbursts can destroy infrastructure and livelihoods on either side. The joint vision’s commitments to hydrological and meteorological data-sharing, glacial lake monitoring, early-warning systems and disaster preparedness provide a useful starting point. These commitments need to develop into regular cooperation between relevant agencies, including joint risk assessments, river-basin management and coordinated emergency responses. The region’s environmental challenges cannot be addressed through isolated national measures.
Shah’s visit has opened a window for a more substantive engagement between India and Nepal. The agreements on financial assistance, railways, ports, energy and institutional cooperation offer a considerable agenda. Yet the relationship will be judged by whether these commitments are implemented and whether the two governments find the political confidence to address their longstanding differences. Nepal’s political transformation has changed the domestic setting in which India must operate. While the geographical, economic, and social foundations of the relationship remain, managing them requires greater sensitivity and reciprocity, and for India, the test is whether it can pursue its legitimate interests while recognising Nepal’s political autonomy and the expectations of its people. A partnership built on that understanding would credibly reinforce relations rooted as much in geography as in historical ties.

title: ‘अपनी पार्टी में बात करेंगे सपा के साथ बैठना है या नहीं’, सीट शेयरिंग से पहले प्रत्याशियों की घोषणा से इमरान मसूद नाराज
description: समाजवादी पार्टी ने मंगलवार रात पांच सीटों पर प्रत्याशियों की घोषणा की थी। इनमें इमरान मसूद के क्षेत्र की दो सीटें- बेहद और सहारनपुर देहात शामिल हैं। इसके अलावा पश्चिमी यूपी की कैराना और अमरोहा सीट पर भी सपा ने उम्मीदवार घोषित कर दिए हैं।
author: जनसत्ता न्यूज डेस्क
content:
समाजवादी पार्टी द्वारा उत्तर प्रदेश में पांच विधानसभा सीटों पर प्रत्याशी घोषित करना इमरान मसूद को रास नहीं आया है। इमरान मसूद ने न्यूज एजेंसी पीटीआई से बातचीत में समाजवादी पार्टी की तरफ से गंभीरता नहीं दिखाई दे रही। उन्होंने कहा कि अब आगे सपा के साथ बैठना है भी या नहीं, इस पर कांग्रेस नेतृत्व से बात की जाएगी।
इमरान मसूद ने कहा कि सपा-कांग्रेस के बीच सीट शेयरिंग को लेकर चर्चा हो रही थी लेकिन अचानक से उम्मीदवारों की घोषणा कर दी गई। सहारनपुर में भी सपा ने प्रत्याशी घोषित कर दिए। समझ नहीं आ रहा कि सपा को कांग्रेस से लड़ना है या बीजेपी से लड़ना है।
कांग्रेस नेता ने दावा किया की सीट शेयरिंग को लेकर उनकी पार्टी की तरफ से ईमानदारी से प्रयास किए जा रहे हैं लेकिन पहले यह तय करना होगा कि समाजवादी पार्टी चुनाव में कांग्रेस से लड़ना चाहती है या बीजेपी से लड़ना चाहती है।
‘हाय-तौबा की जरूरत नहीं’
कांग्रेस पार्टी की नाराजगी पर समाजवादी पार्टी के राज्यसभा सांसद रामजी लाल सुमन ने कहा कि इस पर हाय-तौबा क्यों हो रही है। ये सभी सीटें सपा जीती हुई है, हमारे वहां विधायक हैं, चाहे आगे कर लो या पीछे कर लो, हमें वहां लड़ना ही लड़ना है।
उन्होंने कहा, “कांग्रेस पार्टी के लोगों से मेरा विनम्र आग्रह है कि हम जितना व्यवहारिक सोचेंगे, जमीनी हकीकत के आधार पर सोचेंगे, तो मैं समझता हूं कि गठबंधन भी जल्दी हो जाएगा और उसके परिणाम भी अच्छे निकलेंगे। सपा अध्यक्ष अखिलेश यादव ने कई बार कहा है कि हमें दांव प्रत्याशी पर लगाना चाहिए जो जीतने की स्थिति में हो।”
सपा प्रवक्ता ने भी कसा कांग्रेस पर तंज
समाजवादी पार्टी के प्रवक्ता डॉक्टर आशुतोष वर्मा ने कहा कि सपा पूरी तरह से चुनाव में जाने के लिए तैयार है। सपा कार्यकर्ताओं को यह बेचैनी है कि अगर बहुत देर की जाएगी तो चुनाव लड़ने भर का चुनाव रह जाएगा, जीतने भर का नहीं। इस समय सारी लड़ाई सीट को जीतने के लिए है।
उन्होंने कहा कि सपा ने जिन चार सीटों पर प्रत्याशी घोषित किए हैं, उनमें चार सिटिंग विधायक हैं। उन पर सवाल ही नहीं बनता है, जो पांचवीं सीट ललितपुर की घोषित की गई है, उसका आप 2022 का परिणाम देख लीजिए। तब वहां सपा को 70 हजार और कांग्रेस को तीन हजार वोट मिले थे।
आशुतोष वर्मा ने कहा कि बराबरी कैसे की जाए और किस तरीके से की जाए, यह भी कांग्रेस पार्टी को सोचना है। सपा बार-बार कह रही है कि जीतना हमारा लक्ष्य है और अगर हम जीत नहीं सकते हैं तो लड़ने भर के लिए सबको आजादी है कि जो चाहे, वहां लड़े जाकर।

title: सपा ने जिन पांच सीटों के लिए उम्मीदवारों की पहली सूची की है जारी, वहां 2022 में क्या रहा चुनाव परिणाम?
description: समाजवादी पार्टी ने पहली सूची में जिन पांच सीटों के लिए उम्मीदवार घोषित किए हैं उनमें सहारनपुर की बेहट सीट, सहारनपुर देहात, शामली की कैराना, अमरोहा और ललितपुर सीट शामिल है।
author: Kapil Tiwari
content:
उत्तर प्रदेश में अगले साल यानी 2027 के शुरुआत में होने वाले विधानसभा चुनाव के लिए समाजवादी पार्टी ने मंगलवार रात को पांच प्रत्याशियों की पहली लिस्ट जारी कर दी। सपा ने यह सूची ऐसे वक्त में जारी की जब कांग्रेस के साथ सीट बंटवारे को लेकर खींचतान चल रही है।
समाजवादी पार्टी ने पहली सूची में जिन पांच सीटों के लिए उम्मीदवार घोषित किए हैं उनमें सहारनपुर की बेहट सीट, सहारनपुर देहात, शामली की कैराना, अमरोहा और ललितपुर सीट शामिल है।
सपा की 5 सीटों के पांचों प्रत्याशी
सपा ने जिन 5 सीटों के लिए उम्मीदवार घोषित किए हैं उनमें ललितपुर से ज्योति सिंह लोधी और सहारनपुर देहात से आशु मलिक को टिकट दिया गया है। सहारनपुर की ही बेहट सीट से उमर अली खान को उम्मीदवार घोषित किया गया है। शामली से की कैराना सीट से नाहिद हसन, अमरोहा विधानसभा क्षेत्र से महबूब अली को टिकट मिला है।
इन पांचों सीटों पर 2022 के चुनाव में कैसा रहा था रिजल्ट?
इन पांच सीटों के पिछले चुनावी रिजल्ट की बात करें तो 4 सीटें ऐसी हैं जहां सपा के मौजूदा विधायक हैं जबकि ललितपुर की सीट बीजेपी के पास है।
पांचों सीटों का पिछले चुनाव का रिजल्ट
ललितपुर
पिछले चुनाव में ललितपुर सीट पर बीजेपी के रामरतन कुशवाहा ने जीत हासिल की थी। कुशवाहा को कुल 1,76,550 वोट मिले थे जबकि दूसरे स्थान पर बीएसपी के चंद्र भूषण सिंह रहे थे। उन्हें 1 लाख के करीब वोट मिले थे। सपा उम्मीदवार रमेश प्रसाद इस सीट पर तीसरे स्थान पर रहे थे। उन्हें 68,597 वोट मिले थे। इस बार इस सीट पर सपा ने ज्योति सिंह लोधी को उम्मीदवार बनाया है जो 2017 में चुनाव लड़ी थीं और हार गई थीं।
कैराना (शामली)
शामली जिले की कैराना सीट पर सपा के नाहिद हसन मौजूदा विधायक हैं और उन्हें ही पार्टी ने टिकट भी दिया है। पिछले चुनाव में नाहिद हसन को 1,31,035 वोट मिले थे। दूसरे स्थान पर बीजेपी की मृगांका सिंह को 1,05,148 वोट मिले थे जबकि BSP के राजेंद्र और कांग्रेस उम्मीदवार अखलाक क्रमश: तीसरे और चौथे नंबर पर रहे थे।
अमरोहा
अमरोहा सीट पर पिछले चुनाव में सपा के महबूब अली ने जीत दर्ज की थी, जबकि बीजेपी उम्मीदवार राम सिंह दूसरे स्थान पर रहे थे। महबूब अली को 1,28,735 वोट और राम सिंह को 57,699 वोट मिले। वहीं, BSP के नावेद अयाज 34,585 वोटों के साथ तीसरे और कांग्रेस के सलीम खान 846 वोट पाकर चौथे नंबर पर थे।
सहारनपुर देहात
पिछले चुनाव में इस सीट पर सपा के आशु मलिक ने 1,07,007 वोट हासिल कर जीत दर्ज की थी। बीजेपी के जगपाल सिंह को 76,262 वोट मिले थे। बीएसपी के अजब सिंह को 62,637 वोट, AIMIM के मरगूब को 8,187 वोट और पांचवें पायदान पर रहे कांग्रेस के संदीप कुमार को 1,217 वोट मिले थे।
बेहट विधानसभा सीट
सहारनपुर की बेहट सीट पर भी सपा के ही उमर अली खान को जीत मिली थी। उन्हें कुल 1,34,513 वोट मिले थे। दूसरे स्थान पर बीजेपी के नरेश सैनी रहने थे जिन्हें 96,633 वोट मिले थे। तीसरे नंबर पर BSP के रईस मलिक को 45,075 वोट मिले थे और चौथे स्थान पर कांग्रेस के पूनम कंबोज को सिर्फ 1632 वोट मिले थे।

title: अमीर परिवारों के पुरुषों में जल्दी मौत का जोखिम 62% कम, महिलाओं के मामले में भी दिखा अंतर, भारतीयों पर हुई स्टडी में खुलासा
description: भारत में अमीर और गरीब लोगों की मृत्यु दर में बड़ा अंतर सामने आया है। एक नई स्टडी के मुताबिक, अमीर पुरुषों में कम उम्र में मौत का खतरा 62 फीसदी कम है, जबकि मुस्लिम पुरुषों में भी मृत्यु का जोखिम कम पाया गया।
author: ZEESHAN SHAIKH
content:
भारत में किसी व्यक्ति की उम्र कितनी होगी, यह सिर्फ उसकी जाति या धर्म पर निर्भर नहीं करता, बल्कि उसकी आर्थिक स्थिति भी इसमें बड़ी भूमिका निभाती है। एक नई स्टडी में सामने आया है कि देश के सबसे अमीर परिवारों में रहने वाले पुरुषों की कामकाजी उम्र के दौरान मौत होने का खतरा सबसे गरीब परिवारों के पुरुषों के मुकाबले 62 फीसदी कम है। महिलाओं के मामले में भी यह अंतर काफी बड़ा है। अमीर परिवारों की महिलाओं में गरीब परिवारों की महिलाओं के मुकाबले मौत का जोखिम 42 फीसदी कम पाया गया है।
यह स्टडी बताती है कि भारत में 15 से 59 साल की उम्र के लोगों के जीवित रहने की संभावना पर घरेलू संपत्ति का असर जाति और धर्म से भी ज्यादा है। हालांकि, इसके बावजूद कुछ सामाजिक समूहों में मौत का खतरा अधिक बना हुआ है। खासतौर पर अनुसूचित जाति (SC) की महिलाओं में ऊंची जाति की हिंदू महिलाओं के मुकाबले मौत का जोखिम ज्यादा पाया गया। वहीं, मुस्लिम पुरुषों में ऊंची जाति के हिंदू पुरुषों की तुलना में मृत्यु का जोखिम कम दर्ज किया गया।
क्या कहती है नई स्टडी?
यह रिसर्च ‘डेमोग्राफिक रिसर्च’ नाम के पीयर-रिव्यूड जर्नल में प्रकाशित हुई है। इसे मैक्स प्लैंक इंस्टीट्यूट फॉर डेमोग्राफिक रिसर्च के मोराध्वज धाकड़ और इंटरनेशनल इंस्टीट्यूट फॉर पॉपुलेशन साइंसेज (IIPS) की नंदिता सैकिया ने किया है।
शोधकर्ताओं ने भारत में वयस्कों की मृत्यु दर को समझने के लिए नेशनल फैमिली हेल्थ सर्वे (NFHS) के तीन चरणों के आंकड़ों का अध्ययन किया। इनमें 1998-99, 2015-16 और 2019-21 के सर्वे शामिल हैं। इस रिसर्च में 15 से 59 साल की उम्र के लोगों की मृत्यु दर और उनकी आर्थिक-सामाजिक स्थिति के बीच संबंधों को समझने की कोशिश की गई।
स्टडी के मुताबिक, सबसे गरीब परिवारों के 1,000 पुरुषों में 280 की मौत होने की संभावना थी, जबकि सबसे अमीर परिवारों में यह संख्या 158 थी। यानी अमीर परिवारों के पुरुषों में मौत का जोखिम काफी कम पाया गया। महिलाओं के मामले में भी ऐसा ही अंतर देखने को मिला। सबसे गरीब परिवारों की हर 1,000 महिलाओं में 157 की मौत होने की संभावना थी, जबकि सबसे अमीर परिवारों में यह आंकड़ा 87 था।
शोधकर्ताओं ने जाति, धर्म, ग्रामीण और शहरी इलाकों में रहने तथा अलग-अलग राज्यों के अंतर को ध्यान में रखते हुए भी आंकड़ों का विश्लेषण किया। इसके बाद भी सबसे अमीर 20 फीसदी परिवारों के पुरुषों में सबसे गरीब 20 फीसदी परिवारों के पुरुषों के मुकाबले मौत का जोखिम 62 फीसदी कम पाया गया। वहीं, महिलाओं में यह जोखिम 42 फीसदी कम था।
जाति के आधार पर भी सामने आया अंतर, SC महिलाओं में ज्यादा खतरा
स्टडी में जाति के आधार पर मृत्यु दर में अंतर भी देखा गया। इसके मुताबिक, अनुसूचित जाति (SC) और अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) के पुरुषों में ऊंची जाति के हिंदू पुरुषों की तुलना में मृत्यु दर ज्यादा थी। हालांकि, शोधकर्ताओं का कहना है कि इस अंतर के पीछे उनकी आर्थिक स्थिति और भौगोलिक परिस्थितियां बड़ी वजह हो सकती हैं।
2019-21 के आंकड़ों के अनुसार, अनुसूचित जाति के पुरुषों में मृत्यु की संभावना प्रति 1,000 लोगों पर 256 थी। वहीं, अनुसूचित जनजाति के पुरुषों में यह आंकड़ा 254 था। इसकी तुलना में ऊंची जाति के हिंदू पुरुषों में यह संख्या 197 दर्ज की गई।
महिलाओं के मामले में भी सामाजिक अंतर देखने को मिला। स्टडी के मुताबिक, आर्थिक स्थिति और रहने की जगह जैसे कारकों को ध्यान में रखने के बाद भी अनुसूचित जाति की महिलाओं में ऊंची जाति की हिंदू महिलाओं के मुकाबले वयस्क उम्र में मौत का जोखिम 19 फीसदी ज्यादा था।
मुस्लिम पुरुषों में ऊंची जाति के हिंदुओं से कम मृत्यु दर
इस स्टडी का एक अहम निष्कर्ष मुस्लिम पुरुषों की मृत्यु दर से जुड़ा है। शोधकर्ताओं ने पाया कि तीनों सर्वे के दौरान मुस्लिम पुरुषों में ऊंची जाति के हिंदू पुरुषों की तुलना में वयस्क उम्र में मौत का जोखिम लगातार कम रहा। 2019-21 के आंकड़ों के मुताबिक, घरेलू संपत्ति, रहने की जगह और राज्य के अंतर को ध्यान में रखने के बाद भी मुस्लिम पुरुषों में ऊंची जाति के हिंदू पुरुषों की तुलना में मौत का जोखिम 21 फीसदी कम था।
शोधकर्ताओं ने इसके पीछे कुछ संभावित वजहों का जिक्र किया है। उनके मुताबिक, मुस्लिम समुदाय के वयस्कों में शराब का सेवन कम होना और कई राज्यों में मुस्लिम आबादी का शहरी इलाकों में ज्यादा रहना इसकी संभावित वजहें हो सकती हैं। शहरी इलाकों में रहने से स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं तक पहुंच भी बेहतर हो सकती है।
हालांकि, मुस्लिम महिलाओं में ऐसा अंतर देखने को नहीं मिला। 2019-21 के आंकड़ों के अनुसार, आर्थिक स्थिति और भौगोलिक परिस्थितियों को ध्यान में रखने के बाद मुस्लिम महिलाओं में ऊंची जाति की हिंदू महिलाओं की तुलना में मृत्यु का जोखिम उल्लेखनीय रूप से अलग नहीं पाया गया।
पुरुषों के मुकाबले महिलाओं की मृत्यु दर में तेजी से आई गिरावट
स्टडी में एक और अहम बात सामने आई है। पिछले दो दशकों में भारत में महिलाओं की वयस्क मृत्यु दर में पुरुषों के मुकाबले ज्यादा तेजी से गिरावट आई है। 1998-99 में 15 से 59 साल की उम्र के बीच प्रति 1,000 महिलाओं में 208 की मौत होने की संभावना थी।
2019-21 तक यह आंकड़ा घटकर 125 रह गया। यानी इसमें करीब 40 फीसदी की गिरावट आई। वहीं, पुरुषों में यह गिरावट काफी कम रही। 1998-99 में प्रति 1,000 पुरुषों में 268 की मौत होने की संभावना थी, जो 2019-21 में घटकर 221 रह गई। इस तरह पुरुषों की मृत्यु दर में करीब 17 फीसदी की कमी आई।
कोविड महामारी के दौरान बढ़ी पुरुषों की मृत्यु दर
रिसर्च में यह भी सामने आया कि पुरुषों की वयस्क मृत्यु दर में 2015-16 से 2019-21 के बीच बढ़ोतरी हुई। इस दौरान प्रति 1,000 पुरुषों में मौत की संभावना 209 से बढ़कर 221 हो गई। शोधकर्ताओं के मुताबिक, इस बढ़ोतरी की एक बड़ी वजह कोविड-19 महामारी के दौरान पुरुषों की अधिक मौतें हो सकती हैं। इसके अलावा कामकाज से जुड़ी जोखिम भरी परिस्थितियां भी पुरुषों की मृत्यु दर को प्रभावित कर सकती हैं।
गरीबी कम करने से घट सकती है मृत्यु दर
शोधकर्ताओं का कहना है कि भारत में लोगों की आर्थिक स्थिति और उनकी जीवित रहने की संभावना के बीच गहरा संबंध है। बेहतर आर्थिक स्थिति होने से लोगों को स्वास्थ्य सेवाओं, बेहतर खानपान और सुरक्षित रहने की परिस्थितियों तक पहुंच मिल सकती है।
स्टडी में कहा गया है कि आर्थिक स्थिरता बढ़ाने और गरीबी कम करने से सभी सामाजिक समूहों में वयस्क मृत्यु दर को कम करने में काफी मदद मिल सकती है। इसके साथ ही जाति और सामाजिक समूहों के आधार पर मौजूद असमानताओं को दूर करने के लिए विशेष योजनाओं और बेहतर स्वास्थ्य नीतियों की भी जरूरत है।
यह भी पढ़ें: दिल्ली: जामा मस्जिद थाने में 9 पुलिसवालों पर चाकू से हमला, VIP ड्यूटी के चलते 30 पुलिसकर्मी कहीं और थे तैनात
दिल्ली के जामा मस्जिद पुलिस स्टेशन में एक 30 साल के व्यक्ति ने थाने के अंदर पुलिसवालों पर चाकू से हमला कर दिया। इस हमले में सब इंस्पेक्टर समेत 9 पुलिसवाले घायल हो गए। आरोपी अपनी पॉकेट में चाकू लेकर थाने के अंदर पहुंचा और पुलिसकर्मियों पर हमला कर दिया। पूरी खबर पढ़ने के लिए क्लिक करें।

title: Diwali Night Koyta Attack: Accused Apprehended In Pune
description: A 19-year-old youth, Ganesh Laxman Shetty, has been arrested in Pune for allegedly attacking a woman with a 'koyta' (sickle) on Diwali night following an argument over a firecracker. He was apprehended from Pune railway station on Tuesday after being on the run.
author: Text Feed
content:
A 19-year-old youth has been arrested in Pune for a brutal "koyta" attack on a woman on Diwali night, following an argument over a firecracker, highlighting concerns about public safety during festive seasons.
Key Points
- A youth was arrested on Wednesday for allegedly attacking a 19-year-old woman with a "koyta" on Diwali night in Pune.
- The accused, Ganesh Laxman Shetty (19), was apprehended from Pune railway station on Tuesday.
- The attack followed a heated argument on Diwali when the woman's father's autorickshaw ran over a firecracker.
- Shetty chased the autorickshaw and attacked the woman with a sickle after the initial confrontation.
- He has been booked for attempt to murder under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
A youth who was absconding after allegedly attacking a 19-year-old woman with a "koyta" (heavy sickle) following an argument on Diwali night in Pune has been arrested, a police official said on Wednesday.
Details Of The Attack And Arrest
Accused Ganesh Laxman Shetty (19) was taken into custody from Pune railway station on Tuesday, he said.
Police said the woman was travelling in an autorickshaw driven by her father on Diwali when the three-wheeler ran over a firecracker, triggering a heated exchange between her and Shetty.
After some time, when they left the spot, Shetty chased the autorickshaw and attacked her with a koyta. He had been on the run since then, the official said.
Shetty has been booked for attempt to murder under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, he added.

title: IAS officer harassment: Udhayanidhi seeks TVK MLA's arrest, targets Vijay
description: Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin has formally complained to the state DGP, demanding the immediate arrest of TVK Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh and a CBI probe into the alleged harassment of a district collector. Stalin also sought to name Chief Secretary M Sai Kumar as an accused for allegedly attempting to cover up the offence, questioning the Chief Minister's silence on the matter. The DMK leader highlighted the delay in registering an FIR and criticised the government for allegedly shielding the accused, while also addressing other allegations against DMK functionaries.
author: Senjo M R
content:
Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin has intensified political pressure, demanding a CBI probe into the alleged harassment of a district collector by TVK Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh and questioning the Chief Minister's handling of the sensitive issue.
Key Points
- Udhayanidhi Stalin formally complained to the state DGP on Wednesday, demanding the immediate arrest of TVK Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh for alleged harassment of a district collector.
- Stalin also sought a CBI probe into the matter and accused Chief Secretary M Sai Kumar of attempting to cover up the offence by asking the IAS officer to seek a transfer.
- The DMK leader criticised the Chief Minister for alleged silence, noting it took 116 days to register an FIR against the legislator, only after judicial intervention earlier this week.
- Udhayanidhi also demanded action against Assembly Deputy Speaker M Ravishankar over a separate assault allegation that surfaced 16 days ago.
- He defended DMK MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan and youth wing functionary Ashik against counter-allegations, claiming the BDO spoke rudely to Karthikeyan and Ashik had previously filed a complaint against his accuser.
Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Wednesday submitted a formal complaint to the state DGP, demanding the immediate arrest of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh and a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the alleged harassment of the district collector.
Speaking to reporters in Chennai after meeting the police chief, Udhayanidhi also sought that chief secretary M Sai Kumar be named an accused in the case for allegedly attempting to cover up the offence.
Demand For CBI Probe And Chief Secretary's Role
Claiming that the woman IAS officer had lodged a complaint with the chief secretary 116 days ago on July 31, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader alleged that instead of initiating action, the top bureaucrat had tried to hush up the matter by asking her to seek a transfer to another district.
"I want to ask whether the chief secretary informed the chief minister about this issue. If he did not, it is a grave mistake. If he did, why has the CM remained silent till today," Udhayanidhi asked, taking a jibe at Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay for allegedly "sleeping" despite holding the law and order portfolio.
He pointed out that it took 116 days even to register an FIR against the legislator, and that action was initiated only after judicial intervention.
The Madras High Court took up the matter earlier this week, following which police registered a case and served summons on Vignesh.
Stating that the opposition had "zero trust" in the state government and the chief minister, Udhayanidhi alleged that the administration had spent the past four months trying to shield the accused and demanded that the case be handed over to the CBI.
He noted that DMK MP and deputy general secretary Kanimozhi was the first to bring the incident to public attention, and hit out at "virtual warriors" for launching derogatory online attacks against the victim since the allegations surfaced.
Opposition Questions Government's Handling Of Cases
In his representation to the DGP, Udhayanidhi also demanded police action and the arrest of the Assembly Deputy Speaker M Ravishankar over a separate assault allegation that surfaced 16 days ago.
He claimed that although a video had been circulated showing the Deputy Speaker and the complainant speaking amicably, the latter subsequently told the media that he was coerced into recording it and stood by his assault charge.
Questioned by reporters about social media claims by ruling party supporters that bureaucrats remained sympathetic to the DMK, Udhayanidhi asked whether there was any precedent in India of an MLA allegedly sending obscene messages to a district collector and creating a ruckus at her camp office in an inebriated state.
Mocking the TVK government's electoral pitch of bringing 'maatram' (change), he said the public had begun calling it 'durnaatram' (stench).
DMK Defends Its Functionaries Against Counter-Allegations
Dismissing counter-allegations levelled by the TVK against DMK functionaries in Kallakurichi district as an attempt to divert attention, Udhayanidhi defended Rishivandiyam DMK MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against charges of intimidating a woman official.
He said Karthikeyan had merely called the Block Development Officer (BDO) as part of his duty after a woman worker from an oppressed community engaged in the Breakfast Scheme complained of being scolded by her.
On November 18, a complaint letter written by a woman government official in Kallakurichi district surfaced, triggering a political row.
In the letter, the official alleged that the Rishivandiyam DMK MLA called her at 8.32 pm on October 18 regarding the appointment of a specific woman worker under the Breakfast Scheme in the Tirukoilur Panchayat Union. She claimed the legislator spoke to her disrespectfully and issued threats over the phone.
Udhayanidhi alleged that the BDO had spoken rudely to the legislator.
He said Karthikeyan had lodged a complaint with the District Collector, adding that three other individuals -- Vimala, Bhuvaneswari, and Subramanian -- had also lodged police complaints against the official.
Addressing Further Allegations Against DMK Members
On marriage-fraud allegations against DMK youth wing functionary Ashik, Udhayanidhi said an internal inquiry revealed that Ashik had lodged a police complaint against the same woman nearly three months ago alleging she had cheated him, which went uninvestigated.
"The police are under their control. If there is valid evidence, let them (government) take action as per law," he added.

title: 26/11 terrorist Ajmal Kasab's lawyers still to be paid
description: Two lawyers, Amin Solkar and Farhana Shah, who represented 26/11 Mumbai terror attack perpetrator Ajmal Kasab before the Bombay High Court in 2010, are still awaiting their remuneration 15 years after the proceedings concluded. Despite being appointed by the Maharashtra government and their pay scale explicitly linked to that of special public prosecutors, the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority (MSLSA) is demanding detailed bills and memos, which the lawyers deem unreasonable after such a long period.
author: Sunanda P
content:
Two lawyers who represented the lone captured 26/11 Mumbai terror attack perpetrator, Ajmal Kasab, before the Bombay high court in 2010 are still awaiting their remuneration 15 years after the proceedings concluded, despite their official appointment by the Maharashtra government.
Key Points
- Amin Solkar and Farhana Shah, who defended Ajmal Kasab in the Bombay high court, have not received their fees for 15 years.
- They were appointed by the Maharashtra government in 2010, with remuneration linked to special public prosecutors.
- The Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority (MSLSA) is demanding detailed bills and memos, which the lawyers find unreasonable after so long.
- Other lawyers involved in the Kasab trial, like Abbas Kazmi, had their remuneration settled promptly.
- Kasab was hanged on November 21, 2012, after his death sentence was upheld by the high court and Supreme Court.
Eighteen years after the 26/11 terror attacks, two lawyers who set aside their other cases to represent the lone captured Pakistani terrorist Ajmal Kasab continue to await their remuneration.
Amin Solkar and Farhana Shah represented Kasab before the Bombay high court for nine months following their appointment by the Maharashtra government in 2010.
The two were nominated by the high court and appointed by the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority (MSLSA) via a notification on June 8, 2010, to defend Kasab in his appeal against the death penalty awarded to him by a trial court.
Unpaid Dues and Official Demands
According to the notification, signed by the then secretary A K Sonawane, Solkar was to be paid on a par with a special public prosecutor and Shah was to receive remuneration equivalent to that of an additional public prosecutor conducting a death penalty confirmation case.
Official sources pegged this amount between Rs 1,500 and Rs 2,000 per day.
However, more than 15 years after the high court proceedings concluded, both advocates say they are yet to receive their dues.
"We have still not received our fees for representing Kasab. I have been corresponding with the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority time and again, but there seems to be no positive headway," Solkar told PTI.
According to both lawyers, whenever they raise the matter with the MSLSA, they are asked to submit detailed bills and memos specifying the exact number of dates and hours they appeared for the accused, a demand termed by them as "unreasonable" after so many years, and also pointing out that nobody would retain granular records of daily court hours over a decade later.
Contrasting Experiences and Legal Provisions
Ajmal Kasab was hanged on November 21, 2012, at the Yerwada Central Jail in Pune.
Solkar said that their appointment letters explicitly linked their pay scale to that of the prosecution.
"What is stopping the government from using the same pay scale and clearing our dues?" Solkar questioned.
Echoing his concern, Shah questioned the insistence on itemised memos when both the government notification and the order passed by the then Chief Justice of the high court clearly defined their fee structure.
"We gave our entire day for nine months to argue this case. We had to keep all our other cases on the backburner so that there was no hurdle caused to the proceedings," Shah said, adding that the notification stipulated their fees were to be cleared as soon as the high court delivered its verdict.
An official from the state legal services authority maintained that, as per standard practice, advocates are required to submit formal bills and memos for the clearance of fees.
In contrast, advocate Abbas Kazmi, who defended Kasab during the trial before special judge M L Tahaliyani, said his dues were settled promptly.
"My remuneration was cleared by the government soon after the completion of the trial," Kazmi said.
Under legal provisions, if an accused fails to engage a counsel, the court nominates a lawyer from the legal services authority to ensure a fair trial.
The 26/11 Attacks and Kasab's Fate
The Bombay high court commenced hearing the confirmation of Kasab's death sentence and his appeal in June 2010, upholding the capital punishment in February 2011.
The Supreme Court subsequently affirmed the verdict, and Kasab, who was lodged at the Arthur Road prison following his capture, was hanged at Yerwada Central Jail in Pune on November 21, 2012.
A total of 166 people, including six Americans, were killed in the November 26, 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, during which 10 heavily armed Pakistani terrorists laid siege to key locations across the city for over 60 hours.

title: Pune Court Attack: Victim Critical With Skull Fracture, Severe Hand Injuries; Next 72 Hours Crucial
description: Sassoon General Hospital Dean Dr Yellappa Jadhav said Kiwale was brought to the hospital with multiple injuries to both hands, including fractures, and the back of his head
author: Ankit Shukla
content:
Pune: Mandar Maruti Kiwale, who was attacked outside the Pune District and Sessions Court on Wednesday, remains critical at Sassoon General Hospital. He has suffered severe injuries to both hands, a fracture at the base of his skull and significant blood loss. Doctors said the next 72 hours would be crucial as they assess the possibility of internal bleeding in his brain.
Sassoon General Hospital Dean Dr Yellappa Jadhav said Kiwale was brought to the hospital with multiple injuries to both hands, including fractures, and the back of his head.
Watch Video:
Kiwale also suffered bullet graze injuries to the right side of his back and the upper part of his right arm. The bullet injuries appeared to be superficial, with no deep penetration, Dr Jadhav said.
Kiwale's blood pressure was 80/60 mmHg at the time of admission, indicating significant blood loss. It improved to 100/70 mmHg after doctors administered intravenous fluids.
Dr Jadhav said the patient was speaking normally and responding to treatment. However, doctors are yet to determine whether the skull fracture has caused bleeding within the brain.
A team of specialists, including general surgeons, orthopaedic surgeons, plastic surgeons and neurosurgeons, has stabilised him for now. Doctors were scheduled to take him to the operation theatre for further treatment.
The dean said it was too early to comment on Kiwale's prognosis. Doctors will assess the extent of blood loss and the results of further investigations before deciding on the next course of treatment.
Attacked outside court on hearing day
Kiwale was attacked near Gate No. 4 of the court on Wednesday afternoon. The assailants allegedly opened fire before attacking him with koytas (sharp-edged weapons) and fleeing on two-wheelers.
The attack took place on the day Kiwale's murder case was scheduled for a hearing. He is Accused No. 3 in Sessions Case No. 759/2025, pertaining to a murder case registered at Ambegaon Police Station. The case was at the evidence stage.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) (Crime) Gauhar Hasan had earlier told The Free Press Journal that the police had identified some suspects and deployed multiple Crime Branch teams to trace them. The motive behind the attack is still under investigation.

title: Nashik: Gangapur Dam Boat Club Unlikely To Reopen Before December Amid Pending Permissions
description: The MTDC has not announced a definitive date for the resumption of operations. The boat club uses water from the dam, and its reopening depends on the completion of the formal agreement process, which requires permission from the Water Resources Department to use the water
author: Prashant Nikale
content:
Nashik: For the past four to five months, tourists visiting Gangapur Dam to enjoy boating have had to return disappointed. The Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC) Boat Club, which has remained closed since the monsoon, shows no signs of reopening. The process of obtaining permission from the Water Resources Department and renewing the agreement remains stalled at the administrative level.
As the matter falls outside the jurisdiction of the local office and requires a decision from higher authorities, tourists will likely have to wait until after December for a resolution. In recent years, the boat club at Gangapur Dam had become a major tourist attraction in Nashik, drawing residents and visitors from outside the city. With the facility closed, the tourist spot now lies deserted.
The MTDC has not announced a definitive date for the resumption of operations. The boat club uses water from the dam, and its reopening depends on the completion of the formal agreement process, which requires permission from the Water Resources Department to use the water.
A five-year agreement with the MTDC expired in December 2025. Although the authorities extended permission for a short period thereafter, the state government’s new tourism policy necessitated a formal renewal of the agreement. The government has introduced new provisions regarding the leasing of government land in dam areas, and the agreement must now comply with the updated policy.
A proposal must be submitted to the regulatory board for approval, with higher authorities rather than the local office taking the final decision.
The Executive Engineer of the Water Resources Department clarified that the agreement must be renewed in accordance with the provisions of the new tourism policy. He also said the local office was following up on the matter with higher authorities.
The renewal process will move forward only after the regulatory board grants approval. Consequently, a decision is likely only after December, and the date for resuming operations remains uncertain.

title: Beed CEO Orders FIR Over ₹41.33 Lakh Misappropriation In Parli Silt-Removal Scheme
description: Zilla Parishad Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jithin Rahman has ordered the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) following an inquiry that uncovered financial irregularities worth ₹41,33,511 in the implementation of the state government's Gaalmukt Dharan, Gaalyukt Shivar (silt-free dam, silt-rich farm) scheme in Wantakli gram panchayat of Parli tehsil
author: Manish Gajbhiye
content:
Beed: Zilla Parishad Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jithin Rahman has ordered the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) following an inquiry that uncovered financial irregularities worth ₹41,33,511 in the implementation of the state government's Gaalmukt Dharan, Gaalyukt Shivar (silt-free dam, silt-rich farm) scheme in Wantakli gram panchayat of Parli tehsil.
Acting on the inquiry report, Rahman on Nov 20 directed Parli Panchayat Samiti Block Development Officer (BDO) Rajvardhan Bhosale to lodge a formal complaint at the local police station and initiate legal action.
Following the directive, Bhosale entrusted Panchayat Samiti Extension Officer RB Shendge with further action in the matter on Nov 23.
The irregularities came to light after incumbent Wantakli Sarpanch Gangabai Dnyanoba Hange lodged a formal complaint on Sept 25, 2026, alleging large-scale misappropriation of funds meant for farmers.
According to the complaint, former sarpanch Hanumant Mane and the gram panchayat officer concerned allegedly colluded to illegally disburse funds using joint signatures between 2023 and 2026, even though Mane's term as sarpanch had expired on Dec 31, 2022. A subsequent joint inquiry at the Parli Panchayat Samiti and Beed Zilla Parishad levels substantiated the allegations of financial misconduct.
No-confidence motion against sarpanch
Meanwhile, the corruption probe has triggered political friction in the village. Shortly after the inquiry gained momentum, eight gram panchayat members moved a no-confidence motion against Hange, who had raised the allegations. Voting on the motion is expected to take place soon.

title: वैभव सूर्यवंशी को टी 20 इंटरनेशनल टीम में परमानेंट जगह कब मिलेगी
description: एशिया कप राइज़िंग स्टार्स में इंडिया ए की तरफ़ से खेलते हुए यूएई के ख़िलाफ़ 53 गेंद में 204 रनों की रिकॉर्डतोड़ पारी खेलने वाले वैभव इंडियन टीम के ओपनर के तौर पर कब अपनी जगह पक्की कर पाएंगे?
author: भरत शर्मा
content:
वैभव सूर्यवंशी को टी20 इंटरनेशनल टीम में परमानेंट जगह कब मिलेगी?
  - Author, भरत शर्मा
  - पदनाम, बीबीसी संवाददाता
- प्रकाशित
- पढ़ने का समय: 7 मिनट
टीनएजर बच्चों में वीडियो गेम काफ़ी पसंद किया जाता है. लेकिन 15 साल के वैभव सूर्यवंशी ऐसे टीनएजर हैं, जो आजकल प्रोफ़ेशनल क्रिकेट को ही वीडियो गेम में बदल रहे हैं.
24 नवंबर को दोहा में हुए एक मैच में उन्होंने ऐसा ही कुछ किया.
वैभव ने लिस्ट ए क्रिकेट की एक ही पारी में सबसे तेज़ 100 रन (28 बॉल), सबसे तेज़ 150 रन (40 बॉल) और सबसे तेज़ 200 रन (52 बॉल) का रिकॉर्ड बना दिया.
उनकी इस पारी में कुल 28 छक्के थे. जी हां, 28 छक्के. यानी 204 रनों की इस पारी में 168 रन छक्कों से ही बटोर लिए.
वैभव की ताज़ा पारी ने एक बार फिर इस सवाल को हवा दी है कि ये लड़का इंडिया की टी20 क्रिकेट टीम में बतौर ओपनर अपनी जगह पक्की कब कर पाएगा? और क्या टी20 के अलावा उन्हें वनडे क्रिकेट में भी आज़माया जाना चाहिए?
आंकड़े क्या कहते हैं
सबसे पहले डेटा पर ही नज़र डाल लेते हैं.
अब तक खेले गए 10 टी20 इंटरनेशनल मैच में वैभव ने 29.50 की एवरेज और 185.53 के स्ट्राइक रेट से 295 रन बनाए हैं, जिनमें सबसे ज़्यादा पारी 81 रनों की रही.
उन्हें अब तक इंग्लैंड के सामने तीन, ज़िम्बाब्वे के सामने तीन, न्यूज़ीलैंड के सामने दो और पाकिस्तान-श्रीलंका के सामने एक-एक मैच में मौका दिया गया है.
दूसरी ओर, आईपीएल की अब तक खेली गई 23 पारियों में उन्होंने 1028 रन बनाए हैं, जहां उनकी औसत 44.69 और स्ट्राइक रेट 228.95 रहा.
इनमें से सात मैच उन्होंने 2025 सीज़न और 16 मैच साल 2026 के आईपीएल में खेले.
और आईपीएल 2026 में ही उन्होंने क्रिस गेल का एक सीज़न में सबसे ज़्यादा छक्के मारने का रिकॉर्ड भी तोड़ा था.
गेल ने 2012 सीज़न में 59 छक्के मारे थे, जबकि राजस्थान रॉयल्स के इस टीएनएज सेंसेशन ने 2026 में 72 छक्के जड़े.
छक्कों का ज़िक्र इसलिए ज़रूरी है क्योंकि वैभव सूर्यवंशी के खेलने के स्टाइल में उनके एग्रेशन और सिक्स हिटिंग एबिलिटी की बात बार-बार होती है.
कुछ एक्सपर्ट का मानना है कि वैभव सूर्यवंशी को भारत की टी20 इंटरनेशनल टीम में परमानेंट जगह मिलनी चाहिए और ओपनर की उनकी पोज़िशन से कुछ समय तक छेड़छाड़ नहीं की जानी चाहिए.
'कंपटीशन तगड़ा है'
वरिष्ठ खेल पत्रकार और विशेषज्ञ अयाज़ मेनन से जब ये पूछा गया कि ऐसी शानदार पारियां खेलने के बावजूद वैभव को टीम में जगह देकर लंबे तक क्यों नहीं आज़माया जाता तो उन्होंने कहा कि ये बिलकुल वाजिब सवाल है.
हाल में इंडियन टीम ने न्यूज़ीलैंड में पाँच मैचों की टी20 सिरीज़ खेली जिनमें से दो में वैभव सूर्यवंशी को टीम में खिलाया गया.
इनमें से एक मैच में उन्हें ओपन करने का मौका मिला और उन्होंने 19 बॉल में 45 रन बनाए.
कप्तान श्रेयस अय्यर से जब सिरीज़ से पहले वैभव को मौका देने के के बारे में पूछा गया था तो उन्होंने कहा था, ''ये ज़रूरी है कि उसके जैसा टैलेंट ड्रेसिंग रूम के आसपास ख़ुश रहे.''
अय्यर के मुताबिक़, ''वो बहुत ही यंग है और उसके पास आने वाले सालों में कई सारे मौके आएंगे. वो सीधे ऐसे टीम में वॉक इन नहीं कर सकता क्योंकि हमारे ओपनर भी लगातार अच्छा प्रदर्शन कर रहे हैं.''
लेकिन क्या ये सही स्ट्रेटेजी है?
अयाज़ मेमन ने बीबीसी से कहा, ''ज़्यादातर लोगों का कहना है कि वैभव सूर्यवंशी 'चाइल्ड प्रोडिजी' हैं या वंस इन ए जनरेशन प्लेयर हैं. ऐसे खिलाड़ी को अगर सही समय पर मौके न मिलें और वो भी लगातार, तो इसके नुक़सान भी हो सकते हैं. सचिन तेंदुलकर को भी बहुत कम उम्र में मौका दिया गया था और उन्हें जब मौका दिया गया तो फिर लगातार मौके दिए गए, उसके बाद उन्होंने जो किया वो हम सभी के सामने है.'
साल 1989 में पाकिस्तान के ख़िलाफ़ सचिन तेंदुलकर ने जब टेस्ट और वनडे में डेब्यू किया तो उनकी उम्र 16 साल थी.
अगर वर्ल्ड रिकॉर्ड की बात करें तो पाकिस्तान के हसन रज़ा ने महज़ 14 साल 233 दिनों की उम्र में ज़िम्बाब्वे के ख़िलाफ़ पहला वनडे खेला था.
आम तौर पर इंग्लैंड और ऑस्ट्रेलिया में काउंटी और स्टेट टीम से खेलने वाले खिलाड़ियों को नेशनल टीम में जगह बनाने में काफ़ी समय लग जाता है, लेकिन इंटरनेशनल क्रिकेट में कम उम्र में डेब्यू करने और अपनी जगह बनाने वाले एशियाई खिलाड़ियों की लिस्ट लंबी है.
आपके लिए नितिन श्रीवास्तव द्वारा चुनी गईं खास कहानियाँ
और जानें
समाप्त
मंगलवार को यूएई के ख़िलाफ़ खेली गई वैभव की पारी को लेकर अयाज़ मेमन ने कहा, ''वैभव की कल की पारी एक फ़्रीक पारी थी, जैसे कि वो सेलेक्टर्स को कोई मैसेज दे रहे हों. ऐसा खिलाड़ी कभी-कभार आता है. जब अच्छा खेलने के बावजूद टीम में परमानेंसी की उम्मीद नहीं दिखती तो खिलाड़ी के मेंटल स्ट्रेंथ पर भी इसका असर पड़ सकता है.''
उन्होंने कहा, ''कोई भी खिलाड़ी ये सोच सकता है कि अच्छा खेलने के बावजूद टीम में ठीक से जगह नहीं बन रही, अब और क्या किया जाए. दस मैच में फ़ेल होने पर बाहर करना समझ आता है. लेकिन एक-दो मैच खिलाना, फिर बाहर कर देना सही नहीं है. वैभव को लंबा मौका दिए जाने की ज़रूरत है.''
लेकिन कप्तान अय्यर की ओपनिंग पेयर की दलील का क्या. इस पर मेमन ने कहा, ''ये बात सही है कि अभिषेक शर्मा और संजू सैमसन, दोनों बढ़िया खिलाड़ी हैं, लेकिन आपको वैभव के लिए जगह बनाने के रास्ते खोजने होंगे. ऐसा नहीं कर सकते कि कभी खिला रहे हैं, कभी बाहर कर दे रहे हैं.'
बीबीसी ने वैभव के बारे में जब जानी-मानी स्पोर्ट्स एक्सपर्ट और राइटर मीनाक्षी राव से बात की तो उन्होंने कहा कि इस खिलाड़ी को लेकर बैलेंस्ड अप्रोच की ज़रूरत है.
मीनाक्षी के मुताबिक़, ''वैभव को लेकर चारों तरफ़ काफ़ी हाइप है. जब वो बाकी जगह अच्छा करते हैं तो काफ़ी चर्चा होती है, जब इंडियन टीम से खेलते हुए किसी दिन नाकाम हो जाते हैं तो कह दिया जाता है कि ख़राब खेल रहा है, ये सब सही नहीं है. ऐसी उम्मीद करना बेमानी है कि वो हर मैच में स्कोर करेंगे. लेकिन उन्हें मौके लगातार देने होंगे.''
मीनाक्षी का कहना है कि वैभव की आक्रामक बल्लेबाज़ी उनका यूएसपी है, और इससे छेड़छाड़ नहीं की जानी चाहिए. लेकिन इसके साथ-साथ उन्हें इंटरनेशनल पिच और इंटरनेशनल बॉलर्स के सामने टेस्ट ज़रूर करना चाहिए.
साथ ही वैभव को कुछ टी20 मैचों में 30-40 रनों की पारियां लगातार खेलकर अपनी कंसिस्टेंसी का अंदाज़ा भी देना होगा.
उन्होंने कहा, ''वैभव को इंटरनेशनल क्रिकेट में पिच और बॉलर को समझने की ज़रूरत होगी. क्योंकि आने वाले समय में बॉलर भी उनके खेल को रीड करेंगे, ऐसे में उन्हें जवाब खोजने होंगे. टेक्निकली अपने खेल को और सॉलिड बनाना होगा. वो ड्रेसिंग रूम में रहकर काफ़ी कुछ सीख सकते हैं.''
मीनाक्षी का मानना है कि वैभव को अगले साल होने वाले वनडे वर्ल्ड कप से पहले कुछ वनडे मैच में भी खिलाना चाहिए. साथ ही उन्हें घरेलू क्रिकेट में भी जब-जब मौका मिले, लंबे फॉर्मेट भी खेलने चाहिए.
उन्होंने कहा, 'ये बात सही है कि उनकी उम्र कम है, ऐसे में टीम में जगह पक्की करने के लिए उनके पास अभी काफ़ी समय है. लेकिन वो जिस फॉर्म में है, जो एग्रेशन उनके खेल में आज है, वो बरक़रार रखना होगा. टैलेंट की कोई कमी नहीं है, लेकिन उसके साथ कंसिस्टेंसी, एडेप्टिबिलिटी, मैच की अंडरस्टैंडिंग और टेक्निकल इंफो चाहिए होगी. और ये सब उन्हें इंटरनेशनल मैच में खेलकर ही मिलेगा.''
मीनाक्षी के मुताबिक़, 'अगर वो 15 साल के बजाय 16 साल की उम्र में परमानेंट प्लेयर बन जाएं तो भी कोई दिक़्क़त नहीं है, क्योंकि उनके पास समय है. लेकिन उन्हें सेलेक्टिव टूर ज़रूर खिलाने होंगे क्योंकि दुनिया भर के बॉलर ने उन्हें रीड करना शुरू कर दिया होगा. और उन्हें भी अब इंटरनेशनल बॉलर को रीड करना सीखना होगा.''
बीबीसी के लिए कलेक्टिव न्यूज़रूम की ओर से प्रकाशित.
