title: Memories and scars of 26/11 Mumbai attacks stay alive, 18 years on
description: Eighteen years after the 2008 terror attacks that shook Mumbai and exposed glaring lacunae in India's security and intelligence apparatus, the horrors of the 60hour assault and  bloodletting remain etched in public memory.
author: PTI
content:
Memories and scars of 26/11 Mumbai attacks stay alive, 18 years on
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 18:31 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 18:31 IST
The multi-day siege exposed critical vulnerabilities in coastal security and intelligence coordination, triggering a sweeping overhaul of India's counter-terrorism framework. While key conspirators face prosecution years
Eighteen years after the 2008 terror attacks that shook Mumbai and exposed glaring lacunae in India’s security and intelligence apparatus, the horrors of the 60-hour assault and bloodletting remain etched in public memory.
As the financial capital, know for its unbreakable spirit and courage in the face of adversity, prepares to commemorate the 18th anniversary of 26/11, the carnage remains a grim reminder of the human cost of terrorism and the importance of sustained vigilance and preparedness against security threats.
The November 26, 2008 attacks, carried out by 10 heavily armed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists who sailed into Mumbai from Pakistan, left 166 people, including foreigners, dead and more than 300 injured, making it one of the deadliest terror strikes in an Indian city.
Mumbai has endured several major terrorist attacks over the past three decades or so. On March 12, 1993, bomb blasts struck 12 locations in the megapolis killing 257 and injuring thousands. The city reeled under the serial train blasts on July 11, 2006, killing 188 people, while 27 people died in triple explosions at Dadar, Zaveri Bazaar and Opera House on July 13, 2011.
The 2008 attacks, which began on the night of November 26 and continued until the morning of November 29, targeted several prominent locations, including the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Trident Hotel, Nariman House (Chabad House), Leopold Cafe and Cama and Albless Hospital.
The heavily armed terrorists launched coordinated attacks, taking hostages and engaging security personnel in prolonged gun battles. The operations posed enormous challenges as the attackers occupied buildings, used their height and layout to their advantage and held people hostage.
The coordinated response by the Mumbai Police, armed police personnel, Indian Navy’s Marine Commandos and the National Security Guard (NSG) eventually brought the roughly 60-hours siege to an end.
The sea-borne attacks exposed vulnerabilities in coastal security, intelligence gathering and coordination among security agencies, prompting a major overhaul of India’s counter-terrorism preparedness.
Among the 10 attackers, Mohammed Ajmal Kasab was captured alive. He was subsequently tried, convicted and hanged in November 2012. David Coleman Headley, one of the key conspirators who conducted reconnaissance of Mumbai before the attacks, later deposed before an Indian court through video-conferencing from the United States.
Tahawwur Hussain Rana, another accused in the 26/11 conspiracy, was extradited from the US in 2025 to stand trial in India.
However, several masterminds and handlers of the attacks continue to remain beyond India’s reach, with many believed to be based in Pakistan.
The chargesheet filed in the case had stated that the manner in which the attacks were conducted showed they were meticulously planned and executed after extensive training, preparation and briefing.
The attacks prompted global condemnation and led to significant changes in India’s counter-terrorism measures.
Every year floral tributes are paid at the Mumbai Police headquarters to those who made the ultimate sacrifice while fighting terrorists during the attacks. Homage is also paid at Mumbai CSMT, Cama and Albless Hospital and other locations which were targeted by the Pakistani terrorists.
Mumbaikars also gather at ”Prerana Sthal”, the statue of Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Ombale, who fought with terrorists with a lathi and was killed while catching the terrorist Kasab at Girgaon Chowpatty in south Mumbai.

title: Cracked margins: How Tamil Nadu's bird flu scare and 50% surge in maize prices are squeezing poultry farmers
description: Ex-farm egg prices have dropped 10–20% over the past 10 days—sliding to ₹5.60 in Namakkal—after a Tamil Nadu bird flu outbreak disrupted exports and pushed surplus stock into domestic markets, compounding a 50% surge in maize feed costs and weaker seasonal demand.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Cracked margins: How Tamil Nadu's bird flu scare and 50% surge in maize prices are squeezing poultry farmers
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 18:17 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 18:17 IST
Ex-farm egg prices have dropped 10–20% over the past 10 days—sliding to ₹5.60 in Namakkal—after a Tamil Nadu bird flu outbreak disrupted exports and pushed surplus stock into domestic markets, compounding a 50% surge in maize feed costs and weaker seasonal demand.
Egg prices have declined 10-20% over the past 8-10 days as a bird flu outbreak in Tamil Nadu has disrupted exports, diverting surplus supplies into the domestic market at a time when seasonal demand is weakening in southern India.
According to an Economic Times report, the sharp correction in prices has dashed poultry farmers' hopes of better winter realisations, with production costs remaining elevated due to a surge in prices of key feed ingredients such as maize and soybean meal. The combination of lower realisations and higher input costs is squeezing margins across the poultry industry.
Ex-farm egg prices, which had risen following Chhath Puja, began declining after bird flu was confirmed in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, on November 13. The outbreak prompted containment measures, including the culling of birds and a 90-day ban on poultry farming in the affected region.
Prices in Namakkal, India's largest poultry-producing hub, fell from a high of ₹6.70 per egg on November 11 to ₹5.60, a decline of around 16%. The correction has been relatively lower in Delhi, West Bengal, Gujarat and Maharashtra, where prices have dropped 6-10%, while most southern states have reported declines of more than 15%.
Export disruption adds to the supply glut
Namakkal is India's principal egg export hub and accounts for more than 90% of the country's egg exports, the report quoted Sanjeev Chintawar, chief operating officer of the National Egg Coordination Committee (NECC), as saying.
The region was exporting around 1 crore eggs a day during the corresponding period last year. However, daily exports had already fallen to around 15-20 lakh eggs just before the outbreak, according to Chintawar. The latest disruption has further aggravated the supply situation, with eggs that would otherwise have been exported finding their way into the domestic market.
Demand has also weakened in southern India during the Hindu month of Karthik, when consumption of non-vegetarian food typically declines. This has compounded the oversupply at a time when poultry farmers were expecting consumption to pick up during the winter season.
Farmers had reduced production for around two months before Diwali to manage rising feed costs and were planning to increase output ahead of winter in anticipation of better prices, Chintawar said.
He added that feed suppliers had started refusing to extend credit to poultry farmers amid subdued egg and chicken prices, affecting bird nutrition and potentially impacting productivity.
Also read: Cabinet clears ₹6,302 crore for new Assam airport, Tamil Nadu port expansion
Rising feed costs deepen farmers' losses
The price decline comes against a backdrop of sharply higher poultry feed costs. Maize prices have increased around 50% from a year earlier, while soybean meal has become approximately 30% more expensive.
Maize, broken rice, soybean meal and millets are among the key ingredients used in poultry feed. The increase in input costs has left farmers struggling to recover production expenses even as selling prices decline.
The impact is also being felt in the chicken market. Production costs for chicken have risen above ₹120 per kg, while farmers are receiving only around ₹80 per kg, the report quoted K G Anand, general manager at Venkateshwara Hatcheries, as saying.
"Farmers are bleeding," Anand said, highlighting the widening gap between production costs and realisations.
Divya Kumar Gulati, immediate past president of the Compound Livestock Feed Manufacturers Association of India, said the industry was facing widespread losses, with producers struggling to sustain operations amid the adverse market conditions.
The combination of disrupted exports, seasonal weakness in consumption and elevated feed costs has put the poultry industry under pressure just as farmers had expected the winter months to bring improved demand and better price realisations.

title: Delhi air pollution: Should you run an air purifier all day? Usage and filter replacement explained
description: Air purifiers pass the air in a room through filters that absorb particulate matter and other pollutants. These filters require cleaning or replacement at regular intervals.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Delhi air pollution: Should you run an air purifier all day? Usage and filter replacement explained
- Edited bySudarsanan M
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 18:15 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 18:15 IST
As persistent severe pollution strains household air quality, continuous indoor filtration significantly lowers airborne allergens and fine particulate matter. Maintaining optimal performance, however, requires regular m
Delhi’s air quality is expected to remain in the ‘poor’ category for the next few days, the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has predicted. The CPCB has forecast that the average air quality index (AQI) in the national capital will remain ‘poor’ until November 27. With several places in Delhi still facing pollutants like PM2.5, air purifiers are increasingly being used at homes.
Air purifiers draw the air into the machine, pass it through filters that trap or absorb the pollutants, and release the filtered air back into the room. Using an air purifier comes with questions about its duration, filters and other factors. Here is an easy guide.
Should you run an air purifier all day?
If the goal is to avoid any exposure to pollution, running an air purifier throughout the day is an effective approach. Indoor air pollution is not a static metric. Dust gets disturbed, outdoor pollution seeps indoors via windows and gaps around doors, people and pets add new pollutants to the space and cooking leads to the particles and gases.
Running the air purifier continuously can lower the amount of many common airborne pollutants, such as dust and allergens. The machines work best in an enclosed environment, with doors and windows kept shut during periods of high pollution.
What is indoor AQI?
Indoor AQI is the air quality within and around buildings and structures. Common pollutants indoors can increase the risk of health concerns.
Fuel-burning combustion appliances, tobacco products, central heating and cooling systems, products for household cleaning, personal care, or hobbies and outdoor air pollution are some of the biggest factors that lead to a poor indoor AQI.
Usage and filter replacement explained
Most air purifiers use a combination of filters, each of which is designed to tackle a different type of pollutant. Many devices also come with sensors that monitor changes in indoor air quality.
The first stage of use is usually a pre-filter, where the machine captures larger particles such as dust, pet fur and other visible debris. The next step involves an activated carbon filter, which reduces smoke and certain volatile organic compounds released by household products.
The most important stage is generally the HEPA (High Efficiency Particulate Air) filter, which traps tiny airborne particles such as fine dust, pollen, mold spores and other contaminants. It is particularly useful when dealing with particulate matter like PM2.5.
Filters accumulate dust and pollutants over time and need periodic cleaning or replacement, depending on the type and manufacturer's recommendations. A clogged filter can reduce airflow and hamper the machine’s effectiveness.
Replace HEPA filters every six months to one year, according to the manufacturer's schedule. In places with high air pollution, the filters can be replaced after four to six months.
Air purifiers can reduce indoor exposure to particulate matter but do not eliminate all pollutants or make people immune to the harmful impact of air pollution. The effectiveness of the device depends on the filtration technology, capacity of the machine, room size and duration of use.

title: सुप्रीम कोर्ट का आदेश, फिर भी नहीं जला कार्तिगई दीपम; अब कलेक्टर ने SC में दाखिल की स्टेटस रिपोर्ट
description: मदुरै जिला कलेक्टर तमिलनाडु के तिरुपरनकुंद्रम पहाड़ी पर दीपाथून स्तंभ पर कार्तिगई दीपम का दीपक न जलाने पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट में स्टेटस रिपोर्ट दाखिल की है. इसको लेकर वकील ने कहा कि नियमों का पालन नहीं किया गया.
author: श्रुति कौल
content:
Karthigai Deepam: तमिलनाडु के तिरुपरनकुंद्रम पहाड़ी पर दीपाथून स्तंभ पर कार्तिगई दीपम का दीया न जलाने को लेकर मदुरै जिला कलेक्टर की ओर से सुप्रीम कोर्ट में स्टेटस रिपोर्ट दाखिल की गई. मामले को लेकर कलेक्टर की तरफ से पेश हुए सीनियर वकील गोपाल शंकरनारायणन ने जस्टिस अरविंद कुमार और जस्टिस विपुल पंचोली की पीठ को बताया कि सभी नियमों का पालन किया गया फिर भी दीपक को विवादित जगह पर नहीं जलाया गया.
सुप्रीम कोर्ट की ओर से बीते 24 नवंबर 2026 को आदेश जारी किया गया था, जिसमें विवादित दीपाथून पर कार्तिगई दीपम जलाने की अनुमति दी गई थी. हालांकि, उस स्थल पर दीपम नहीं जलाया गया, जिसके बाद सुप्रीम कोर्ट में यह स्टेटस रिपोर्ट दाखिल की गई.
मामले को लेकर वकील गोपाल शंकरनारायणन ने दाखिल स्टेटस रिपोर्ट में कहा कि जो कुछ भी हुआ, उसके लिए मुझे स्टेटस रिपोर्ट दाखिल करनी थी. उन्होंने कोर्ट से कहा,' आप इस पर विचार कर सकते हैं, क्योंकि दुर्भाग्य से दीपाथून में यह मामला सामने नहीं आ पाया था. कलेक्टर के तौर पर मैंने उन सभी प्रक्रियाओं का पालन किया है, जिनका मुझे पालन करना था. इसलिए हमने वह रिपोर्ट दाखिल कर दी है. इस पर विचार किया जाए.'
जस्टिस अरविंद कुमार ने दाखिल रिपोर्ट को लेकर कहा,' सुप्रीम कोर्ट के आदेश के मुताबिक, कलेक्टर को इवेंट के 3 दिन बाद स्टेटस रिपोर्ट दाखिल करनी है.' इसको लेकर सीनियर वकील ने कहा कि बेहतर होगा कि प्रतिवादियों की ओर से इस मुद्दे को उठाने से खुद पहले ही कलेक्टर अदालत के ध्यान में यह मामला लाएं. वकील ने कहा,' मुझे भरोसा है है कि दूसरी ओर के लोग इस मुद्दे को उठाएंगे कि वहां दीपम नहीं जलाई गई थी. इसलिए हमने सोचा कि यही ठीक होगा कि हम खुद ही अदालत के ध्यान में यह मुद्दा लाएं.'
दीपाथून पर दीया जलाने की मांग करने वाले पक्ष की तरफ से पेश हुए वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता गुरु कृष्णकुमार ने दीया जलाने की अनुमति न मिलने को दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण बताया. उन्होंने कहा कि एक तरह से यह नियमों के उल्लंघन के लिए अग्रिम उल्लेख मांगने जैसी कोशिश है. कृष्णकुमार ने अदालत को बताया कि मंदिर के बोर्ड ऑफ ट्रस्टीज के नाम से एक बयान जारी किया गया था, जिसमें साफ कहा गया था कि परंपरा के हिसाब से ही उच्चिपिल्लयार मंदिर में दीया जलाया जाना चाहिए. हालांकि, बाद में कई पुजारियों की ओर से इस तरह के बयान जारी करने से साफ मना कर दिया गया.
वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता गुरु कृष्णकुमार ने आगे कहा कि फैसले को न मानना कोर्ट के आदेश को अनदेखा करने की एक सोची-समझी साजिश है, जिसमें वे सफल भी हो गए. उन्होंने कहा कि यह साफतौर पर कानून का उल्लंघन है. उन्होंने कहा कि अधिकारियों ने कोर्ट को आदेश मानने का पूरा भरोसा दिलाया, लेकिन आखिरी समय पर इससे मुकर गए. गुरु कृष्णकुमार ने कहा कि अखंड लौ अभी भी उच्चिपिल्लयार मंडपम में जल रही है. ऐसे में कानून का सम्मान करते हुए दीपक को दीपाथून पर स्थापित किया जाना चाहिए.

title: घाटी में ठंड का 'लॉकडाउन', कश्मीर पर सर्दी का सितम, लद्दाख भी जमा; शोपियां में -4.2, द्रास में -10.4 पर पारा!
description: कश्मीर और लद्दाख में समय से पहले कड़ाके की ठंड पड़ने लगी है. शोपियां का तापमान -4.2°C तक गिरा, द्रास -10.4°C पर जमा, जबकि श्रीनगर में न्यूनतम तापमान -1.9°C दर्ज किया गया. दोनों क्षेत्रों में कड़ाके की ठंड के कारण जनजीवन लगभग ठप हो गया है और मौसम पूरी तरह शुष्क बना हुआ है.
author: खालिद हुसैन
content:
कश्मीर और लद्दाख में समय से पहले ही कड़ाके की ठंड ने अपनी पकड़ मजबूत कर ली है. रात का तापमान फ्रीजिंग प्वॉइंट से काफी नीचे चला गया है, जिससे दोनों क्षेत्रों में सुबह की दिनचर्या लगभग ठप हो गई है। बुधवार को घाटी में शोपियां सबसे ठंडा आबादी वाला इलाका रहा, जहां तापमान -4.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया. वहीं, श्रीनगर में इस सीजन की सबसे ठंडी रात रही, जहां तापमान -1.9 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिर गया.
मौसम विभाग (MeT) के आंकड़ों के मुताबिक, श्रीनगर का न्यूनतम तापमान सामान्य से 2.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस नीचे रहा, जबकि श्रीनगर हवाई अड्डे पर तापमान और भी गिरकर -2.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया.
इस कड़ाके की सूखी ठंड से बचने के लिए लोग पारंपरिक 'फेरन' (ऊनी वस्त्र) पहन रहे हैं और 'कांगड़ी' (अंगीठी) और हीटिंग उपकरणों का सहारा ले रहे हैं. घाटी में सुबह के समय सड़कों और खुले मैदानों पर पाला जम गया है.
जोजिला दर्रे के पार, केंद्र शासित प्रदेश लद्दाख में भी तापमान फ्रीजिंग प्वॉइंट से काफी नीचे चला गया है, जिससे जल स्रोत जम गए हैं और बाहरी गतिविधियां धीमी हो गई हैं. दुनिया की दूसरी सबसे ठंडी आबादी वाली जगह, द्रास में तापमान -10.4 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जबकि लेह में न्यूनतम तापमान -8.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा. करगिल में तापमान -7.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्योमा में -9.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिर गया, जो इस ठंडे रेगिस्तानी इलाके में कड़ाके की ठंड की शुरुआत को दर्शाता है. पूरी घाटी में तापमान शून्य से नीचे पहुंच गया है.
रात भर की कड़ाके की ठंड का सबसे ज्यादा असर दक्षिण कश्मीर में देखने को मिला:
उत्तर और मध्य कश्मीर में, लगभग सभी मौसम केंद्रों पर तापमान शून्य से नीचे चला गया:
कश्मीर और लद्दाख की कड़ाके की ठंड के विपरीत, जम्मू संभाग में रातें अपेक्षाकृत नरम रहीं, हालांकि ऊंचाई वाले इलाकों में तापमान में काफी गिरावट दर्ज की गई:
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, पिछले 24 घंटों में जम्मू, कश्मीर और लद्दाख में कहीं भी बारिश या बर्फबारी नहीं हुई है. मौसम विभाग के अधिकारियों ने बताया कि रात में आसमान साफ रहने के कारण 'रेडिएटिव कूलिंग' (ऊष्मा का तेजी से निकलना) बढ़ रही है, जिससे न्यूनतम तापमान और गिर रहा है. हालांकि, दिन में धूप निकलने से थोड़ी राहत जरूर मिल रही है.
मौसम विभाग ने 30 नवंबर तक दोनों केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में मौसम मुख्य रूप से शुष्क रहने का अनुमान जताया है. इसका मतलब है कि आने वाले दिनों में सूखी ठंड और बढ़ सकती है.

title: दवाओं का ये कैसा खेल, 324 सैंपल क्वॉलिटी टेस्ट में फेल! असम में मिलीं नकली गोलियां
description: CDSCO की जांच में अक्टूबर 2026 में पूरे देश में जांच की गई और करीब 324 दवाओं के सैंपल क्वॉलिटी स्टैंडर्ड पर खरे नहीं उतरे. करीब 37 सैंपल केंद्रीय लैब और 287 सैंपल राज्य की लैब में NSQ पाए गए, जबकि असम में नकली दवा का एक मामला भी सामने आया.
author: रचित कुमार
content:
नकली और घटिया क्वालिटी दवाओं के खिलाफ देशभर में एक्शन जारी है. अक्टूबर के महीने में भी बड़ी संख्या में दवाएं जांच में फेल हो गईं. पिछले महीने देशभर में 324 दवाओं के सैंपल क्वॉलिटी जांच में फेल पाए गए. केंद्रीय औषधि मानक नियंत्रण संगठन यानी CDSCO की रिपोर्ट में 37 दवाओं को सेंट्रल लैब की जांच में नॉट ऑफ स्टैंडर्ड क्वॉलिटी (NSQ) घोषित किया गया है. ड्रग टेस्टिंग लैब में 287 दवाएं NSQ पाई गईं. असम में नकली दवा का 1 मामला सामने आया. यहां दूसरी कंपनी के ब्रांड नाम का इस्तेमाल कर अवैध निर्माता ने नकली दवाई बनाई थी. इस मामले में CDSCO और राज्य के ड्रग रेग्युलेटर जांच कर रहे हैं और दोषियों पर कानून के तहत कार्रवाई होगी.
गौरतलब है कि NSQ का मतलब जांचे गए खास बैच का गुणवत्ता मानकों पर फेल होना है, पूरे ब्रांड की सभी दवाएं खराब होना नहीं.
रेगुलेटर के मुताबिक, संबंधित बैच की पहचान कर बाजार से हटाने की कार्रवाई की जा रही है. CDSCO ने एक बयान में कहा, निगरानी गतिविधि के तहत, NSQ और नकली दवाओं की लिस्ट हर महीने CDSCO पोर्टल पर मुहैया कराई जाती है. अक्टूबर-2026 के लिए, सेंट्रल ड्रग लैब ने 37 दवा नमूनों को NSQ के तौर पर पहचाना है, जबकि स्टेट ड्रग्स टेस्टिंग लैब ने 287 दवा नमूनों को NSQ माना है. किसी दवा नमूने को NSQ तब माना जाता है, जब वह तय क्वॉलिटी स्टैंडर्ड में से किसी एक या ज्यादा में फेल हो जाता है. यह नाकामी सिर्फ सरकारी लैब के जांचे गए उस खास बैच की दवाओं तक ही सीमित है. इसका मतलब यह नहीं है कि बाजार में मौजूद अन्य दवाओं को लेकर भी कोई चिंता होनी चाहिए.
इसके अलावा, असम की स्टेट ड्रग्स अथॉरिटी से मिले 1 दवा नमूने को 'नकली' दवा के रूप में पहचाना गया है. इसे किसी अवैध निर्माता ने किसी अन्य कंपनी के ब्रांड नाम का उपयोग करके बनाया गया था. इस मामले की जांच चल रही है और कानून व नियमों के मुताबिक उचित कार्रवाई की जाएगी.
NSQ और नकली दवाओं की पहचान करने की यह प्रक्रिया राज्य नियामकों के सहयोग से नियमित रूप से की जाती है, ताकि ऐसी दवाओं की पहचान करके उन्हें बाजार से हटाया जा सके.
दरअसल, लैब में दवाओं के सैंपल की जांच की जाती है. यहां घुलनशीलता, सॉल्ट या एक्टिव इंग्रेडिएंट की मात्रा, वजन और शुद्धता के आधार पर जांच होती है. अगर मानक कम पाया जाता है, तो उसको NSQ घोषित किया जाता है. लेकिन आप घर में भी दवाओं की जांच कर सकते हैं. इसकी पहचान, दवा की पैकेजिंग, उसके असर और लक्षणों से की जा सकती है. इसके अलावा, इन्फेक्शन, शुगर, ब्लड प्रेशर की दवा लेने के बावजूद भी अगर परेशानी कंट्रोल में ना आ रही हो, तो भी वह NSQ दवा हो सकती है.

title: AAP Sarpanch’s Husband Shot in Punjab's Tarn Taran Amid Drug Feud; Wife Alleges Delayed Police Response
description: The victim, Sukhbir Singh, is the husband of Manjit Kaur, the sitting AAP sarpanch of Nawan Pind Daleke village under the Khadoor Sahib constituency.
author: Namya Kapur
content:
AAP Sarpanch’s Husband Shot in Punjab's Tarn Taran Amid Drug Feud; Wife Alleges Delayed Police Response
The victim, Sukhbir Singh, is the husband of Manjit Kaur, the sitting AAP sarpanch of Nawan Pind Daleke village under the Khadoor Sahib constituency.
- India News
- 2 min read
Tarn Taran: In a daylight attack linked to local anti-drug efforts, motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire on the husband of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) village sarpanch in Punjab’s Tarn Taran district, leaving him critically injured.
The victim, Sukhbir Singh, is the husband of Manjit Kaur, the sitting AAP sarpanch of Nawan Pind Daleke village under the Khadoor Sahib constituency.
According to police officials, the incident took place near the Daleke village turn while Sukhbir Singh and his wife were travelling together on a motorcycle from their village toward Tarn Taran.
Recounting the sequence of events, Manjit Kaur stated that the assailants intercepted them mid-route.
Advertisement
The attackers first rammed their motorcycle into the couple's two-wheeler to force them to a halt before opening indiscriminate fire.
Sukhbir Singh sustained gunshot wounds in the ambush, while the attackers fled the scene immediately afterwards.
Advertisement
Residents and police shifted the injured man to the Tarn Taran Civil Hospital, where he is currently undergoing treatment.
Preliminary police investigations indicate that the shooting stemmed from a feud over illegal drug peddling in the area.
Sadar police have identified the two prime suspects as brothers Mangal Singh and Udam Singh, alias Uday, both residents of Palasaur Kalan village.
Investigators noted that the accused suspected Sukhbir Singh of tipping off law enforcement about another villager, Amritpal Singh, who was recently arrested by the police for alleged drug-selling activities.
Manjit Kaur confirmed that her family had been actively opposing local drug smugglers in the village, which triggered the retaliatory strike.
She also raised concerns over law enforcement's response time, alleging that police personnel arrived at the scene significantly late, allowing the perpetrators to escape without resistance.
Following the incident, Sadar police registered a First Information Report (FIR) against the two accused brothers under Sections 109 (attempt to murder), 304, 324(4), and 351(B) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), alongside Sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act.
Senior police officials stated that the crime scene has been examined and dedicated teams are conducting raids to apprehend the absconding suspects.

title: Congress Signals Unwillingness to Compromise on Less Than 120 Seats During Talks with SP: Sources
description: The development indicates differences between the two alliance partners over the allocation of constituencies as they work towards finalising their seat-sharing arrangement.
author: Asian News International
content:
Congress Signals Unwillingness to Compromise on Less Than 120 Seats During Talks with SP: Sources
The development indicates differences between the two alliance partners over the allocation of constituencies as they work towards finalising their seat-sharing arrangement.
- India News
- 2 min read
New Delhi: The Congress has sought 120 seats in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections during seat-sharing discussions with the Samajwadi Party (SP) and is unwilling to accept a lower number, according to top sources in the Congress party. The demand was conveyed during a meeting between leaders of the two parties in Delhi, where the Congress submitted a list of 120 constituencies it wants to contest, sources said.
According to Congress sources, the party has also sought two seats in Saharanpur, where the Samajwadi Party has subsequently announced its candidates. The development indicates differences between the two alliance partners over the allocation of constituencies as they work towards finalising their seat-sharing arrangement.
Sources further said that the Congress has made it clear that it would not agree to contest fewer than 120 seats, maintaining its position during the negotiations. The Congress's proposed list reportedly includes several constituencies in Rae Bareli and Amethi districts, even though the Samajwadi Party has sitting MLAs in some of those seats. The inclusion of these constituencies in the Congress's demand could add another point of discussion between the two parties during the seat-sharing negotiations.
Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has emphasised that the selection of candidates should be guided by electoral considerations and the ability to defeat the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the state Assembly elections. In a lengthy post on X, Yadav underlined the need for mutual understanding between the alliance partners and said that the winning factor should be given importance while deciding the final candidates.
Advertisement
He also stressed that there should be a consensus candidate on every seat, representing the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework, to take on the ruling BJP.

Jalandhar: A man died after allegedly sustaining multiple injuries from a sharp-edged weapon during a fight in a neighbourhood in Jalandhar, police said on Wednesday. ACP Central Onkar Singh Brar said the police received information about a fight in the neighbourhood, following which the injured man was taken to Civil Hospital by his family. However, doctors declared him dead a few minutes after his arrival.
Speaking to the reporters, Brar said, “Our police team received information that a fight had broken out in the neighbourhood...the injured person was immediately taken by his family to the Civil Hospital. A few minutes later, doctors declared him dead. Based on the preliminary investigation, it appears he sustained multiple injuries inflicted by a sharp-edged weapon.”

Brar further said that, according to verbal accounts, the two groups had a longstanding dispute. Police teams are currently working to apprehend those involved in the incident. "According to verbal accounts, there was a long-standing dispute between the two groups. Our police teams are currently on the ground to apprehend them, and they will be arrested soon. It is being reported that there were three or four individuals," he said. Further investigation into the incident is underway.

title: What are western disturbances? Could they predict North India’s pollution levels?
description: Seasonal weather patterns influence how pollution builds up and disperses across the Indo-Gangetic Plain. New research suggests that western disturbances could help predict winter pollution severity months in advance
author: Sneha Mahale
content:
What are western disturbances? Could they predict North India’s pollution levels?
Seasonal weather patterns influence how pollution builds up and disperses across the Indo-Gangetic Plain. New research suggests that western disturbances could help predict winter pollution severity months in advance
Winter conditions are strengthening across northern India, with temperatures falling and fog expected in several states. Emissions from vehicles, industries, construction, waste burning, and agricultural fires contribute to the pollution load across North India. But meteorological conditions also play an important role in determining how much of it accumulates near the ground.
Weak winds, low temperatures and a shallow atmospheric boundary layer limit the dispersal of pollutants. A 2020 study published in Scientific Reports, using the WRF-Chem atmospheric chemistry model, found that the ventilation coefficient across the Indo-Gangetic Plain was about four times lower in winter than in the post-monsoon season.
Fog is another feature of North Indian winters. A 2022 study of 69 sites across India found that radiation fog accounted for 68.1 per cent of all fog events and 70 per cent of dense fog events. Radiation fog forms when the ground cools overnight, lowering the temperature of the air above it until water vapour condenses into tiny droplets. Delhi, Lucknow and Patna also recorded significant increases in fog frequency. Fog often coincides with high pollution because both are favoured by humid conditions and weak winds. However, fog itself is not an indicator of PM2.5 levels.
Larger weather systems also influence rainfall and wind patterns across northern India. One such system, the western disturbance, could help predict how severe winter pollution is likely to be.
How western disturbances affect pollution
Western disturbances (WDs) are weather systems that originate around the Mediterranean region and move eastwards towards northern India. They bring winter rain and snowfall to parts of the western Himalayas and influence wind patterns across the plains.
A 2026 study published in Science Advances examined the relationship between WDs and winter PM2.5 pollution across northern India. The researchers found that precipitation associated with strong western disturbances explained 74 per cent of the year-to-year variation in winter PM2.5 pollution across northern India, after accounting for long-term trends. The researchers also found that average winter PM2.5 concentrations were about 20 per cent higher during winters with below-average precipitation from western disturbances.
“Winter air pollution across the Indo-Gangetic Plain is often aggravated by weak winds and temperature inversions that trap pollutants near the surface. Western disturbances can interrupt these stagnant conditions by bringing stronger winds, precipitation, and improved atmospheric ventilation,” said researchers Yuanyu Xie, Mi Zhou and Denise L Mauzerall in a joint response.
The amount of rainfall and the strength of each system matter. The researchers analysed 177 WDs between 2015 and 2024. Strong, wet WDs produced PM2.5 reductions approximately 2.5 times greater than strong, dry WDs.
One example was a strong WD in January 2019. It brought rainfall and improved ventilation across northern India, reducing average PM2.5 concentrations by approximately 30 per cent over several days.
However, not every western disturbance improves air quality. “Our analysis shows that weak, dry disturbances often have little effect and can sometimes coincide with increases in PM2.5. Even strong storms may produce limited improvements if precipitation does not reach polluted areas or stagnant conditions persist. Therefore, forecasting the arrival of a WD alone is insufficient. We also need to predict its intensity, track, precipitation, and local meteorological impacts,” said the researchers.
How far ahead can we predict pollution?
WD activity is influenced by the subtropical jet stream, which is linked to sea surface temperature anomalies in the North Atlantic and tropical Indian Ocean during the preceding autumn. “These oceanic signals provide an opportunity to anticipate whether the coming winter will be relatively more or less polluted,” said the researchers.
The authors tested whether these signals could help predict winter pollution severity one season ahead. “Our study demonstrates the potential to predict winter pollution severity approximately one season in advance, using sea surface temperature anomalies from September-November to anticipate pollution conditions during December-February,” said the researchers.
The researchers caution that the prediction model has some limitations. PM2.5 monitoring data are available for only about a decade, making it difficult to test how well the model works under different climate conditions.
Pollution levels also depend on local emissions, temperature inversions, the movement of pollutants between regions, and other weather conditions. Seasonal forecasts cannot account for all these factors. The relationship between ocean temperatures, weather patterns and pollution could also change as the climate changes.
Forecasts of individual western disturbances could help with shorter-term air quality predictions. Dr Akshay Deoras, senior research scientist at the National Centre for Atmospheric Science and the Department of Meteorology, University of Reading, says, “Air quality forecasting has advanced considerably in recent years, with sophisticated modelling systems now capable of tracking pollution and predicting changes in air quality at relatively local scales.”
Indian forecasting systems generally provide air quality forecasts three to 10 days ahead, although accuracy tends to decline with lead time. These models also incorporate observations of aerosols, emissions and fire activity to improve their predictions, Deoras says. He explains how weather affects pollution levels: “Rainfall, in particular, washes out pollutants through a process known as atmospheric scavenging, whilst stronger winds help disperse accumulated pollutants.”
The impact also depends on the strength and path of a WD. “If the system is weak or does not penetrate sufficiently far south, the associated rainfall may be limited, and wind speeds may not increase significantly,” he says.
Seasonal forecasts could give authorities more time to prepare for a potentially severe pollution winter. Shorter-range forecasts could help anticipate changes in air quality over the coming days. Both could improve planning, but controlling emissions from vehicles, industries, construction, and other sources remains essential to reducing pollution.
Sneha Mahale is a Mumbai-based journalist and editor who covers climate change, wildlife, health, and culture. She specialises in long-form features and reported essays, that connect policy, people, and place.

title: Delhi knife attack: Who is Nabeel, the man who stabbed 9 cops inside Jama Masjid police station
description: The accused, identified as Nabeel, allegedly attacked five policemen inside the station before fleeing on a stolen two-wheeler. He was later traced to Chitli Qabar, where four more officers were injured before police shot him in both legs
author: FP News Desk
content:
Delhi knife attack: Who is Nabeel, the man who stabbed 9 cops inside Jama Masjid police station
The accused, identified as Nabeel, allegedly attacked five policemen inside the station before fleeing on a stolen two-wheeler. He was later traced to Chitli Qabar, where four more officers were injured before police shot him in both legs
Nine Delhi Police personnel were injured after a man allegedly attacked officers with a knife inside the Jama Masjid police station in Old Delhi on Monday afternoon. The suspect, identified as Nabeel, was later caught after a police operation in the nearby Chitli Qabar area, where he allegedly attacked officers again.
Police, as per news agency PTI, opened fire during the confrontation, shooting him in both legs before taking him into custody, according to the account provided by officials. He was taken to Lok Nayak Hospital (LNJP) for treatment.
The incident began around 2.30 pm when Nabeel visited the police station in connection with a family dispute. During the interaction, he allegedly pulled out a knife and attacked officers inside the premises, injuring five of them.
He then fled the police station, allegedly stopping a commuter at knifepoint and taking his two-wheeler to escape through the crowded streets of Old Delhi.
Police trace suspect to Chitli Qabar
A police team launched a search operation after the attack and tracked Nabeel to the Chitli Qabar area, where officers attempted to apprehend him around 4.30 pm.
However, police said he allegedly attacked the team with the knife again, injuring four more personnel from the Special Staff unit. Officers then opened fire, saying they had to defend themselves and bring him under control.
According to Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh, the team fired eight rounds, six of which hit Nabeel in both legs. He was subsequently taken to hospital for treatment.
Nine policemen injured, suspect has previous case
Of the nine injured personnel, five were taken to Sir Ganga Ram Hospital after the initial attack at the police station. Nabeel was admitted to Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, where he was being treated for his gunshot wounds.
Police said Nabeel, a resident of the Kala Mahal area near Jama Masjid, had a previous criminal case registered against him at Daryaganj police station in 2022 under Section 324 of the Indian Penal Code, which dealt with voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons.
DCP Singh said three cases were being registered in connection with the incident: the attack on police personnel inside the station, the alleged theft of the two-wheeler during his escape, and the subsequent assault on officers in Chitli Qabar.
Police have said Nabeel appeared to be mentally stable, although he was aggressive. His motive for the attacks has not yet been established, and investigators are looking into the circumstances surrounding the incident.

title: Re-imaging partnership: India rolls out $1.62-bn package for Nepal, focuses on energy, trade and connectivi...
description: A joint vision document released by the two countries said all outstanding matters, including those related to water resources, energy, trade and commerce, and boundaries, would be resolved through mutual discussion and dialogue
author: Snehesh Alex Philip
content:
Re-imaging partnership: India rolls out $1.62-bn package for Nepal, focuses on energy, trade and connectivity
A joint vision document released by the two countries said all outstanding matters, including those related to water resources, energy, trade and commerce, and boundaries, would be resolved through mutual discussion and dialogue
India and Nepal on Monday vowed to reimagine their partnership, unveiling an ambitious roadmap for cooperation as Prime Minister Narendra Modi rolled out the red carpet for his visiting Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, and announced a $1.62-billion financial assistance package for the Himalayan nation.
Describing India's support for Nepal's development journey as unwavering, Modi announced development assistance worth ₹15,000 crore (NPR 24,000 crore).
The package includes grant assistance of ₹3,500 crore (NPR 5,600 crore) for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure projects, along with a rupee-denominated Line of Credit worth ₹11,500 crore (NPR 18,400 crore) for energy-sector projects.
Specific projects and the modalities for extending the assistance will be finalised through mutual consultations.
A joint vision document titled Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal said the two leaders agreed that the bilateral partnership should reflect contemporary political, economic and technological realities.
It also called for an updated and forward-looking legal framework under which existing bilateral agreements, including the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, could be reviewed on the basis of mutual consent.
The document said all outstanding matters, including those related to water resources, energy, trade and commerce, and boundaries, would be resolved through mutual discussion and dialogue.
The two sides also decided to activate the High-Level Monitoring Group, led by Nepal's Foreign Secretary and India's Ambassador to Nepal. The group will meet at least once every six months to ensure the speedy implementation of proposed projects, ideas and initiatives, and facilitate the necessary clearances and approvals.
The monitoring group will submit its reports to the India-Nepal Joint Commission, co-chaired by the foreign ministers of both countries. The two leaders also decided that the next meeting of the Joint Commission would be held in 2027.
Connectivity gets a push
In a significant boost to Nepal's transit connectivity, Modi announced access to Deendayal Port at Kandla in Gujarat for Nepal's transit trade. Access to Paradip Port in Odisha will also be made available once the necessary infrastructure is in place.
Connectivity emerged as a major pillar of the discussions, with both leaders agreeing to strengthen cross-border infrastructure through new railway lines, bridges, Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) and petroleum pipelines.
The two prime ministers also flagged off the inaugural Sarayu-Kamala Express rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur. The service is expected to boost religious and cultural tourism along the Ramayana Circuit while strengthening the civilisational ties between the two countries.
They also agreed to explore similar connectivity initiatives to promote Buddhist and Shiv-Shakti religious tourism circuits.
In another major railway-related development, the two sides finalised the Field Location Survey for the proposed Raxaul-Kathmandu electrified broad-gauge railway line. India and Nepal will also collaborate in developing Nepal's East-West Railway.
Both leaders virtually laid the foundation stone for a new Integrated Check Post at Banbasa and welcomed progress in the construction of ICPs at Bhairahawa, Sunauli and Dodhara-Chandani. Three ICPs along the India-Nepal border are already operational.
A new cross-border motorable bridge connecting Dharchula in India with Darchula in Nepal was also inaugurated, providing a direct connectivity link between western Nepal and India.
Energy and petroleum connectivity
Expanding cross-border energy infrastructure was another key focus of the discussions.
The two leaders dedicated Phase II of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj petroleum pipeline to the people of Nepal.
They also virtually laid the foundation stone for a petroleum terminal at Jhapa in Nepal and stressed the need to begin work on the Siliguri-Jhapa petroleum pipeline at the earliest. Both sides agreed to explore cooperation in developing gas pipelines between the two countries.
The prime ministers also reviewed progress in the hydropower sector in line with the India-Nepal Joint Vision Document for Power Sector Cooperation and the Long-Term Power Trade Agreement.
Welcoming the active participation of Indian companies in Nepal's hydropower sector, both sides agreed to expedite the completion of projects being developed by Indian firms.
The two leaders virtually laid the foundation stone for the 669-MW Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project.
They also directed the Pancheshwar Development Authority and the Joint Committee on Water Resources to expedite the finalisation of the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project and begin its implementation.
Both sides further agreed to accelerate work on the DPRs of the Saptakoshi and Sunkoshi multipurpose projects, which aim to harness water resources for mutual benefit and mitigate the impact of floods.
The two countries also welcomed progress towards the formation of joint ventures for two high-capacity cross-border transmission lines connecting Inaruwa in Nepal with New Purnea in India, and Dododhara in Nepal with Bareilly in India.
Education and technology cooperation
As part of an expansion of India's development and capacity-building assistance, the two leaders agreed that India would establish an offshore IIT campus in Nepal.
The proposed institution is expected to strengthen Nepal's higher education ecosystem and create employment opportunities.
Both leaders also welcomed growing cooperation in technology, including start-ups and digital and financial connectivity, underlining the importance of expanding the partnership beyond traditional areas of cooperation.

title: SC agrees to hear contempt plea against Tamil Nadu govt over Deepam row
description: The contempt plea urged initiation of action against the Tamil Nadu government for allegedly failing to comply with its directions on lighting of the lamp
author: Press Trust of India
content:
SC agrees to hear contempt plea against Tamil Nadu govt over Deepam row
The contempt plea urged initiation of action against the Tamil Nadu government for allegedly failing to comply with its directions on lighting of the lamp
Listen to This Article
The Supreme Court on Wednesday said it will hear the contempt plea and peruse the status report of the Tamil Nadu government over the issue of non-lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai district.
The contempt plea urged initiation of action against the Tamil Nadu government for allegedly failing to comply with its directions on lighting of the lamp.
The matter was mentioned before a bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi.
During the proceedings, the counsel for the state government informed the bench that he was required to file a status report detailing the developments in the matter and urged the bench to take it up, pointing out that the traditional lamp had, unfortunately, not been lit at Deepathoon.
A senior advocate, appearing for the petitioner seeking permission to light the lamp, termed the developments "most unfortunate".
Also Read
He submitted that the state government had informed the Madras High Court that prohibitory orders were in force and that customary practices did not permit the lighting of the lamp at the disputed location.
Alleging deliberate non-compliance with the Supreme Court's directions, the petitioner's counsel argued that the flame should have been carried to Deepathoon and the lamp lit there.
He also pointed out that the state government had repeatedly assured the high court, until the last moment, that it would comply with the court's directions.
The counsel urged the bench to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings against the authorities concerned, alleging that the state government had circumvented the apex court's directions.
He also referred to the review petition filed by the state government.
When the senior advocate indicated that the petitioners would move a contempt petition, the bench said, "File it, and then we will see." The latest developments follow the Tamil Nadu government's failure to implement the top court's November 21 order permitting the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp to be lit at Deepathoon, a stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill, on November 24 as a one-time measure.
The dispute centres on the traditional practice of lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop location and the state authorities' objections to implementing the direction, citing law-and-order restrictions and customary practices.

title: Delhi pollution: AQI stays above 200, forecast warns of no immediate relief
description: he capital's air quality remained in the poor category on Wednesday, with five locations recording very poor readings, while the IMD forecast no immediate improvement over the coming days
author: Barkha Mathur
content:
Delhi pollution: AQI stays above 200, forecast warns of no immediate relief
he capital's air quality remained in the poor category on Wednesday, with five locations recording very poor readings, while the IMD forecast no immediate improvement over the coming days
Listen to This Article
Delhi woke up to another morning of poor air quality on Wednesday, with the city's average Air Quality Index (AQI) at 228 at 7 am, compared with 242 at the same time on Tuesday, according to real-time data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
The marginal decline has done little to change the overall picture. Of the 59 monitoring stations in the capital, 56 had valid readings. Thirty-six recorded AQI levels above 200, including five where the readings crossed 300, placing them in the 'very poor' category.
Anand Vihar recorded the highest AQI at 336, followed by Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 332. North Campus, Delhi University, recorded 313, while Burari Crossing and IGNOU, Maidan Garhi, reported 305 and 302, respectively.
At the other end, Sri Aurobindo Marg recorded the lowest AQI at 140, followed by IMD Lodhi Road at 147 and Patparganj at 148. These locations were in the 'moderate' category. PM10 and PM2.5 were the prominent pollutants in the city's overall reading.
NCR cities continue to report poor air
Also Read
Air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR) remained uneven, with several cities recording readings in the poor category. Panchgaon in Haryana reported the highest AQI in the region at 294, followed by Gurugram at 280.
Meerut recorded an AQI of 248, followed by Ghaziabad at 240 and Bhiwadi at 236. Bahadurgarh and Dharuhera in Haryana reported readings of 231 and 229, respectively, while Delhi stood at 228.
Noida recorded an AQI of 215, while Bulandshahr and Greater Noida reported 211 and 209, respectively. Baghpat was at 206. Rohtak and Sonipat recorded readings of 199 and 190, respectively.
Among the better-performing cities in the region, Palwal recorded the lowest AQI at 86, followed by Panipat at 133, Bharatpur at 141 and Hapur at 142. Alwar and Faridabad reported readings of 145 and 155, respectively.
Khanna records India's highest AQI
Among the 283 cities with valid readings in the CPCB's 7 am dataset, Khanna in Punjab recorded the highest AQI at 323, followed by Jalandhar at 304 and Panchgaon in Haryana at 294.
Shamli in Uttar Pradesh reported an AQI of 282, followed by Gurugram at 280. Ballabgarh in Haryana and Anpara in Uttar Pradesh both recorded 255, while Ludhiana in Punjab reported 254. Mandideep in Madhya Pradesh recorded 253.
At the other end, Chikkaballapur in Karnataka recorded the lowest AQI at 19, followed by Madikeri in the same state at 24 and Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu at 28. Eloor in Kerala reported 30, while Koppal in Karnataka recorded 34.
Aizawl in Mizoram, which had featured among the cleanest cities in the previous day's list, recorded an AQI of 38 on Wednesday.
Stubble burning, Delhi vehicles add to PM2.5 load
The latest source-apportionment estimates for Delhi by the Air Quality Warning and Integrated Decision Support System for Emissions - Delhi (AIRWISE-Delhi) indicate that vehicular emissions accounted for 20.5 per cent of the estimated PM2.5 load, while stubble burning in the areas near Delhi contributed 2.3 per cent and waste burning add 1.9 per cent.
The India Meteorological Department's Air Quality Early Warning System has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to remain in the 'poor' category from November 24 to November 27. Its outlook for the subsequent six days indicates that conditions could remain between poor and very poor.

title: Zojila tunnel likely to be completed in next 6-8 months: Nitin Gadkari
description: Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari said around 70% of the Zojila tunnel work is complete, with the project expected to provide all-weather connectivity between Kashmir and Ladakh.
author: Press Trust of India
content:
Zojila tunnel likely to be completed in next 6-8 months: Nitin Gadkari
Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari said around 70% of the Zojila tunnel work is complete, with the project expected to provide all-weather connectivity between Kashmir and Ladakh.
Listen to This Article
Asia's longest tunnel project at Zojila, which will ensure all-weather connectivity between Srinagar and Ladakh, will be completed in 6-8 months, Road Transport and Highways minister Nitin Gadkari said on Tuesday.
 Addressing the 7th World Landslide Forum (WLF-7), Gadkari further said that building connectivity on fragile Himalayan terrain demands a careful balance between development and environmental protection.
 "As of now, about 70 per cent of the total work on the Zojila tunnel project has been completed. The project will be completed in the next 6-8 months," he said.
 Gadkari further said every project must be guided by a sound understanding of local geology, hydrology and slope stability, supported by modern technology and long-term monitoring.
 Asia's longest tunnel project at Zojila had achieved a breakthrough on June 9 with the completion of over 13 kms of excavation work.
Also Read
 The breakthrough has brought the decades-old dream of all-weather connectivity between the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh closer to reality.
 In tunnelling, a breakthrough refers to the moment when teams from both sides meet at a given point. The tunnel, 9.5 metre wide, 7.57 metre high, and 13.153 km long, is a horseshoe-shaped, single-tube, two-lane road tunnel built at an elevation of around 11,578 feet above sea level. The project cost is around Rs 6,500 crore.
 The geostrategically important tunnel on the Srinagar-Leh National Highway will provide year-round, weather-proof connectivity to Ladakh, and reduce the earlier 1-1.5 hours travel time to just a 15-minute drive, officials said.
 The tunnel from Baltal in the Ganderbal district of central Kashmir to Minimarg in Drass district of the Union Territory of Ladakh has an 18-km approach road.
 Megha Engineering and Infrastructure Limited (MEIL), the agency which is executing the project, used the New Austrian Tunnelling Method (NATM) to pierce through the Himalayas and navigate the fragile geology. The entire project is 31 km long, including the approach road and bridges, stretching from Sonmarg to Minimarg.
 Once operational, the tunnel would enhance both civilian and military mobility across the treacherous Zojila Pass that is usually rendered shut for traffic for three winter months due to heavy snowfall.

title: ₹8,852-crore holiday membership fraud: Why ED attached  ₹557-crore assets of 2 firms across Mumbai, Pune and Satara
description: The ED has provisionally attached properties worth  ₹556.72 crore in Mumbai, Pune and Satara in an alleged  ₹8,852-crore investment fraud involving two firms. The companies allegedly ran unregistered holiday membership schemes, routing funds through over 87 entities in a Ponzi-type operation.
author: Livemint
content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has provisionally attached immovable properties worth ₹556.72 crore across Mumbai, Pune and Satara in connection with an alleged ₹8,852-crore investment fraud involving two companies that collected money from the public through holiday membership and investment schemes promising attractive returns.
The attachment is part of the agency's money-laundering investigation into Royal Twinkle Star Club Limited (RTSCL), Citrus Check Inns Limited (CCIL) and their associated entities, Hindustan Times reported.
According to the ED, the companies allegedly mobilised funds between April 2008 and March 2017 by offering long-term holiday membership plans and investment schemes that promised monetary returns as well as holiday benefits.
The schemes were allegedly operated without obtaining the necessary registration from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
The ED's investigation found that RTSCL and CCIL collected approximately ₹8,852 crore from investors over the nine-year period. Of this, around ₹3,430 crore was repaid to investors, while ₹3,077 crore was allegedly distributed as commission to agents involved in bringing in investors.
Another ₹1,723 crore was transferred to associated entities through loans, advances and other financial transactions, according to the agency.
The ED has estimated the proceeds of crime at approximately ₹5,422 crore, Hindustan Times reported.
According to The Times of India, the agency has alleged that money collected from fresh investors was used to repay earlier investors, indicating a Ponzi-type fund circulation mechanism.
The investigation also uncovered an alleged network of more than 87 group companies, firms and associated entities controlled by promoter Om Prakash Goenka and his family members.
According to the ED, funds collected through the schemes were routed through these entities and subsequently deployed in real estate, hospitality and other businesses.
Commission agents allegedly played a significant role in mobilising funds from the public and facilitating investor enrolments, the agency said, as reported by The Times of India.
RTSCL, which is part of the Mirah Group of Companies, has been involved in business activities, including hotels and restaurants, since 2002, according to the Times of India report.
The company introduced time-sharing holiday membership schemes that offered customers different investment options, including refundable and non-refundable plans.
Under these arrangements, investors could use their contributions to avail themselves of holiday packages.
Alternatively, those who did not utilise the holiday benefits were promised repayment of their investment, along with an additional monetary benefit, within a specified period.
The ED alleges that the companies mobilised substantial public funds through these arrangements without securing the required SEBI registration.
The money-laundering investigation reportedly stems from an FIR registered at Mumbai's RAK Marg police station, which alleged that the companies collected substantial sums from investors through their holiday membership and investment schemes by promising attractive returns and holiday benefits.
The ED subsequently initiated its probe into the alleged diversion and laundering of funds collected from investors.

title: IIT Bombay's ceiling fan replacement drive: Why are hostel rooms getting wall-mounted fans?
description: Importantly, IIT Bombay has not officially confirmed that the fan replacement is a dedicated suicide-prevention initiative.
author: Ravi Hari
content:
Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay has begun replacing ceiling fans and fan rods in hostel rooms with wall-mounted fans as part of a campus-wide renovation and maintenance exercise. The move has drawn attention amid renewed concerns over student suicides at premier educational institutions.
The replacement drive has been initiated after a student died by suicide in July, but gained renewed attention following the death of 22-year-old BTech student Sahil Wakode in September.
The institute is installing wall-mounted fans across its hostels and other utility areas on campus. Images of wall-mounted fans arriving at the Powai campus as part of the renovation work have also circulated widely on social media.
While the timing has prompted questions about whether the move is intended to prevent student suicides, the institute has not officially defined the replacement exercise as a suicide-prevention measure.
Why is IIT Bombay replacing ceiling fans with wall-mounted fans?
The shift comes against the backdrop of repeated student suicide cases at premier educational institutions, including IIT Bombay. Ceiling fans and their supporting rods can potentially be used as ligature points in suicide attempts. Replacing them with wall-mounted alternatives is therefore being viewed as a possible physical-safety intervention in hostel rooms.
The move could reduce access to certain potential hanging points in student accommodation. However, it is not clear whether the institute has formally adopted the measure as part of a broader suicide-prevention policy.

title: Priyank Kharge pitches Mangaluru as Karnataka’s next growth hub
description: Karnataka's Minister Priyank Kharge called for increased investment in Mangaluru to foster economic growth and innovation. The government plans to develop growth centers by leveraging the strengths of various regions. Kharge emphasized the importance of partnering with educational institutions for skill development and improving job opportunities. Additional initiatives include the ELEVATE programme, which provides grants to startups and encourages innovation.
author: ET Bureau
content:
Speaking at the inauguration of Deloitte’s 27th office in India in Mangaluru, Kharge said Dakshina Kannada accounts for 5.3% of Karnataka’s GDP. Its talent pool, educational institutions and quality of life could drive the state’s next phase of growth, he added.
“Our objective through Beyond Bengaluru is to take opportunities to where talent already exists, rather than expecting talent to move to Bengaluru,” Kharge said, calling on industry to help build stronger regional economic ecosystems.
He said Deloitte’s decision to open an office in Mangaluru was the kind of industry participation the state wanted to encourage under its Beyond Bengaluru initiative.
Kharge said the government was seeking to develop multiple growth centres outside Bengaluru by tapping the economic strengths of individual regions. At the recent Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru, the government identified key growth opportunities and committed about Rs 6,000 crore for the region’s development.
He also highlighted the Local Economy Acceleration Programme (LEAP), aimed at attracting investment and generating jobs by building on local strengths.
Pointing to Mangaluru’s education ecosystem and talent base, Kharge urged companies such as Deloitte to partner with colleges and the government on skilling programmes. “Why should a student studying in Mangaluru not be equipped to work with a company like Deloitte?” he said.
The minister also suggested setting up a Centre of Excellence in Mangaluru, potentially in health sciences, given the region’s strong healthcare sector.
Kharge said developing regional cities had become increasingly important as Bengaluru faces mounting pressure from rapid growth and migration.
He also urged local entrepreneurs to tap Karnataka’s ELEVATE programme, which offers eligible startups equity-free grants of up to Rs 1 crore. The state’s regulatory sandbox, meanwhile, allows startups to test solutions to public-sector challenges with the government. Sixteen startups have enrolled so far, with the state aiming to raise participation to 100.
“The next phase of Karnataka’s growth must come from our regions,” Kharge said.

title: 'Hindus not infiltrators': Bengal CM Suvendu directs police to trace, send back illegal Bangladeshi Muslim immigrants
description: Adhikari told SP Manish Joshi that illegal Muslim immigrants from Bangladesh had no place in the state and must be sent back.
author: PTI
content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari addressing a meeting.
Credit: PTI Photo
Cooch Behar: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday directed the police to trace, "one by one", Muslim immigrants who had allegedly entered the Cooch Behar district illegally from Bangladesh and send them back, while describing Hindus fleeing the neighbouring country as refugees deserving shelter.
Addressing a programme during his visit to Cooch Behar for the Rash Mela, Adhikari told SP Manish Joshi that illegal Muslim immigrants from Bangladesh had no place in the state and must be sent back through the routes they had used to enter India.
"Illegal Muslim infiltrators from Bangladesh have to be identified and traced, one by one, in this district. They must be sent back through the same routes they used to enter. They have to be driven out," he said.
The chief minister said Hindus coming from Bangladesh should not be treated as infiltrators, as they had crossed the border to escape religious persecution and save their lives.
"Those Hindus who have come from across the border are not infiltrators. They are refugees. They have come here to protect their religion and save their lives. They must be given shelter," he said.
Adhikari, who also holds the Home portfolio, directed the state police and the Border Security Force (BSF) to work in close coordination to strengthen security along the international border.
He said the state government had provided the necessary land to the BSF for border infrastructure and fencing, and asserted that all forms of smuggling must be stopped once the fencing work was completed.
The chief minister also asked the police to crack down on what he described as illegal madrasas in border areas, besides taking action against ganja cultivation, circulation of fake currency and drug trafficking.

title: पहले विदेश यात्रा में आई रुकावट, अब पासपोर्ट में जन्मस्थान पर सवाल... सौरव दास से MEA ने मांगा जवाब
description: CJP के सह-संयोजक सौरव दास को चेन्नई के क्षेत्रीय पासपोर्ट कार्यालय ने नोटिस जारी किया है. उनसे सात दिन के अंदर अपने जन्मस्थान की जानकारी स्पष्ट करने को कहा गया है. विदेश मंत्रालय का कहना है कि जवाब मिलने तक उन्हें पासपोर्ट का इस्तेमाल न करने की सलाह दी गई है.
author: aajtak.in
content:
कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) के सह-संयोजक सौरव दास को पासपोर्ट के मामले में चेन्नई के क्षेत्रीय पासपोर्ट कार्यालय ने नोटिस जारी किया है. उनसे अपने जन्मस्थान के बारे में सात दिन के अंदर जवाब देने को कहा गया है. विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता रणधीर जायसवाल ने बुधवार को इसकी जानकारी दी. उन्होंने बताया कि सौरव दास को जवाब देने तक अपने पासपोर्ट का इस्तेमाल न करने की सलाह भी दी गई है.
रणधीर जायसवाल के मुताबिक, पासपोर्ट कार्यालय ने 23 नवंबर को यह नोटिस जारी किया था. यह कदम कानून लागू करने वाली एजेंसियों से मिली जानकारी के बाद उठाया गया. उन्होंने कहा कि पासपोर्ट के लिए आवेदन करते समय सही जानकारी देना जरूरी है. अगर किसी जानकारी को छिपाने या उसमें गड़बड़ी की बात सामने आती है, तो संबंधित व्यक्ति से जवाब मांगा जाता है.
जन्मस्थान की जानकारी पर मांगा गया जवाब
विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता ने बताया कि पासपोर्ट कार्यालय ने सौरव दास से उनके जन्मस्थान के बारे में स्पष्टीकरण मांगा है. उन्हें इसके लिए सात दिन का समय दिया गया है. जायसवाल ने कहा कि पासपोर्ट आवेदन में सही जानकारी देना जरूरी है. अगर किसी व्यक्ति की ओर से तथ्य छिपाने या गलत जानकारी देने की बात सामने आती है, तो पासपोर्ट कार्यालय नोटिस जारी कर सकता है. इस मामले में भी अधिकारियों को मिली जानकारी के आधार पर सौरव दास से जवाब मांगा गया है.
दरअसल, सौरव दास ने दावा किया था कि उन्हें दिल्ली एयरपोर्ट पर लंदन जाने वाली फ्लाइट में सवार होने से रोक दिया गया. उन्होंने बताया था कि वह रात 1 बजे की फ्लाइट से ब्रिटेन जाने वाले थे.
सौरव दास के मुताबिक, इमिग्रेशन अधिकारियों ने उन्हें बताया कि उनका पासपोर्ट फ्लैग किया गया है. वह ब्रिटेन में 'कॉकरोच मूवमेंट' पर एक पैनल चर्चा में हिस्सा लेने जा रहे थे. इस कार्यक्रम का आयोजन ऑक्सफोर्ड यूनिवर्सिटी स्टूडेंट्स यूनियन की ओर से किया गया था.
मोदी सरकार पर लगाए आरोप
सौरव दास ने सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफॉर्म X पर एक पोस्ट में अपनी यात्रा रोके जाने के लिए मोदी सरकार को जिम्मेदार ठहराया था. उन्होंने आरोप लगाया कि सरकार उन्हें विदेश में अपनी बात रखने से रोकना चाहती है.
उन्होंने दावा किया था कि उन्हें ऑक्सफोर्ड के अलावा कैम्ब्रिज, लंदन स्कूल ऑफ इकोनॉमिक्स (LSE) और एडिनबर्ग में भी बोलने के लिए बुलाया गया था. सौरव दास ने कहा कि इस घटना से उनका काम प्रभावित नहीं होगा और वह आगे भी विदेश यात्रा करेंगे.
CJP के संस्थापक अभिजीत दीपके ने भी इस मामले पर सरकार की आलोचना की थी. उन्होंने आरोप लगाया कि सत्ता में बैठे किसी व्यक्ति को सौरव दास का ऑक्सफोर्ड में बोलने का न्योता मिलना पसंद नहीं आया. सौरव दास ने कहा कि इस घटना से वह पीछे नहीं हटेंगे. उनका कहना है कि वह आगे भी अपना काम जारी रखेंगे और विदेश यात्रा करेंगे.

title: AAP के मंच पर धीरेंद्र शास्त्री आए नजर तो विजेता दहिया भड़के, 'थोड़ी भी शर्म अगर...'
description: बाबा बागेश्वर के कार्यक्रम में मनीष सिसोदिया के पहुंचने से विजेता दहिया भड़क गए हैं. उन्होंने कहा है कि क्या मान सरकार ने 5 साल में काम नहीं किया है जो इनका आशीर्वाद लेने आए हो.
author: दीक्षा छाबड़ा
content:
AAP के मंच पर धीरेंद्र शास्त्री आए नजर तो विजेता दहिया भड़के, 'थोड़ी भी शर्म अगर...'
बाबा बागेश्वर के कार्यक्रम में मनीष सिसोदिया के पहुंचने से विजेता दहिया भड़क गए हैं. उन्होंने कहा है कि क्या मान सरकार ने 5 साल में काम नहीं किया है जो इनका आशीर्वाद लेने आए हो.
कथावाचक बाबा बागेश्वर का पंजाब में कार्यक्रम हो रहा है. उनके इस कार्यक्रम में शामिल होने के लिए आम आदमी पार्टी के वरिष्ठ नेता मनीष सिसोदिया पहुंचे थे. ये कार्यक्रम आम आदमी पार्टी ने ही आयोजित किया था. इस कार्यक्रम में मनीष सिसोदिया के पहुंचने पर विजेता दहिया भड़के हैं. उन्होंने मनीष सिसोदिया को कहा ह कि आपको थोड़ी सी भी शर्म नहीं आती है क्या.
विजेता ने सोशल मीडिया पर एक वीडियो शेयर किया है और मनीष सिसोदिया को खरी-खोटी सुनाई है. उन्होंने कहा, ''मुझसे मत कहा करो विजेता राजनीति में आओ. मनीष सिसोदिया हूं क्या मैं जो अपना लेवल ऐसे गिरा दूंगा. ये देखो क्या लिखा है. मनीष सिसोदिया ने मान सरकार के लिए मांगा बाबा का आशीर्वाद. कौन से बाबा क्या- धीरेंद्र शास्त्री.''
5 साल में कोई काम नहीं किया?
''वो मनुवादी जो कहता है मैं जात-पात खत्म करने के पक्ष में नहीं हूं. वो जो नफरत फैलाता है, वो जो बुलडोजर चलाने की बात करता है. इतना अंधविश्वास और पाखंड फैलाते हैं. उससे मनीष सिसोदिया आशीर्वाद मांग रहे हैं क्यों 5 साल में कुछ भी काम नहीं किया है क्या आपकी सरकार ने? आज जो ये सब करना पड़ रहा है. थोड़ी सी भी शर्म आती है? अपना लेवल इतना कैसे गिरा देते हो.''

— Vijeta Dahiya (@VijetaDahiya) November 24, 2026
उन्होंने आगे कहा, ''बिलकिस बानो केस में जब 11 आरोपियों को गुजरात सरकार ने रिहा किया था. उसके बाद जब इनसे इस केस के बारे में पूछा गया तो मनीष सिसोदिया ने कहा था, हमे इससे कोई मतलब नहीं है. तो ऐसी जीत भी क्या ही जीत है. ये कोई जीतना है क्या. ऐसी जीत पर थूकता हूं मैं, ऐसी राजनीति पर. मुझे उम्मीद थी उन लोगों से कि ये लोग कुछ करेंगे लेकिन ये है इनकी नई राजनीति.''
बता दें पंजाब में 2027 में चुनाव होने वाले हैं. चुनाव से पहले पंजाब में पार्टियों ने प्रचार करना शुरू कर दिया है. आम आदमी पार्टी भी अपने प्रचार में लगी हुई है.
