title: India, China Held Talks in Eastern Sector Recently: MEA
description: "A meeting of the senior-most military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently; discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management and addressing outstanding issues along the LAC," Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.
author: Asian News International
content:
India, China Held Talks in Eastern Sector Recently: MEA
"A meeting of the senior-most military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently; discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management and addressing outstanding issues along the LAC," Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.
- India News
- 2 min read
New Delhi: India and China recently held a meeting of their senior-most military commanders in the eastern sector, with discussions centred on border management and addressing outstanding issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) announced on Wednesday.
Speaking at the weekly media briefing in New Delhi, MEA official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal noted that New Delhi and Beijing maintain regular engagement through diplomatic and military mechanisms.
"India and China engage regularly through diplomatic and military mechanisms. A meeting of the senior-most military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently; discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management and addressing outstanding issues along the LAC. Such interactions are aimed at maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas and preventing any escalations," Jaiswal said.
Previously, on October 23, the MEA stated that both nations continue to rely on existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to settle outstanding issues and "avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control", while underlining that calm in the India-China border areas gets disturbed when Chinese troops depart from established patrolling patterns.
Advertisement
"As we have noted in the past, the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns. Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control," Jaiswal had remarked at that briefing.
He had further noted that both sides agreed to examine ways to improve understanding of the LAC in relevant areas to achieve better border management.
Advertisement
"I would also like to emphasise that the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations," he had stated.
Earlier, on September 8, the MEA reported that the first senior-most military commander-level flag meeting took place along the LAC at Wacha on the Indian side in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and at Damai on the Chinese side on September 7.
According to Jaiswal, those meetings followed understandings reached between the representatives of India and China and subsequent discussions held under the Working Mechanisms for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC).

title: 1,700 Indian nationals deported from US since start of 2026: MEA
description: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal says India verifies the nationality of individuals before accepting deportees, reiterating New Delhi’s cooperation with Washington on migration while opposing illegal immigration.
author: FP News Desk
content:
1,700 Indian nationals deported from US since start of 2026: MEA
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal says India verifies the nationality of individuals before accepting deportees, reiterating New Delhi’s cooperation with Washington on migration while opposing illegal immigration.
As many as 1,700 Indian nationals have been deported from the United States since the beginning of 2026, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday, underlining that India follows a nationality verification process before accepting individuals facing deportation.
Addressing a question on the latest deportation figures during the ministry’s bi-weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India continues to cooperate with Washington on migration and mobility-related matters but remains firmly opposed to illegal immigration.
He said the two countries maintain cooperation on deportations and that Indian authorities verify the nationality of individuals before agreeing to take them back.
"Where and when we receive information about a person to be deported, we verify his or her nationality and thereafter we agree to take him back," Jaiswal said.
Providing the latest figures, he added that 1,700 Indian nationals had been deported from the US since the beginning of the year.
The latest figure marks an increase from 1,273 Indian nationals deported from the US between January 1 and July 31, 2026, as shared by Jaiswal in July. At the time, the MEA spokesperson had also highlighted India’s due diligence process before facilitating the return of individuals facing deportation from foreign countries.
”We continue to work with several foreign governments on deportation issues. We do conduct due diligence on our side to confirm the nationality of the person concerned,” Jaiswal had said.
He had further clarified that arrangements for facilitating travel or return to India are undertaken only after the government is satisfied with the nationality of the individual concerned.
Providing the figures for the previous year during the July briefing, Jaiswal had said that a total of 3,567 Indian nationals were deported from the United States in 2025.

title: Gangajal from Triveni, Rudraksha from Pashupatinath: Decoding the Hindu symbolism behind Modi and Balen Sha...
description: During their New Delhi meeting, PM Narendra Modi gifted Nepalese counterpart Balen Shah a kalash of Gangajal from Triveni Sangam, receiving Rudraksha and Chandan from Kathmandu’s Pashupatinath Temple in return. Here is the spiritual significance behind the exchange and what it signals about India and Nepal’s shared Hindu heritage
author: FP Explainers
content:
Gangajal from Triveni, Rudraksha from Pashupatinath: Decoding the Hindu symbolism behind Modi and Balen Shah’s gift exchange
During their New Delhi meeting, PM Narendra Modi gifted Nepalese counterpart Balen Shah a kalash of Gangajal from Triveni Sangam, receiving Rudraksha and Chandan from Kathmandu’s Pashupatinath Temple in return. Here is the spiritual significance behind the exchange and what it signals about India and Nepal’s shared Hindu heritage
Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah made his first visit to India on Sunday (November 22). His Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, welcomed him in New Delhi, and the duo had a bilateral meeting at the Hyderabad House, where the Indian prime minister presented some religious gifts to him.
PM Modi gave a kalash of Gangajal from Triveni Sangam to the Nepali PM. In return, Shah gifted PM Modi a Rudraksha garland and Chandan (sandalwood) from the Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu.
Here we have more about the bilateral meeting and Shah's India visit.
Balen Shah's 1st visit to New Delhi as PM
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah exchanged religious gifts on Sunday (November 23), ahead of their bilateral talks at Hyderabad House in New Delhi.
PM Modi presented Shah with a kalash of Gangajal from Triveni Sangam, while Shah gifted Modi a Rudraksha garland and Chandan (sandalwood) from the Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu. The exchange took place as the two leaders met to review India-Nepal relations and discuss ways to strengthen cooperation.
According to the Times of India report, the discussions were expected to cover economic cooperation, trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development.
The gifts carried religious and cultural significance, with each leader choosing items associated with an important Hindu pilgrimage site in his country.
Why PM Modi chose Gangajal from Triveni Sangam
PM Modi gifted Shah a kalash (auspicious pot) of Gangajal brought from Triveni. The gift was significant because Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, is considered one of Hinduism’s holiest pilgrimage sites.
It is the confluence of three sacred rivers: the Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati.
In Hindu religious tradition, the Ganga is revered not merely as a river but also as a goddess. Its water, known as Gangajal, is regarded as sacred and is used in religious ceremonies and rituals. The water is traditionally associated with spiritual purification and the removal of ritual impurity.
The significance of Gangajal also comes from the religious importance attached to the Ganga in Hindu mythology. The river is worshipped as a divine mother, and its water holds a central place in Hindu practices, including prayers, offerings and purification rituals.
Gifting Gangajal therefore carries a religious meaning beyond the material value of the water.
The choice of water from Triveni also connected the gift to an important Hindu pilgrimage destination in India. The Sangam attracts pilgrims throughout the year, with particularly large gatherings during the Kumbh and Ardh Kumbh festivals.
Pashupatinath’s Rudraksha and Hinduism
Rudraksha beads are closely associated with Lord Shiva in Hindu religious traditions. The word is derived from two Sanskrit terms: Rudra, another name for Shiva, and Aksha, meaning eyes or tears.
According to religious belief described in the Shiva Purana, Rudraksha originated from the tears shed by Lord Shiva. The beads are consequently regarded as sacred and are worn by devotees as a symbol of their devotion to Shiva.
Rudraksha beads are traditionally worn by devotees and ascetics and are associated with spiritual well-being and devotion. Drik Panchang notes that the significance of Rudraksha is described in the Shiva Mahapurana and the Shrimad Devi Bhagavata Purana.
Its religious association with Shiva makes it an important object in Hindu worship and spiritual practices.
The Rudraksha and Chandan presented by Shah were brought from the Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu, Nepal. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, the temple is situated on the banks of the Bagmati River and is regarded as Nepal’s most revered Hindu temple.
The deity is worshipped there in the form of a Shiva Lingam.
The temple is an important pilgrimage destination for Hindus from Nepal, India and other parts of the world. Maha Shivaratri is its most significant annual festival, when devotees, pilgrims and ascetics gather to worship Lord Shiva.
The temple complex is also part of the Kathmandu Valley UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1979.
But what's the significance of sandalwood? Sandalwood, commonly called Chandan in Hindu religious practices, is associated with worship and auspiciousness. Sandalwood paste is traditionally used in religious rituals and applied as a tilak on the forehead. Its inclusion alongside Rudraksha made the gift a collection of religious offerings associated with Pashupatinath.
But the reports on the November 23 exchange do not specify the particular ritual significance or form of the sandalwood presented by Shah.
India, Nepal’s shared Hindu heritage
One of the strongest cultural links between India and Nepal comes from the Ramayana.
Janakpur in Nepal is traditionally identified as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, while Ayodhya in India is associated with Lord Ram.
Sita’s marriage to Ram connects the two places through one of Hinduism’s most important epics. Janakpur is home to the Janaki Mandir, an important pilgrimage destination dedicated to Goddess Sita.
Religious travel between India and Nepal is an established part of their cultural relationship. The Embassy of Nepal notes that thousands of Nepali citizens visit pilgrimage destinations in India every year. These include Haridwar, Rishikesh, Varanasi, Gaya and Vaishno Devi.
Similarly, Indian pilgrims visit Nepal’s Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu and the Ram-Janaki Temple in Janakpur.
The two countries have formalised their religious and cultural connections: India and Nepal have promoted cultural exchanges through sister-city arrangements between Varanasi and Kathmandu, Bodh Gaya and Lumbini, and Ayodhya and Janakpurdham.
In May 2018, the two countries launched the India-Nepal Ramayana Circuit to promote religious tourism. India also offered a grant of Rs 100 crore for the development of Janakpur and its surrounding areas.
The cultural relationship also includes languages, literature, music, cinema and religious traditions. Hindi, Nepali, Maithili, Bhojpuri and Awadhi are among the languages shared across the two countries.
Both also use the Devanagari script for several languages, while Sanskrit forms the linguistic foundation of many of them.

title: 'Avoid official or sensitive work on WhatsApp': India issues cyber advisory, warns of account misuse
description: India’s home ministry has issued a cybersecurity advisory, cautioning people against using WhatsApp Web for official, confidential or sensitive work. It warned that an authenticated session could be misused to gain unauthorised access to a user's account
author: FP News Desk
content:
'Avoid official or sensitive work on WhatsApp': India issues cyber advisory, warns of account misuse
India’s home ministry has issued a cybersecurity advisory, cautioning people against using WhatsApp Web for official, confidential or sensitive work. It warned that an authenticated session could be misused to gain unauthorised access to a user's account
India has cautioned users against leaving WhatsApp Web sessions logged in on office and shared computers. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has issued a WhatsApp Web advisory, warning that compromised sessions could allow criminals to read messages, impersonate account holders and exploit trusted identities. The warning comes amid a series of cyber incidents targeting businesses and organisations worldwide.
The advisory, issued by the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) of the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), says a malicious actor gaining access to an authenticated WhatsApp Web session could read private messages, send messages while impersonating the account holder, access contacts and group conversations, and exploit the user's trusted identity for fraud, phishing and social engineering.
The warning specifically highlights the risks of using WhatsApp Web on office computers, shared systems, public computers and devices accessible to other people. The advisory also asks them not to remain permanently logged in and to manually log out after every session, warning that simply closing a browser tab or window does not amount to logging out.
The home ministry recommended using Incognito or Private Browsing mode when access is unavoidable, avoiding public or untrusted computers, and keeping operating systems, browsers and security software updated.
The advisory comes at a time when suspected cyberattacks have been reported from across Europe and the US in recent weeks, ranging from refrigeration systems to highly protected Pentagon and aviation systems of America.
In most cases, suspected attackers could not be identified, with agencies continuing to probe vulnerabilities and apply fixes to plug the technical loopholes. Cyber agencies worldwide have highlighted the mounting scale of cybersecurity challenge with the artificial intelligence technology reaching state and non-state actors alike when geopolitical order is undergoing a massive overhaul.
Dos and Do’ts in the advisory: What should WhatsApp users do?
The I4C advisory recommends a number of precautions, particularly for people accessing WhatsApp Web from computers used by multiple individuals.
Avoid sensitive work: Do not exchange confidential government, organisational or financial information through WhatsApp Web on computers.
Log out after every session: Manually log out instead of simply closing the browser tab or window.
Avoid public computers: Do not access WhatsApp Web through cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres or borrowed computers.
Use private browsing: If access is unavoidable, use Incognito or Private Browsing mode on a trusted computer and log out manually.
Check account activity: Watch out for unexpected messages, unusual replies from contacts and other unexplained activity.
Keep devices updated: Update operating systems, browsers and security software, and avoid suspicious downloads and unknown files.
Users should also periodically check the Linked Devices section in WhatsApp settings and log out of devices or sessions they do not recognise, the advisory said.
The I4C has separately advised organisations to verify urgent financial instructions received through WhatsApp or email through a direct voice call or in-person confirmation. Employees should never execute suspicious attachments, particularly files claiming to contain mandatory regulatory updates.
I4C had earlier warned of WhatsApp account takeover targeting executives
The November advisory follows two earlier warnings issued by the I4C in June and August 2026 about a campaign targeting senior executives, company directors, chartered accountants and corporate finance professionals.
In its June 22 advisory, the I4C described a cybercrime operation known as the 'Boss Scam' or CEO impersonation fraud.
According to the government, criminals impersonate regulatory authorities such as the Reserve Bank of India and send executives malicious compressed files through email or WhatsApp, often under the pretext of urgent regulatory compliance or a mandatory security update.
These files contain malicious Windows executable (.exe) and Dynamic Link Library (.dll) files. When extracted and executed on a computer, the malware can compromise the device and hijack active WhatsApp Web session tokens.
Once inside an executive's account, fraudsters can contact employees, particularly those in finance and accounts departments, and instruct them to transfer money to specified bank accounts.
In some cases, attackers may also manipulate the victim's contact list, saving their own number under the name of the CEO to make fraudulent instructions appear genuine.
The I4C's August 7 advisory reported a sharp rise in complaints involving WhatsApp account takeovers through malicious files disguised as account statements and regulatory communications. Similar incidents had been reported from Delhi, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.
The agency said it had alerted more than 58,000 potential victims through SMS notifications in the preceding 30 days. It also said more than 10,000 Indians had been protected from the campaign through the blocking of command-and-control servers.
The campaign illustrates how a seemingly routine document or message can become the starting point of a much larger corporate security breach.
WhatsApp Web and the threat of account takeover
WhatsApp Web allows users to access their WhatsApp accounts through a computer browser, linking the desktop session to their mobile account.
The convenience, however, can become a security vulnerability when users leave sessions authenticated on shared or inadequately protected devices.
A compromised session could give an attacker access to conversations and contacts without necessarily having to impersonate the user through a different phone number. Messages sent from the genuine account can appear legitimate to friends, colleagues and business associates.
This creates opportunities for fraudsters to exploit existing trust. An attacker could, for instance, impersonate a senior executive and send an urgent payment instruction to an employee, or circulate malicious files through groups and personal conversations.
The danger is not limited to someone physically accessing an unattended computer. Malware installed on a compromised computer can also be used to steal information and hijack active WhatsApp Web sessions.
India's growing cybersecurity challenge
The warnings also come against the backdrop of a significant increase in cyber incidents reported to India's national cybersecurity agency.
According to data shared by the Ministry of Home Affairs in Parliament in March 2026, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (Cert-In) tracked 29,44,248 cybersecurity incidents in 2025, compared with 20,41,360 in 2024 and 15,92,917 in 2023.
The figures cover reported and tracked cybersecurity incidents and should not be confused with the number of confirmed data breaches. Nevertheless, they indicate the scale of the challenge facing India's digital infrastructure.
Several recent incidents have also highlighted the vulnerability of major Indian organisations.
SBI: Nearly 3,900 customer records exposed
In October 2026, the State Bank of India reported a cyber incident involving 3,897 customer records that appeared on the dark web.
A Reuters report said that the exposed information included customers' names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, residential addresses, customer identifiers and loan records.
SBI engaged an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident. The bank said customer account balances remained safe and that the incident was not expected to materially affect its core operations.
Bank of Baroda: Employee email account compromised
In July 2026, Bank of Baroda confirmed a cybersecurity incident after information and internal documents allegedly linked to the bank appeared on the dark web.
The bank said the incident involved a compromised employee email account, resulting in unauthorised access to certain data. It initiated a forensic investigation and said it was working with the relevant authorities.
The incident underlined how the compromise of an individual employee's account can potentially expose information belonging to a much larger organisation.
Cyberattacks elsewhere: When digital disruption hits the real economy
The problem is not confined to India. Cyberattacks targeting major companies and their supply chains have demonstrated how a single point of compromise can disrupt operations across entire industries.
In August 2025, Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), the British luxury carmaker owned by India's Tata Motors, suffered a major cyberattack that forced it to halt production.
The disruption lasted almost six weeks before manufacturing began to resume.
A report by Britain's independent Cyber Monitoring Centre estimated that the incident cost the UK economy £1.9 billion ($2.55 billion) and affected more than 5,000 organisations, including suppliers and dealerships.
The incident demonstrated that cyberattacks can have consequences extending far beyond stolen information, disrupting manufacturing, employment and supply chains.
Marks & Spencer: Hackers exploited a third-party contractor
British retailer Marks & Spencer (M&S) also suffered a major cyberattack in 2025.
The company's chief executive said hackers had gained access by using social engineering to trick employees at a third-party contractor, rather than by directly breaking through the retailer's digital defences.
The attack disrupted online services and operations. An Associated Press report said the incident had cost M&S around £300 million, with its online services having been disrupted for about two months.
The case highlighted another major vulnerability: even organisations with substantial cybersecurity infrastructure can be exposed through their employees, contractors and external service providers.
The larger lesson is that digital security is no longer just about protecting passwords or avoiding suspicious links. An authenticated account, a trusted identity or an unattended computer can become an entry point for criminals.
As the I4C puts it in its advisory: "Stay Alert. Log Out After Every Session. Protect Your Digital Identity.”

title: SC examines duty-free shops' regulatory exemption in nicotine pouch case
description: The Supreme Court issued notice on a plea challenging a Bombay High Court ruling that goods sold at duty-free shops are not exempt from domestic regulatory requirements
author: Bhavini Mishra
content:
SC examines duty-free shops' regulatory exemption in nicotine pouch case
The Supreme Court issued notice on a plea challenging a Bombay High Court ruling that goods sold at duty-free shops are not exempt from domestic regulatory requirements
Listen to This Article
The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notice on a plea by Mumbai Travel Retail Private Limited challenging a Bombay High Court ruling that goods imported into India are not exempt from domestic regulatory laws merely because they are stored or sold at duty-free shops beyond the customs frontier.
A Bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M Pancholi issued notice after hearing senior advocate Shyam Divan, appearing for the company.
The dispute concerns restrictions imposed by authorities on the sale of tobacco-free nicotine pouches, marketed under the brands ZYN and FOX, at international departure duty-free outlets at Mumbai airport.
Divan argued that the High Court’s findings had implications extending beyond the products in question and could affect the entire duty-free retail industry.
He submitted that the ruling was contrary to the Supreme Court’s earlier judgments on the customs frontier and the point at which imported goods become part of the domestic market.
Also Read
Challenging the restrictions on the nicotine pouches, Divan said the High Court had accepted the company’s contention that there was no material to establish that the products were drugs.
However, it had declined to quash the communications restricting their sale and instead directed the company to approach the authorities with a representation.
He explained that the pouches are placed inside the mouth, allowing nicotine to be absorbed by the body. The products, he said, were sold in several countries and were not imported for domestic consumption in India.
On the legal position governing duty-free outlets, Divan submitted that goods stored in bonded warehouses for sale at such shops did not enter the domestic tariff area until they crossed the customs barrier. Relying on the Supreme Court’s judgments in Garden Silk Mills and Kiran Spinning Mills, he argued that import for domestic consumption was complete only when goods crossed the customs frontier and a bill of entry for home consumption was filed.
The Bench sought clarification on the distinction between goods entering India’s territorial waters and those crossing the customs barrier. Divan maintained that the two were legally distinct stages.
He also cited the Supreme Court’s ruling concerning duty-free shops operated by the India Tourism Development Corporation at Bengaluru airport, submitting that goods kept in bonded warehouses could not be treated as having crossed the customs frontier.
Divan cautioned that the High Court’s observations could have wider consequences for duty-free retailers, including the applicability of domestic laws governing metrology, packaging, standardised weights and food safety.
He further told the Bench that imports were broadly classified as free, restricted or prohibited, and that the nicotine pouches fell within the category of freely importable goods.
Their presence within airport premises, he argued, did not make them subject to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, while they remained in bonded warehouses outside the domestic tariff area.
The products are sold at duty-free outlets operated by Mumbai Travel Retail and Flemingo Dutyfree Shop Private Limited at Mumbai International Airport.
Authorities restricted their sale on the ground that they qualified as drugs under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and required an import licence and registration.
The Bombay High Court held that the exemption available to duty-free shops was confined to fiscal measures, such as customs duties and indirect taxes, and did not extend to regulatory requirements under public health and safety laws.
It held that goods entering India’s territorial waters remained subject to domestic regulatory laws even when stored or sold through duty-free shops.
However, it declined to determine conclusively whether the nicotine pouches qualified as drugs under Section 3(b) of the Act, observing that their classification would depend on their composition and intended use.

title: Centre plans time-bound disposal of arbitral challenges, decree execution
description: The proposed amendments to the existing legal framework seek to improve the enforceability and finality of arbitral awards and ensure the timely execution of decrees
author: Bhavini Mishra
content:
Centre plans time-bound disposal of arbitral challenges, decree execution
The proposed amendments to the existing legal framework seek to improve the enforceability and finality of arbitral awards and ensure the timely execution of decrees
Listen to This Article
The Centre is proposing further amendments to ensure that challenges to arbitral awards are resolved and decrees are executed within a stipulated timeframe, Rajiv Mani, secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice, said on Wednesday.
Speaking at the ICA-SCC Arbitration Institute Conclave in New Delhi, Mani said the proposed changes would build on the existing legal framework, including the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, and the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, to improve the enforceability and finality of arbitral awards.
“Besides the enactment of the Commercial Courts Act of 2015, we are also proposing to introduce further amendments so that the finality of an arbitral award, when challenged under the applicable law and the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, is resolved within a time-bound manner, and the execution of the decree takes place, of course, in a time-bound manner,” he said.
The remarks come as India and the European Union (EU) move towards operationalising their free trade agreement (FTA), which is expected to expand cross-border trade and investment.
The India-EU Investment Protection Agreement is also under negotiation, with an early conclusion in view, Mani said.
Also Read
He said a predictable dispute resolution framework would be particularly important for smaller enterprises, exporters and startups seeking to benefit from increased access to international markets. The government also wants arbitration to expand beyond metropolitan centres to Tier-II and Tier-III cities.
Mani said arbitration and mediation should be viewed as complementary mechanisms rather than competing alternatives. While arbitration provides a binding adjudication of disputes, mediation allows parties to reach mutually acceptable settlements while preserving commercial relationships.
He cited the Mediation Act, 2023, as an important addition to India’s dispute resolution framework and said multi-tiered dispute resolution clauses combining negotiation, mediation and arbitration could help parties resolve disagreements more efficiently.
Pre-institution mediation under the Commercial Courts Act also provides an opportunity to settle disputes before approaching courts, he added.
Welcoming the conclusion of negotiations on the India-EU FTA, Mani said the agreement could be signed soon, possibly within the year. He said stronger economic ties between the two sides would require a partnership built on trust and effective mechanisms to address commercial disputes.
India and the EU recorded merchandise trade of approximately $136.5 billion in 2024-25. The FTA is expected to provide preferential market access for around 99.5 per cent of Indian exports by trade value once it comes into force.
Arun Chawla, director general of the Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA), said the agreement could reduce the cost of doing business, while effective dispute resolution mechanisms would help lower the risks associated with cross-border transactions.
He said arbitral institutions needed to focus on credibility, efficiency and adaptability, particularly as commercial disputes increasingly involve emerging technologies, energy transition, infrastructure and intellectual property.
On the use of artificial intelligence in arbitration, he said technology should strengthen human judgement rather than compromise the independence and fairness of adjudication.
Petra Menander, Sweden’s ambassador to India, said bilateral trade between the two countries had expanded significantly over the past decade, with Sweden doubling its exports to India and India tripling its exports to Sweden. The two countries aim to double their economic exchange by 2030.
Caroline Falconer, secretary general of the SCC Arbitration Institute, said parties from more than 90 countries had used the Stockholm-based institution over the past decade. Indian parties featured in its caseload almost every year, primarily in disputes involving European companies. Most arbitrations administered by the institution conclude in approximately a year, she said.
The conclave, organised by the ICA and the SCC Arbitration Institute, also discussed the implications of changing trade, investment and technology trends for India-EU dispute resolution.

title: CII-backed Banaras Biennale to bring art and culture to Varanasi's ghats
description: The 35-day industry-backed event, with an investment of upwards of ₹20 crore, will showcase Varanasi's art, culture, textiles and living practices through exhibitions and workshops
author: Anushka Bhardwaj
content:
CII-backed Banaras Biennale to bring art and culture to Varanasi's ghats
The 35-day industry-backed event, with an investment of upwards of ₹20 crore, will showcase Varanasi's art, culture, textiles and living practices through exhibitions and workshops
Listen to This Article
Varanasi, India’s cultural and spiritual hub, is set to position itself as a global destination for art and culture with the debut edition of the ‘Banaras Biennale’. The 35-day event aims to celebrate the city’s art, culture, textiles and living practices. Backed by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), it will kick off on November 27 and will spread across the ghats, museums, universities and streets of Varanasi through exhibitions, cultural programmes, curated walkthroughs, training workshops and textile factory tours.
The Biennale will coincide with the second edition of the India Biennale, organised by the Ministry of Culture, taking place in Delhi from December 4. The Banaras Biennale is, however, an industry-backed initiative with an investment of upwards of ₹20 crore. “The event is entirely funded by the industry, with several industry partners joining in to make it a financial success,” says Madhav Singhania, steering committee chairman of CII Banaras Biennale 2026. Addressing a press conference in Delhi, he added that the first objective would be to create an institution out of the Biennale in the city of Kashi and then to expand it with every edition.
The event, themed ‘Kashi/light: The City as a Sensorium’, will kick off on Friday with a pre-dawn visit to the Kashi Vishwanath temple, followed by a walkthrough — Paani Mein Lakeere — with the lead visual art curator, Gayatri Sinha. The exhibitions, including the textile curation, Ek Dhaga, Ek Duniya: Silk, Zari and the Light of Kashi, and the photography walkthrough, My River, My Witness, will be open on all days during the Biennale. The event will open to the general public from November 28.
The aim, according to the organisers, is to reimagine the existing rich heritage of Banaras to establish it as a global destination. The peaceful riverfront experience will be enhanced by live music concerts bringing the city’s musical heritage to its ghats. The factory tours and artisan workshops will shift the focus to the making of famous Banarasi textiles, including saris and carpets. The walkthroughs across the ghats will also feature culinary demonstrations. Banaras Hindu University (BHU) will be a venue for multiple workshops, panel discussions and exhibitions.
The ghats of Banaras will be illuminated by another industry-backed event, the Mahindra Kabira Festival, from December 4 to 6. Organised by the Mahindra Group, the event will have its milestone 10th edition, spanning folk music, discussions, art demonstrations, boat rides, a food trail and heritage walks.

title: Delhi HC says senior citizens can evict children from own property without proving harassment, ill treatment
description: The Delhi High Court ruled in favour of a 85-year-old senior citizen who was seeking eviction of his son and daughter from his self-acquired property in South Delhi's Masjid Moth. The couple has been directed to vacate the house in four weeks time.
author: Sneha Biswas
content:
The Delhi High Court has ruled in favour of senior citizens who might not want to co-habit with their kids, for several reasons. Anyone 60 and above seeking to evict their children from self-acquired properties do not necessarily have to prove harassment or ill-treatment in order to do so, the court said. Justice Amit Mahajan held that establishing the need to protect the property and live a peaceful and dignified life can be sufficient reasons for eviction as per the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. The statement was made by the court while allowing an 85-year-old man's plea against orders passed by the District Magistrate and the Divisional Commissioner. The senior citizen moved court seeking eviction of his eldest son and daughter-in-law from his house in South Delhi's Masjid Moth, reported news agency PTI. The court directed the couple to vacate the property within four weeks. It also asked the concerned Station House Officer (SHO) to provide the senior citizen with necessary police assistance to ensure compliance, the news agency added. The court noted that the petitioner was the absolute owner of the property. However, the son and daughter-in-law had no ownership claims. Reportedly, they resided in the house solely because of their relationship with the 85-year-old. According to Live Law, the judgement was passed on November 20, 2026, in Subhash Chander Malhotra v. Raman Malhotra & Ors. Justice Mahajan held that the authorities had wrongly insisted that the senior citizen establish allegations of harassment through clear and cogent evidence before ordering the eviction. The court said that neither the 2007 Act nor the Delhi Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Rules, 2009, mention such a requirement. It observed that mistreatment cases involving elderly parents often take place within the confined walls of homes, which may make it difficult to report with evidence. The High Court also raised questions regarding two enquiry reports submitted by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM). The first report, filed on February 25, 2023, reportedly only stated that the harassment claims could not be verified. The second report, filed on September 17, 2025, also mentioned that harassment had not been established. However, the evidence or findings behind the conclusion remain missing in the reports. The court said a conclusion without supporting evidence cannot be treated as a finding. It also dismissed the authorities' reliance on a business dispute between the petitioner's sons as a reason to dismiss his grievance. HC relied on the Supreme Court's August 2026 ruling in Ravi Kant Gupta v. State of Uttar Pradesh, which recognised the power of Maintenance Tribunals to order eviction where necessary to protect senior citizens. It also referred to Pritam Singh v. Government of NCT of Delhi, which clarified that proof of ill-treatment is not always required for eviction. The petitioner had acquired the property from the Delhi Development Authority in 1980, which was later converted into freehold in 2000. According to PTI, the dispute arose years ago when the senior citizen approached the authorities in 2022. He had alleged that his son and daughter-in-law had refused to vacate despite being asked to. The District Magistrate rejected his plea in August 2023 and again in October 2025, which was also upheld by the Divisional Commissioner in April 2026. The senior citizen subsequently approached HC. title: What does  ₹1.25L monthly budget look like? ‘ ₹30,000 grocery,  ₹20,000 grooming’: Noida couple’s expenses go viral
description: A Noida couple has revealed that they spend around  ₹1.25 lakh every month despite owning a home and paying no rent. Groceries cost them  ₹30,000, while grooming and fitness add another  ₹35,000 to their monthly expenses.
author: Trisha Bhattacharya
content:
Owning a home does not always mean that monthly expenses are low. A couple living in Noida has revealed that they spend around ₹1.25 lakh every month, even though they own their house and do not have to pay rent. The couple shared a video on Instagram explaining their monthly expenses. Their spending includes groceries, household help, gym memberships, grooming, food and travel. The expense breakdown has started a discussion on social media, with many people questioning how a couple can spend so much every month without paying rent. According to the couple, groceries are their biggest monthly expense at ₹30,000. They also spend around ₹20,000 on grooming. Their gym memberships and Pilates classes cost another ₹15,000 every month. Supplements such as protein powder and multivitamins add ₹15,000 to their expenses. The couple said they spend around ₹30,000 on groceries every month and another ₹20,000 on grooming. Their gym and Pilates sessions cost ₹15,000, while supplements add another ₹15,000 to their monthly expenses. They also pay ₹10,000 for household help and spend another ₹10,000 on eating out. Home maintenance costs them ₹8,000, while electricity bills come to around ₹5,000. Internet, mobile and OTT subscriptions together cost ₹6,000. Their monthly commute expenses are between ₹5,000 and ₹6,000. Together, these expenses add up to around ₹1.25 lakh every month. The couple also spends ₹10,000 on household help, which includes cooking and cleaning. Their electricity bill is around ₹5,000, while home maintenance costs them another ₹8,000. They spend ₹6,000 on internet, mobile bills and OTT subscriptions. Travelling to work costs them between ₹5,000 and ₹6,000 every month. The couple also explained how much more they would have to spend if they did not own their home. According to them, renting a similar 3BHK flat in their area would cost around ₹45,000 to ₹50,000 every month. This could take their total monthly expenses from ₹1.25 lakh to nearly ₹1.75 lakh. Their video has received mixed reactions online. Some people questioned the ₹30,000 grocery budget, while others were surprised by the ₹20,000 spent on grooming. Some users also pointed out that spending ₹15,000 on gym memberships and another ₹15,000 on supplements was a personal choice rather than a necessary monthly expense. Others said that the couple's spending showed how expensive certain lifestyles can become in a city like Noida. The couple's video has also started a wider discussion about monthly expenses in Indian cities. Even without rent or home loan payments, costs such as food, fitness, personal care and household help can take up a large part of a family's income. title: Uber, Ola, Mega Cabs fares at Bengaluru Kempegowda airport getting costlier? Here’s what passengers, cab drivers said
description: Passengers and cab drivers at Bengaluru's Kempegowda airport allege ride-hailing platforms are restricting cab availability, pushing up fares despite idle taxis. Commuters report long queues and costly upgrades, while drivers cite two-to-three-hour waits amid declining passenger traffic.
author: Bhanu Pratap
content:
Passengers and cab drivers at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) have accused ride-hailing platforms of manipulating cab availability to push up fares, even as hundreds of taxis allegedly remain idle in airport parking areas, according to a report by Deccan Herald. The reported complaints come amid long passenger queues, failed bookings and extended waiting periods for drivers. Commuters have alleged that they are being pushed towards more expensive cab categories when their preferred rides are unavailable, while drivers say they often spend hours waiting for a single booking, as per the report. The situation has also been compounded by a reported decline in passenger traffic, particularly at the international terminal, which drivers have partly attributed to tensions in West Asia and disruptions to air travel. G Narayana Swamy, president of Karnataka Chalakara Okkuta, told Deccan Herald that hundreds of cabs could be seen parked in the airport's P7 parking zone even as passengers faced long queues at pickup points. He alleged that some authorised cab operators were deliberately restricting vehicle availability to drive up fares. Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL), which operates the airport, has nine authorised cab partners, including KSTDC, Mega Cabs, Uber, Uber Black, Ola, Quick Ride, OHM Electric Cabs and WTI, as per the report. Passengers have reported waiting between 40 and 60 minutes to secure a ride. Some said their initial bookings did not materialise, leaving them with the option of booking more expensive vehicle categories. A passenger travelling from Goa told Deccan Herald that she found at least 60 people waiting at the Uber kiosk when she arrived at around 7 PM last week. Quick Ride had only one pre-booked SUV available, while drivers at the Namma Yatri kiosk reportedly said that only SUVs could be arranged. The passenger said that after waiting for around 45 minutes, the driver assigned to her booking refused the trip because her destination was not close enough to the airport. She was travelling to Marathahalli. She also alleged that another driver demanded an additional fare, raising concerns over the availability of airport taxis and the enforcement of fare rules. Cab drivers have also raised concerns about declining passenger traffic and operational restrictions, saying these are affecting their earnings. According to the report, drivers said they sometimes wait between two and three hours for a single booking. They are required to remain in designated parking areas until their ride-hailing applications clear them to enter the passenger pickup zone. Drivers have particularly flagged weaker demand at the international terminal, which they partly attribute to tensions in West Asia and disruptions to flight operations. A premium cab operator at the airport said it deploys around 800 vehicles across both terminals, with the bulk of demand concentrated at Terminal 1. The operator told the daily that services generally run smoothly outside peak hours, but longer trip durations affect vehicle availability. title: Govt plans amendments to ensure time-bound resolution of challenges to arbitral awards
description: The government is proposing amendments to enhance the efficiency of the dispute-resolution process in India. Union Law Secretary Rajiv Mani highlighted the aim of ensuring timely resolution for challenges to arbitral awards. The introduction of additional measures will support the execution of decrees in a more structured manner. Also, there are ongoing negotiations regarding the India-EU Free Trade Agreement and Investment Protection Agreement.
author: PTI
content:
New Delhi: The government is proposing further amendments to ensure time-bound resolution of challenges to arbitral awards and execution of decrees, Union Law Secretary Rajiv Mani said on Wednesday.
Addressing an ICA-SCC Arbitration Institute conclave on India-EU trade and cross-border commerce here, Mani said the proposed changes would strengthen the country's commercial dispute-resolution framework.
"Besides the enactment of the Commercial Courts Act of 2015, we are also proposing to introduce further amendments so that the finality of an arbitral award, when challenged under the applicable law and the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, is resolved within a time-bound manner, and the execution of the decree takes place in a time-bound way," Mani said, according to a statement issued by the Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA).
Referring to the Mediation Act, 2023, Mani said it provides parties with additional fora for dispute resolution and that arbitration and mediation should not be viewed as competing mechanisms.
"While arbitration provides an adjudicatory mechanism resulting in a binding determination, mediation offers parties an opportunity to resolve disputes in a consensual and amicable manner while preserving the commercial relationship," he said.
Mani, who also heads the legislative department, said that carefully designed multi-tiered clauses combining negotiation, mediation and arbitration could play a useful role in resolving commercial disputes.
Pre-institution mediation under the Commercial Courts Act also provides an opportunity for settlement before the parties approach courts, he added.
Welcoming the conclusion of negotiations on the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA), Mani said the agreement is likely to be signed soon, "perhaps this year itself".
Negotiations on the India-EU Investment Protection Agreement are also continuing, with an early conclusion in view, he said.
Stressing that smaller enterprises particularly needed accessible, affordable and predictable dispute-resolution mechanisms, Mani said the government wants arbitration to expand beyond metropolitan centres to Tier-II and Tier-III cities.

title: IIT Guwahati study identifies regional variations in earthquake activity across Northeast India
description: IIT Guwahati researchers have developed a new method to estimate earthquake-induced ground shaking in Northeast India, accounting for variations in seismic activity and uncertainties in historical records. The study identifies Imphal as the city with the highest estimated ground shaking among eight cities examined, offering insights for earthquake-resistant construction.
author: Bikash Singh
content:
Northeast India lies between two tectonic boundaries and contains the Shillong Plateau and many geological faults, all of which make it prone to earthquakes. The 1897 Shillong earthquake and the 1950 Assam earthquake were devastating to the region. Engineers designing buildings, bridges and other structures must ensure that they can withstand ground shaking during earthquakes. Assessing the extent of ground shaking that could occur during earthquakes is called “seismic hazard assessment.”
Seismic hazard assessment methods use information about previous earthquakes and geological faults to estimate how strongly the ground could shake during a future earthquake. However, there are two problems with this approach, the first problem is that earthquake activity is not uniform in this region, with some parts experiencing more intense seismic activity than others. The second problem is that historical data is not always accurate because of the absence of modern measurement devices in the past.
To bridge this gap, Prof. Abhishek Kumar, Professor, Department of Civil Engineering, along with his research graduate, Dr. Niranjan Borah [Assistant Professor, Barak Valley Engineering College], has developed a method that takes these uncertainties into account when estimating seismic hazards.
The findings of this research have been published in the prestigious Journal of Seismology.
Explaining the research, Prof. Abhishek Kumar said, “We used a mathematical technique called Kernel Density Estimation that considers the local differences in earthquake occurrence. We also considered the orientation of the geological faults because earthquake activity is more likely to occur along a fault than in other areas.”
The research team compiled information on earthquakes that occurred over the past 1,200 years to produce a catalogue containing records of nearly 6,000 earthquakes. They also generated 200 synthetic earthquake catalogues, representing alternative mathematical versions of the historical records. They created these synthetic catalogues by varying earthquake locations and magnitudes within specified uncertainty ranges. A statistical sampling method called Latin Hypercube Sampling was used for this process.
The study area was divided into a geographical grid, and the kernel density method was used to estimate the rate of earthquake occurrence in each cell. The researchers then combined these estimates with mathematical models to calculate potential ground shaking at different locations. They also examined eight cities: Guwahati, Agartala, Imphal, Shillong, Aizawl, Kohima, Gangtok and Itanagar.
Speaking about the key findings of the research, Prof. Kumar said, “The most intense earthquake activity is seen in the Indo-Burma Ranges, followed by western Arunachal Pradesh, central Assam, the Shillong Plateau and southern Sikkim.”
The researchers used a measurement called Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA) to estimate the severity of ground shaking during earthquakes. Imphal had the highest estimated level of ground shaking among the eight cities studied.
IITG method estimates how strongly the ground could shake during future earthquakes. This information, along with site-specific assessments like soil structure, could help engineers and construction specialists design earthquake-resistant structures.
As the next step, the research team plans to incorporate depth-related uncertainties and an earthquake recurrence model into the proposed framework. These enhancements are expected to provide a more comprehensive representation of seismicity, improve the robustness of probabilistic seismic hazard estimates, and further strengthen the applicability of the proposed methodology for seismic hazard assessment in North-East India.

title: Pakistani Netflix series draws fire in India, Islamabad calls backlash ‘weaponising art’
description: Netflix's upcoming series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' is inciting controversy between India and Pakistan. Indian cine bodies are demanding a ban on the show following government advisories against Pakistani content. In response, Pakistani officials are criticizing India's actions as an overreaction to a television drama. The series features popular Pakistani actors and is set to release on December 4, 2023.
author: PTI
content:
New Delhi/Islamabad: Netflix's first Pakistani show "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" was at the centre of a snowballing row on Wednesday with cine bodies in India writing to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a ban and Pakistan minister Ahsan Iqbal using the hashtag #GrowUpIndia to push back and say this amounted to weaponising art and culture.
The trailer of the show, which reunites popular stars Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and Sanam Saeed, dropped on Tuesday but there is no clarity yet on whether the show's December 4 release also includes India or only Pakistan and other countries.
As voices joined in the debate from Pakistan and India, Netflix maintained silence.
"First weaponising sports, then water, and now art and culture. The All Indian Cine Workers Association is urging New Delhi to permanently ban Pakistani content. How insecure do you have to be to see a cricket match as a political threat and a television drama as a national security concern? India, grow up," Iqbal, the minister of planning in Pakistan, said on X.
"Let athletes play, let waters flow, let artists create, and let audiences decide what they watch," he added.
His message found resonance in Pakistan with several social media users speaking up. Actor Ayesha Omer wrote, "Let athletes play, let waters flow, let artists create."
In India, the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) said the show's release in the country would be a violation of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting advisory following last year's Pahalgam terror attack when it asked OTT platforms, streaming services and intermediaries to discontinue Pakistani-origin content.
While the FWICE, which says it has up to five lakh members, took up the issue on Wednesday, AICWA sent its letter on Tuesday.
In its letter, also marked to Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Netflix India, the AICWA termed Pakistan a "terrorist country" that will never wish well for India.
"After the Pulwama attack, AICWA banned Pakistani artists from working in the Indian film industry. After the Pahalgam attack, the Government of India also imposed restrictions on Pakistani artists and content.
"On 8 May 2025, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued an advisory asking all OTT platforms, streaming services and intermediaries in India to stop streaming Pakistan-origin content, including web series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming media," it stated.
The AICWA, which states on its website that it is affiliated with the Maharashtra government and works for the rights of the people related to the film industry, went on to say that the release of the series would go directly against the spirit of that advisory and against the sentiments of the nation.
The FWICE, an umbrella body of 32 associations, asked PM Modi to intervene in the matter and direct the ministry and other concerned authorities to urgently examine the proposed release of the Pakistani series and take appropriate measures.
"We further request that the Government of India ensure that its existing directions and advisories concerning Pakistani-origin entertainment content are appropriately implemented and that all concerned digital streaming platforms and stakeholders adhere to the applicable governmental instructions," the organisation said in the letter.
Earlier, the FWICE had warned that it would "ensure the shoot of all the Netflix projects comes to a halt" if the series is released in India.
"We want to express that we have an objection to the Pakistani show. For us, the country comes first, and Pakistani artists are not welcome," its president B N Tiwari told PTI.
The calls to ban "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" in India have also raised concerns in Pakistan's entertainment industry, which fears the Indian government could tighten restrictions on content originating from Pakistan, including its availability on platforms such as YouTube.
Nadeem Mandviwalla, a well-known producer, distributor, exhibitor and cineplex owner, said the demand from India to ban the series on Netflix will decide the future of original Pakistani content on international streaming platforms.
After the Pahalgam terror attack in 2025, all cultural exchanges were banned and the Pakistan government also restricted the screening of Indian films in Pakistan cinemas.
Mandviwalla said cinema owners and distributors had lost a lot of revenue and business because of the ban but were somehow managing to keep the industry alive.
Omair Alavi, a prominent film critic and podcaster, said the launch of Pakistani content on Netflix and other streaming platforms had made sections of India's entertainment industry feel threatened.
"They have seen the huge popularity of some Pakistani dramas on Youtube, more recently 'Dar-e-Nijat', despite the thaw in cultural and arts relations and exchanges between the two countries," Alavi said.
Jamal Mir, who owns an advertising and marketing agency, said a restriction on Pakistani content on Netflix in India would be a major setback for the streaming platform as well as Pakistani creators.
"Pakistani content requires Indian audiences to succeed and encourage streaming platforms to invest further in Pakistani content as people in both countries relate a lot in culture and art," he added.
Created, directed and produced by Momina Duraid, the series adapts Pakistani novelist Farhat Ishtiaq's 2013 best selling Urdu novel of the same name. It is titled "All the Love Our Hearts Carry" in the international markets.
The series follows six interconnected love stories spanning three generations, with couples pursuing love, navigating troubled marriages and grappling with family expectations as choices made in the past shape their happiness.
It features some of the biggest names in Pakistan's entertainment industry, including Ahad Raza Mir, Iqra Aziz, Hania Aamir and Hamza Ali Abbasi.
The show reunites actors familiar to Indian audiences, with Fawad and Mahira having previously starred together in "Humsafar", while Fawad and Sanam featured in "Zindagi Gulzar Hai" and "Barzakh".
The series, which has been eight years in the making, unveiled its trailer at Karachi's historic Mohatta Palace this week, with the cast in attendance.
Duraid, whose production house has produced some of the most watched Pakistani shows in recent years including "Humsafar" and "Zindagi Gulzar Hai", said Netflix had given them a date for launch.
"We had the trailer launch and we are hoping all goes well as it is a big serial and we want it to be appreciated by audiences from around the world on the Netflix platform," she said.
