title: Trump's tariff threat: Why US is taking aim at Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat
description: The US Trade Representative has determined that India039s acts policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production are quotunreasonablequot and burden or restrict US commerce It has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods to which New Delhi has responded by rejecting the charge
author: Satyam Singh
content:
Trump's tariff threat: Why US is taking aim at Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat
The US Trade Representative has determined that India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production are "unreasonable" and burden or restrict US commerce. It has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, to which New Delhi has responded by rejecting the charge.
India is expanding factories, strengthening supply chains and developing domestic industries to increase its manufacturing capacity and establish itself as a major global manufacturing hub. Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes have been central to that push, with New Delhi offering incentives to bring investment home, expand production and reduce dependence on imports. But the Donald Trump administration took a very different reading of these policies.
Washington is arguing that India's drive for self-reliance risks producing too much manufacturing capacity and output, particularly when domestic demand does not keep pace with the factories being built. That, US officials say, can push Indian companies towards export markets, where they compete with American manufacturers.
The Trump administration has used this argument to justify imposing tariffs on India. The US Trade Representative has determined that India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production are "unreasonable" and burden or restrict US commerce under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. It also claimed that a range of India's industrial and trade practices contribute to "structural excess capacity and production" and has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods. The rate could be lowered to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a qualifying trade agreement.
That puts some of India's most prominent economic initiatives -- from Make in India and PLI to Self-Reliant India -- at the centre of a new trade confrontation. The irony is that the policies Washington is challenging are precisely the ones New Delhi has promoted as the foundation of India's economic rise.
So what exactly does the US object to, and why does Washington believe India's push to manufacture more at home could hurt American workers, businesses and the wider US economy?
Here is a blow-by-blow breakdown of the Section 301 investigation. In its 126-page report, titled 'Report on India's Acts, Policies, and Practices Relating to Structural Excess Capacity and Production in Manufacturing Sectors', the US Trade Representative (USTR) lays out its case against India's manufacturing and trade policies.
THE US CASE, IN SIMPLE TERMS
Imagine a country builds factories capable of producing 100 units of a product when its domestic market needs only 60. If those extra 40 units are produced because the market itself demanded them, Washington's argument does not necessarily apply.
But if government policies, financial incentives, trade barriers or other interventions encourage companies to keep expanding production even when demand does not justify it, the US considers that structural excess capacity.
USTR defines the phenomenon as production or capacity that is persistently above what would exist under market-oriented conditions and is created, sustained or contributed to by government policies or intervention. If the extra production cannot be absorbed at home, manufacturers may look overseas. That can mean more exports, lower prices and more competition for American manufacturers, potentially putting global and US manufactures under pressure.
USTR says this can reduce commercial opportunities for US companies, contribute to lost production, exports, jobs and investment in the US, and create economic-security risks. That is the core of the Section 301 case against India.
WHY MAKE IN INDIA IS IN THE CROSSHAIRS
The most important part of the report is that Washington explicitly names Make in India.
Launched as India's flagship manufacturing push, Make in India seeks to increase manufacturing capacity, attract investment and make India a larger production base. But USTR sees it through a different lens. The report says India has used top-down industrial efforts to maintain and expand manufacturing, establish manufacturing and export targets, and direct resources and financing towards production.
Washington sees a potential problem if that growth is being fuelled by the Indian government rather than the market. USTR says India's manufacturing plans have set a target of raising manufacturing's share to 25 per cent of GDP, which it says would require roughly doubling current manufacturing capacity and production.
The report claims that India is pursuing this expansion through incentive schemes which are designed to encourage domestic production, import substitution and exports.
In other words, the very policies India sees as tools for becoming a manufacturing hub are being portrayed by Washington as mechanisms that can create excess capacity.
PLI: WHY TRUMP ADMIN IS RAISING RED FLAGS
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme is an even more direct target because its basic structure is built around rewarding companies for increasing production. Under this scheme, the Indian government provides financial incentives to eligible companies based on incremental sales or production. The USTR, however, sees the production incentive as part of the mechanism that can expand capacity beyond what market conditions alone would generate.
The report specifically identifies PLI among India's umbrella industrial efforts and links it to the country's manufacturing and export ambitions.
The US is not saying that PLI exists to create excess capacity. It is arguing that the way such incentives operate can contribute to excess capacity when production expands without a corresponding increase in domestic demand.
ATMANIRBHAR BHARAT: SELF-RELIANCE SEEN THROUGH A US TRADE LENS
Then comes Atmanirbhar Bharat, aka Self-Reliant India.
The policy became a key part of India's economic boost to strengthen domestic manufacturing, reduce import dependence and build more resilient supply chains.
From Washington's perspective, however, the concern is that policies promote domestic production, which can go beyond meeting local demand and end up distorting global trade. In its assessment, government incentives, production targets and support for export-oriented industries can encourage manufacturers to expand capacity beyond what market demand would normally justify. If domestic consumption does not keep pace with that expansion, the surplus production can find its way into overseas markets, putting pressure on prices and making it harder for American manufacturers to compete.
The USTR claims that this does not just affect US producers in their home market. It can also limit their opportunities to sell in India and compete in third-country markets, with consequences for American manufacturing output, jobs and investment. It has identified steel, solar, pharmaceuticals, medical devices and information and communications technology (ICT) among the sectors where it sees these concerns playing out.
AND THEN THERE IS IBEF
The fourth umbrella effort explicitly named by USTR is the India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF), a lesser-known but important part of India's trade promotion machinery.
Established in 1996 as a trust under the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, IBEF's primary mandate is to promote the Made in India label in overseas markets and build international awareness of Indian products and services. It works with government departments, industry bodies, export promotion councils and Indian diplomatic missions to showcase India's manufacturing capabilities and business opportunities.
In the case, The USTR claims this model encourages export-led growth and allows Indian manufacturers to expand production beyond what market conditions would otherwise support.
THE US CASE GOES BEYOND THESE FOUR POLICIES
The four names are the most recognisable policies and programmes in the report, but they are only one part of USTR's argument.
The report identifies five broad areas that it considers problematic:
- Industrial plans to expand manufacturing
- Inadequate labour protections
- Financial repression policies
- Sustained market-access barriers
- Failure to address global excess capacity and production, including through imports and foreign direct investment from non-market economies
WHY STEEL, SOLAR, PHARMA AND ICT MATTER
It is not only PLI that Washington has identified. The USTR report identifies issues of wider concern, specifically relating to four strategic industries: health, steel, solar and information and communications technology (ICT).
STEEL
Steel is one of the critical components of overcapacity issues. In any case when capacity is created, it becomes costly to leave it unused. If there is no enough domestic demand, excess capacity can be directed to exports. In this context, growing steel manufacturing capacity in India is part of a global issue.
SOLAR
India's fast-growing manufacturing capacity in the solar-module manufacturing sector is identified by the USTR report, as having significantly exceeded domestic demand in this sector. India seeks to cut down its import dependency and become a manufacturing hub for renewable energy equipment. At the same time, Washington is worried about the global market consequences of such policy-supported production.
HEALTH
Pharmaceuticals and medical devices have been raised in the report. The Indian pharmaceutical industry is very integrated into global production chains, making this issue highly sensitive. Washington's worries are not limited to production alone, but also include domestic manufacturing incentives, import policies, foreign investments and dependence on the inputs coming from non-market economies.
ICT
Another critical issue in this context pertains to information and communication technology and encompasses the supply chains of importance that relate to telecommunications and electronics sectors. In the case of India, domestically produced ICT is crucial for achieving technological self-sufficiency. However, this might restrict US firms from benefiting from this policy.
THE CHINA FACTOR IS ALSO HIDDEN IN THE US ARGUMENT
One of the more consequential parts of the USTR case involves India's relationship with non-market economies, particularly through imports and foreign direct investment.
The US is concerned not only about what India produces itself, but also about whether India's growing manufacturing base relies on inputs, investment or supply chains connected to non-market economies, particularly from China.
That is why USTR specifically cites India's failure to address global excess capacity and production, including through imports and FDI from non-market economies.
THE LABOUR COST ADVANTAGE
Moreover, the US Trade Representative highlights the inadequacies associated with the labour laws of India, pointing out the poor protection offered for collective bargaining rights and weak enforcement of labour laws, which can lead to low wages and a competitive edge for Indian manufacturers. This is further explained by the fact that India had only 28.6 per cent labour share of manufacturing GDP in 2022, which was approximately 19 percentage points less than that in the US.
According to the Washington policymakers, restraining labour costs can enhance the competitiveness of the Indian manufacturers internationally, and adversely affect the interests of workers, putting US manufacturers at a disadvantaged position.
WHY THE US SEES AN UNEVEN PLAYING FIELD
The fifth major area is sustained market-access barriers. One of the main complaints of Washington is that while India desires better access for its manufacturers in international markets, it has created barriers making it tough for foreign firms to compete in India.
According to the USTR, the trade policy of India favors its domestic manufacturing companies and creates barriers to US exports. As a result, Indian industries can increase their production capacity without much competition from foreign firms.
Furthermore, it connects the protectionism practiced by India with its dependence on imports of intermediate products from countries considered non-market economies by the US and investments from those same countries. Particularly, it is pointed out that such imports give Indian producers cheaper raw materials which enables them to decrease the cost of production and compete better on the international market.
The reasoning behind this is that it presents a dual burden on American manufacturers: not only do they encounter obstacles in their attempt to compete in India, but Indian producers have an advantage because of their access to cheaper inputs and export capabilities within the US and elsewhere. USTR claims that India fails to take into account investments made by China in local industries.
SO WHY IS THE US BRINGING IN TARIFFS?
This is where Section 301 becomes important.
Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974 gives Washington a mechanism to investigate foreign practices that it considers unreasonable, discriminatory or harmful to US commerce and to take retaliatory trade action. The current investigation began in March 2026 and covered 16 economies.
The US has now made determinations against 14 of them, including India. Mexico and Norway have not received determinations at this stage.
For India, USTR has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on all goods, subject to stated exemptions and adjustments. It has also proposed considering a 17 per cent rate if India reaches an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the US that addresses the concerns identified in the investigation.
Therefore, the threat of imposing tariffs is not just a mechanism to penalise Indian exports but also an instrument in the hands of Washington to exert pressure on New Delhi.
INDIA REJECTS CORE OF THE US ARGUMENT
Responding to the allegations, New Delhi has rejected the claim that its industrial and trade policies have created structural excess manufacturing capacity. The Indian government said it had taken note of the USTR's determination and that the notice was under examination.
More importantly, it pointed to its position during the investigation.
"In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector," the government said.
"Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement," the statement added.
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?
The tariff is proposed, not yet final. USTR has opened a public comment process, with written comments due by January 5, 2027, and a public hearing scheduled for January 25, 2027. The agency will consider the submissions before deciding on final action. That means the immediate impact is likely to be felt first at the negotiating table.
India and the US are already working towards a bilateral trade agreement and the officials of New Delhi have repeatedly said that they have moved to the last stage of discussions. The threat of 17 per cent import tax rate in case an agreement is made makes an additional instrument for negotiation for the US and the threat is still there.
For New Delhi, the challenge is therefore twofold.
It has to defend the basic premise of its industrial strategy while also preventing a new tariff burden from undermining the export growth that the strategy is designed to create.

title: UP gang lures jobseekers with high-paying Russia jobs, dupes them of lakhs
description: The Uttar Pradesh STF arrested gang leader Pankaj Nishad The case exposes how overseas jobseekers were targeted through online listings
author: India Today News Desk
content:
UP gang lures jobseekers with high-paying Russia jobs, dupes them of lakhs
The Uttar Pradesh STF arrested gang leader Pankaj Nishad. The case exposes how overseas jobseekers were targeted through online listings.
The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force has arrested an gang leader wanted in a case of cheating people by promising to send them to Russia for construction jobs, officials told news agency Press Trust of India on Wednesday.
Pankaj Nishad, also known as Golu, carried a reward of Rs 50,000. He was arrested near Nagarpur crossing in Ambedkar Nagar district on Tuesday evening, the STF said.
Nishad, a resident of Jaldipur village in Azamgarh district, was wanted in a case registered at Tarun police station in Ayodhya in 2024. The case involves charges related to cheating, impersonation and forgery.
According to the STF, the gang used the online directory platform Justdial to identify and lure people seeking jobs abroad. Its members registered their contact numbers on the platform and posed as overseas recruitment agents when jobseekers contacted them.
The accused took the applicants' passports and initially collected Rs 40,000 from each of them. They later demanded another Rs 1.20 lakh with the promise of arranging visas and air tickets. The applicants were told that they would be sent to Russia on work visas for construction jobs with a monthly salary of 4.5 lakh to 5 lakh Russian roubles, the STF said.
The gang worked with a company identified as JS Interference Limited. The STF statement named Sachin Singh as the company's chief executive officer. The accused told investigators that they paid Rs 1 lakh to the company as part of the arrangement.
“Even after collecting the initial amounts, the gang demanded an additional Rs 1 lakh to Rs 2 lakh from the applicants. Those who refused to pay were sent fake flight-holding tickets to make them believe that their travel arrangements were underway,” the STF said, quoting the accused.
The arrest followed intelligence inputs received by an STF team on Tuesday night, according to Press Trust of India.
During questioning, Nishad disclosed that cases had been registered against him at different police stations. He had earlier been arrested in a case registered at Dostpur police station in Sultanpur district in 2021, the STF said.
Nishad has been handed over to the Ayodhya police in connection with the 2024 case. The local police will conduct further legal proceedings in the case involving the alleged collection of money from jobseekers promised construction work in Russia.

title: Ankita Bhandari murder case: FIR against Vinod Arya for leaking her private chats
description: Soni Devi has filed a complaint against Vinod Arya and Anuj Pundir over the disclosure of her daughter039s private chats She says the release violated Ankita Bhandari039s privacy and dignity and distressed the family
author: Ankit Sharma
content:
Ankita Bhandari murder case: FIR against Vinod Arya for leaking her private chats
Soni Devi has filed a complaint against Vinod Arya and Anuj Pundir over the disclosure of her daughter's private chats. She says the release violated Ankita Bhandari's privacy and dignity and distressed the family.
Ankita Bhandari's mother, Soni Devi, has filed a police complaint against expelled BJP leader Vinod Arya and advocate Anuj Pundir over the public disclosure of the deceased's private WhatsApp conversations with her friend, saying that the move violated her daughter's privacy and dignity and hurt the family's sentiments.
A Zero FIR was registered at Rajpur police station in Dehradun on November 25. The case has been transferred to Haridwar's Kotwali police station on grounds of jurisdiction.
The complaint, dated November 22, seeks legal action against Vinod Arya, father of convicted Ankita Bhandari murder case accused Pulkit Arya, and advocate Anuj Pundir for making the private WhatsApp chats between Ankita and her friend Pushpdeep public through the media.
The case pertains to a murder that took place in 2022. Ankita Bhandari, 19, was working as a receptionist at Vanantara Resort near Rishikesh when she went missing on September 18, 2022. Her body was later recovered from the Chilla canal. Resort owner Pulkit Arya, son of former BJP leader Vinod Arya, and two employees, Saurabh Bhaskar and Ankit Gupta, were arrested in the murder case. The killing triggered widespread protests across Uttarakhand, with demands for justice and questions over women's safety and political influence. All three accused were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment by a Kotdwar court on May 30, 2025.
WHAT THE COMPLAINT SAYS
In her complaint, Soni Devi said the private conversations between Ankita and Pushpdeep were collected by investigators during the murder case and were part of the electronic evidence. The chats were also made available to the defence during the trial.
She claimed that the conversations contained personal and sensitive exchanges shared between the two in confidence. During the trial, the defence attempted to question prosecution witnesses about these chats, but the court objected to the questions, considering them irrelevant and related to Ankita's personal dignity and privacy, the complaint stated.
The matter also came before the Uttarakhand High Court, where questions based on the private chats were reportedly not considered relevant and were viewed as contrary to the privacy and dignity of Ankita and her friend.
The complaint said that despite these judicial proceedings, Vinod Arya and advocate Anuj Pundir publicly circulated or displayed the private conversations before the media around one-and-a-half years after the trial court's verdict. It said the disclosure had hurt Ankita's posthumous dignity and reputation and caused deep mental distress to her family.
Soni Devi argued that a person's privacy, dignity and reputation do not cease to matter after their death, particularly when the conversations were exchanged in confidence and there was no legal or justifiable reason to make them public.
VINOD ARYA RELEASES OVER 4,000 PAGES OF CHATS
The complaint comes amid a controversy over Vinod Arya's recent press conference, during which he claimed his son had been wrongly implicated in the murder case due to political pressure. He also alleged that Ankita died by suicide because of harassment by her parents and a male friend, rather than being murdered.
Vinod Arya reportedly released more than 4,000 pages of purported WhatsApp conversations between Ankita and her friend and demanded that the chats be included in the investigation.
The disclosure triggered protests in Haridwar, where office-bearers of the Pahadi Mahasabha approached Nagar Kotwali police and demanded that a case be registered against Vinod Arya, alleging that the release of the chats violated Ankita's privacy.
The latest complaint seeks legal action over the disclosure of Ankita's purported private conversations and an impartial investigation into their source, as demands for a wider probe into the murder continue.

title: Kashi Tamil Sangamam aims to remind youth of India’s cultural unity: Pralhad Joshi
description: Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan will inaugurate the event on November 28.
author: Gayathri Mani
content:
Around 46,000 applications have been received for the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam, of which 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu will be selected, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi said on Wednesday.
The participants will be divided into seven groups of 200 each and will travel from different parts of Tamil Nadu, including Kanyakumari, Chennai and Coimbatore, to Varanasi. Their itinerary will cover Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, with three to four days of travel followed by a four-day programme. The first student delegation has already departed from Kanyakumari, he said.
Joshi told a press conference here, the initiative was conceptualised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2022 to highlight the historical and cultural relationship between Tamil Nadu in the South and Kashi in the North.
The programme aims to remind the younger generation that India has remained culturally united from ancient times to the present day, in keeping with the principle of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat, Joshi said.
When asked about the language debate between centre and Tamil Nadu, Joshi said, “The programme promotes Tamil. Every state should give priority to its regional language — Tamil in Tamil Nadu, Kannada in Karnataka, Odia in Odisha and Gujarati in Gujarat. This is also provided for in the National Education Policy. There is no question of any controversy over this.”
Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan will inaugurate the event on November 28 at 11 am, while Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will attend the concluding ceremony on December 12, Joshi said.
Participants will get an opportunity to understand the culture, languages, traditions and traditional attire of different regions. During previous editions, participants from Uttar Pradesh were taken to Rameswaram.
The Ministry of Education is the nodal ministry for the programme, with the Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti, Banaras Hindu University (BHU) and IIT Madras playing key roles in organising it. Four editions have been held so far.
The theme of the fifth edition is ‘Tirukkural Payilvom’ (lets learn Tirukkural). The literary work of Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar comprises couplets of two lines each.
The fourth edition’s theme was ‘Tamil Karkalam’ (Let us learn Tamil), while the third focused on Sage Agastya, the second featured live speech translation and the first included an eight-day heritage visit.
A nationwide student engagement programme on Tirukkural has also been launched, covering 1,380 higher education institutions across the country. One student from each institution will undertake a structured study of Tirukkural for one month in a language of their choice and receive a stipend of Rs 10,000 through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
Study material will be available in all 22 scheduled languages and English, Joshi said.
An online quiz has also been launched on the MyGov portal. The programme will run from November 28 to December 12.
Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan will inaugurate the event on November 28 at 11 am, while Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will attend the concluding ceremony on December 12, Joshi said.

title: Peace along LAC: India, China hold military-level talks in Arunachal
description: Focus on setting engagement rules, avoiding friction, ensuring open communication
author: Shubhajit Roy
content:
Shubhajit Roy, Diplomatic Editor at The Indian Express, has been a journalist for more than 27 years... Read More
The Indian and Chinese armies held high-level talks this month in the Arunachal Pradesh sector focusing on border management and addressing outstanding issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the Indian government said on Wednesday in the first official confirmation of the talks.
Responding to questions on Wednesday, Ministry of External Affairs official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “India and China engage regularly through diplomatic and military mechanisms and you are well aware of those mechanisms. A meeting of the senior military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently. Discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management as well as addressing outstanding issues along the LAC.”
Jaiswal said such interactions are aimed at maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and preventing any escalation.
The Indian Express had reported on November 22 that India and China have concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks to resolve tensions along the frontier in Arunachal Pradesh before winter sets in fully.
The closely guarded talks, which began immediately after Diwali on November 8, continued for nearly 10 days with a short break in between.
Lt General Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Army’s III Corps (also called the Spear Corps – with its headquarters at Rangapahar near Dimapur in Nagaland) held talks with his Chinese counterpart and other officers. An official from the MEA was also present.
This round of talks was held to set engagement rules between the two sides, avoid friction between troops on the ground, ensure open communication lines between both sides and bring down tensions. Both sides have troops in large numbers in the area.
India and China held their first Corps Commander-level talks in the eastern sector on September 6-7 this year. That meeting at the Wacha-Damai border — Wacha is India’s easternmost border personnel meeting point located in the Kibithoo sector — followed reports of tension in the Taksing area of the Upper Subansiri district.
In August, two weeks before the first round of the military talks, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, the special representatives for boundary talks between the two countries, met in Beijing.
In October, just days before his retirement, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) Director General Shatrujeet Kapur said Indian and Chinese troops had faced off at multiple locations in Arunachal Pradesh.
In response to Kapur’s remarks, the MEA said the situation along the LAC “gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns”. It underlined that “maintenance of peace and tranquility in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations”.
Days later, Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu had said “transgressions” keep happening along the frontier since China does not recognise the McMahon Line.
Agreed upon in 1914 between British India and Tibet, the McMahon Line serves as the de facto boundary between India and China in Arunachal Pradesh. Beijing does not recognise it, saying it was not for Tibet to enter into such an agreement.
Khandu had told reporters: “No doubt transgression has happened. It keeps happening. It is nothing new since the border is not defined. The situation is quite normal now and our Armed Forces are guarding the border very well.”
“China doesn’t consider the McMahon Line in Arunachal and since the state shares a very long border with Tibet, sometimes patrolling parties transgress. Our soldiers go (to) that side, their patrolling parties also come (to) this side sometimes,” he had said.

title: Nicobar forest rights matter: Centre gets time until December 10 to file fresh submissions
description: As part of the Rs 92,000-crore project, the Centre wants to build an integrated township, a transshipment container port at Galathea Bay, a solar and gas-based power plant, and a greenfield military and civilian-use airport
author: Nikhil Ghanekar
content:
An award-winning journalist with 14 years of experience, Nikhil Ghanekar is an Assistant Editor with... Read More
The Calcutta High Court circuit bench at Port Blair on Wednesday granted time to the Centre for filing further submissions in response to a PIL by former civil servant Meena Gupta, who had challenged the Forest Rights Act proceedings to divert 166 sq km of forest land for the Great Nicobar project.
It deferred the final hearings in this PIL and two tagged matters related to the Great Nicobar until January, after arguments by Attorney General for India R Venkataramani and Additional Solicitor General Vikramjit Banerjee as well as the counsel for the petitioner.
Appearing for the Centre, ASJ Banerjee said it is the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956, and not the Forest Rights Act, 2006, which applies to the island group, and this stand has been consistent across administrations. Banerjee sought to argue that there are official letters and Parliamentary responses in this regard and that the Centre will present its stand on this issue in an affidavit.
A bench of Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge and Justice Supratim Bhattacharya gave the Centre time until December 10 to file a supplementary affidavit. It agreed to hear the matter in the second week of January. Further, it also granted time to the Union government to file objections pertaining to the maintainability of two related matters filed by Gupta on the reduction of the buffer zone of Galathea National Park and Campbell Bay National Park.
Even as the bench granted time, the counsel for the petitioner pointed out that the Calcutta HC circuit bench had already settled the issue of maintainability in a May order and had agreed to hear the petitions. After this May order, the Centre had moved the Supreme Court against the HC’s order. However, the Supreme Court had refused to entertain the plea and asked the High Court to hear the matters at the earliest.
Gupta’s petition has challenged the validity of proceedings held under the Forest Rights Act. This includes a challenge to the resolution of three Gram Sabhas in August 2022 on consenting to the diversion of forest land for the Great Nicobar project, the composition of a sub-divisional-level committee that examines resolutions by a Gram Sabha, and the eventual record of forest rights certification issued for land diversion.
As part of the Rs 92,000-crore project, the Centre wants to build an integrated township, a transshipment container port at Galathea Bay, a solar and gas-based power plant, and a greenfield military and civilian-use airport. A recent draft master plan also cited tourism as the backbone of Great Nicobar Island while developing a greenfield coastal city, supported by a service industry and a port-linked finance hub.

title: India rejects US excess capacity claims, says no structural overcapacity in any sector
description: “The Notice is currently under examination,” the ministry said, adding that India had engaged constructively throughout the investigation. | India News
author: HT News Desk
content:

India rejects US excess capacity claims, says no structural overcapacity in any sector
“The Notice is currently under examination,” the ministry said, adding that India had engaged constructively throughout the investigation.
The government of India on Wednesday said it was examining a notice issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in a probe into manufacturing capacity across 14 economies, including India, and reiterated that the country does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.
In a statement issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the government said it had taken note of the notice of determination and request for comments issued by the USTR under Section 301 of the US Trade Act.
“The Notice is currently under examination,” the ministry said, adding that India had engaged constructively throughout the investigation.
Deep Dive
The Department of Commerce had stated, in its response to the notice of initiation and subsequent proceedings, that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector, the statement said.
India also reiterated that trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of the ongoing negotiations for the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA).
“The Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement,” the ministry said, referring to the framework announced on February 2 and the joint statement issued on February 7.
US report targets India's manufacturing policies
The USTR's 189-page report, released on Wednesday, has built its case around India's flagship manufacturing programmes, including Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme.
The report describes India's manufacturing policies as an effort to expand production beyond what market demand would support. It concludes that India's “acts, policies, and practices” concerning manufacturing capacity are unreasonable and burden US commerce.
The USTR estimates that raising manufacturing's share of India's GDP to 25%, as envisaged under Make in India, would require about $500 billion in additional output at 2025 levels.
India has rejected the allegations throughout the eight-month investigation, arguing that it is building manufacturing capacity to meet domestic demand and reduce dependence on certain countries for critical inputs.
In its submissions, India said production rises and falls according to orders and market conditions, rather than being directed by the government. It also argued that Make in India and PLI should not be viewed as schemes to create manufacturing capacity unrelated to demand.
India participated in confidential consultations with the USTR during the investigation. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal had also rejected the charge at the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee in October, saying India “does not have structural excess capacity” in the sectors identified.
Tariff proposal and trade deal talks
The USTR has proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods under the Section 301 investigation. The rate could fall to 17% if India signs a trade agreement with Washington.
The report focuses on sectors such as steel, solar, health and information and communications technology (ICT), and also flags India's labour laws, market access barriers and growing imports of inputs from China.
The proposed tariffs exempt generic medicines in dosage form, hundreds of drug ingredients when used in pharmaceuticals, and patented drugs.
Written comments on the proposed tariffs are due by January 5, 2027, while hearings are scheduled to begin on January 25.
India and the US have been negotiating a bilateral trade agreement since February 2025. The two countries announced a framework for an interim deal in February, with Washington outlining an 18% reciprocal tariff on a range of Indian goods.

title: India to become major global space power, says Skyroot Aerospace CEO
description: Pawan Kumar Chandana said the first private rocket launch by Skyroot Aerospace was only a beginning. | India News
author: PTI
content:
India to become major global space power, says Skyroot Aerospace CEO
Pawan Kumar Chandana said the first private rocket launch by Skyroot Aerospace was only a beginning.
Skyroot Aerospace Co-Founder and CEO Pawan Kumar Chandana on Wednesday said India is poised to emerge as one of the most important countries in the global space sector, with Indian talent expected to drive major achievements in the coming decades.
Chandana was speaking at the 45th Vikram Sarabhai Memorial Lecture on "Find Your Space in Space: The Story of a 2026 Spacepreneur – Roots to Wings: From Vikram Sarabhai to Vikram-1, and Beyond".
Recalling the vision of India's space programme, he said it was inspired by Dr Vikram Sarabhai, who wanted the country to be second to none in applying advanced technologies for the benefit of the common man.
"That started the journey of ISRO and India's space programme," he said.
Chandana said the first private rocket launch by Skyroot Aerospace was only a beginning, adding that the seeds sown in India's private space sector would grow into a much larger ecosystem in the future.
Also read: Sky is no longer the limit: Vikram-1 launch is a leap for India's private space sector
Major developments in the space sector would have a ripple effect and contribute to India's growing global prominence, he said.
"India is going to be one of the most important countries in the space sector globally, and Indian talent is going to be a phenomenal source of space achievements in the coming decades," Chandana said.
Predicting rapid technological advancement, Chandana said humanity could make more progress in the next 10 years than it had achieved over the previous 200 years.
The space sector was one of the biggest career opportunities for young people, he said, urging them to join emerging space companies or venture into entrepreneurship in the sector.
"The future is full of communication, tourism, manufacturing, earth observation from space," Chandana said.
Skyroot Aerospace developed India's first privately developed orbital rocket, Vikram-1, and launched it on July 18, 2026.
A team of more than 1,000 engineers and nearly 400 domestic suppliers played a key role in developing the rocket, Chandana noted.

title: Finance Ministry imposes restrictions on media entry till Budget announcement
description: The Union Budget for 2027-28 is scheduled for February 1; it will be Nirmala Sitharaman's 10th straight Budget and the fourth of the Modi 3.0 government. | India News
author: PTI
content:
Finance Ministry imposes restrictions on media entry till Budget announcement
The Union Budget for 2027-28 is scheduled for February 1; it will be Nirmala Sitharaman's 10th straight Budget and the fourth of the Modi 3.0 government.
The finance ministry has imposed restrictions on the entry of media persons into Kartavya Bhavan-1 till the Budget presentation.
The restrictions, effective from November 30, have been imposed in view of the commencement of the Union Budget preparation process, which is now gaining momentum, sources said.
Media persons will be allowed entry into Kartavya Bhavan 1 during this period only with specific permission from officers authorised for the purpose, they said.
The authorities have asked the concerned officials to ensure strict compliance with the entry restrictions, sources said.
Also read: India shrugs off oil shock to post 7.8% growth in Q1, PM Modi hails ‘herculean feat’
The Union Budget for FY 2027-28 is scheduled to be presented on February 1.
It will be the fourth budget of the Modi 3.0 government and the 10th straight budget for Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, a rare distinction in Indian polity.
The Budget 2027-28 would be presented against the backdrop of global supply chain disruptions triggered by the ongoing West Asia crisis and moderation in global growth.
However, domestic growth is expected to be strong around 7 per cent in the current financial year. India clocked a growth rate of 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of FY27, the fastest among the large economies in the world.
Also read: IMF pegs India’s growth at 7% for FY27-FY28, raises global forecast but warns of risks, debt strain
The budget for the next financial year is expected to focus on the reform continuation exercise to further accelerate economic growth, along with measures to create jobs and boost domestic demand.

title: TN guv asks TVK govt to explain non-compliance of SC order on deepam issue
description: Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has sought an explanation from the TVK government over alleged noncompliance of a Supreme Court directive to light the Karthigai deepam at the stone pillar atop the Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai, official sources said on Wednesday.
author: PTI
content:
TN guv asks TVK govt to explain non-compliance of SC order on deepam issue
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 23:19 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 23:19 IST
State authorities bypassed a supreme court directive to light the traditional lamp on the hilltop stone pillar, opting instead for a customary mandapam location. While temple trustees defended the move by citing long-sta
Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has sought an explanation from the TVK government over alleged non-compliance of a Supreme Court directive to light the Karthigai deepam at the stone pillar atop the Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai, official sources said on Wednesday.
A letter has been sent to the government to furnish official information related to the matter, and specific police instructions followed on the ground, the sources told PTI.
The Karthigai Deepam (lamp) was lit at the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillayar Temple on Tuesday, and not at a spot on the hill where the stone pillar stands. The SC had earlier directed a one-time lighting of the lamp on the stone pillar.
The apex court on Wednesday said it will hear in a day or two applications seeking directions for lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam at the stone pillar atop the Thirupparankundram hill.
A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said the registry will verify the filing of the applications including contempt petitions and the court will see if they can be listed on Thursday or Friday.
Hours after lighting the Karthigai Deepam on Tuesday at the customary location, and skipping the court-directed stone pillar, the temple’s Board of Trustees asserted that long-standing religious traditions must take precedence.
However, the Thirupparankundram temple priests (Sthanikars) disassociated themselves from the Board’s decision.

title: Special trains, enhanced security for Sabarimala pilgrims during pilgrimage season
description: Extensive arrangements have been put in place to ensure safe, comfortable and hassle-free travel for pilgrims during the Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season 2026-27, a statement issued by the railways said.
author: PTI
content:
Special trains, enhanced security for Sabarimala pilgrims during pilgrimage season
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 20:55 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 20:55 IST
Extensive arrangements have been put in place to ensure safe, comfortable and hassle-free travel for pilgrims during the Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season 2026-27, a statement issued by the railways said.
The Southern Railways on Wednesday said that special trains were introduced and security was strengthened to make travel for Sabarimala pilgrims safe and comfortable.
Extensive arrangements have been put in place to ensure safe, comfortable and hassle-free travel for pilgrims during the Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season 2026-27, a statement issued by the railways said.
The arrangements included the introduction of special trains in coordination with other railway zones, much earlier than in previous years, the statement said.
It said that as of November 23, a total of 204 trips of Sabarimala special trains have been notified, covering inter-zonal and intra-zonal services.
Further services will be planned based on passenger demand and reservation trends, it said.
Special arrangements for accommodation, rest, catering, sanitation and onward transportation have been made at the key transit stations in Kottayam, Chengannur, Ernakulam Junction and Ernakulam Town for Sabarimala pilgrims.
The arrangements at the transit stations also included deployment of personnel proficient in Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada to assist pilgrims from other states.
"This will reduce waiting time, ease ticket purchase and ensure effective passenger assistance," the statement said.
It also said that the Southern Railway was working closely with the various state government departments, police and the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) for the smooth movement and welfare of pilgrims.
Additionally, security has been strengthened at important stations and on trains to ensure the safety of pilgrims throughout their journey, the statement said.
The security measures included intensified surveillance, regular monitoring, intelligence gathering, anti-sabotage checks with Railway Protection Force (RPF) dog squads, and Crime Prevention and Detection Squads at important stations, it said.
Besides these, Railway officials from various departments are closely monitoring special train operations, passenger amenities, station management and crowd movement throughout the season, the statement said.
"A dedicated task force will be deployed on Makaravilakku Day at Chengannur, Ernakulam Junction and Kottayam stations to coordinate passenger movement, monitor special train operations and ensure the smooth functioning of the additional booking counters and other facilities."
"All arrangements are reviewed on a day-to-day basis so that services keep pace with changing passenger requirements during the peak pilgrimage period," Southern Railways said.

title: Government proposes amendments for time-bound resolution of challenges to arbitral awards: Law secretary
description: Addressing an ICA-SCC Arbitration Institute conclave on India-EU trade and cross-border commerce here, Mani said the proposed changes would strengthen the country's commercial dispute-resolution framework.
author: PTI
content:
Government proposes amendments for time-bound resolution of challenges to arbitral awards: Law secretary
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 20:53 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 21:04 IST
Addressing an ICA-SCC Arbitration Institute conclave on India-EU trade and cross-border commerce here, Mani said the proposed changes would strengthen the country's commercial dispute-resolution framework.
The government is proposing further amendments to ensure time-bound resolution of challenges to arbitral awards and execution of decrees, Union Law Secretary Rajiv Mani said on Wednesday.
Addressing an ICA-SCC Arbitration Institute conclave on India-EU trade and cross-border commerce here, Mani said the proposed changes would strengthen the country's commercial dispute-resolution framework.
“Besides the enactment of the Commercial Courts Act of 2015, we are also proposing to introduce further amendments so that the finality of an arbitral award, when challenged under the applicable law and the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, is resolved within a time-bound manner, and the execution of the decree takes place in a time-bound way,” Mani said, according to a statement issued by the Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA).
Referring to the Mediation Act, 2023, Mani said it provides parties with additional fora for dispute resolution and that arbitration and mediation should not be viewed as competing mechanisms.
“While arbitration provides an adjudicatory mechanism resulting in a binding determination, mediation offers parties an opportunity to resolve disputes in a consensual and amicable manner while preserving the commercial relationship,” he said.
Mani, who also heads the legislative department, said that carefully designed multi-tiered clauses combining negotiation, mediation and arbitration could play a useful role in resolving commercial disputes.
Pre-institution mediation under the Commercial Courts Act also provides an opportunity for settlement before the parties approach courts, he added.
Welcoming the conclusion of negotiations on the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA), Mani said the agreement is likely to be signed soon, “perhaps this year itself”.
Negotiations on the India-EU Investment Protection Agreement are also continuing, with an early conclusion in view, he said.
Stressing that smaller enterprises particularly needed accessible, affordable and predictable dispute-resolution mechanisms, Mani said the government wants arbitration to expand beyond metropolitan centres to Tier-II and Tier-III cities.

title: न गाय पाली, न डेयरी खोली... फिर भी भारत में ला दी दूध की बाढ़, कौन थे 'मिल्कमैन ऑफ इंडिया?'
description: जानिए 'मिल्कमैन ऑफ इंडिया' डॉ. वर्गीस कुरियन की प्रेरक कहानी, जिन्होंने बिना खुद डेयरी खोले 'ऑपरेशन फ्लड' और अमूल के जरिए भारत को दुनिया का सबसे बड़ा दूध उत्पादक देश बना दिया.
author: रवींद्र प्रताप सिंह
content:
न गाय पाली, न डेयरी खोली, फिर भी भारत को दूध उत्पादन में आत्मनिर्भर बनाने की ऐसी कहानी लिखी, जिसने देश की तस्वीर बदल दी. ये थे डॉ. वर्गीस कुरियन, जिन्हें 'मिल्कमैन ऑफ इंडिया' के नाम से जाना जाता है. कुरियन का जन्म 26 नवंबर 1921 को केरल के कोझिकोड में हुआ था. उन्होंने गुजरात के आनंद से श्वेत क्रांति की शुरुआत की और किसानों को दूध के कारोबार में सीधे भागीदार बनाया. उन्होंने अमूल को सिर्फ एक डेयरी ब्रांड नहीं, बल्कि किसानों की आर्थिक ताकत का प्रतीक बना दिया.
डॉ. वर्गीज कुरियन के नेतृत्व में शुरू हुए ऑपरेशन फ्लड ने भारत को दूध की कमी वाले देश से दुनिया के सबसे बड़े दूध उत्पादकों में शामिल कर दिया. कुरियन न तो पशुपालक थे, न ही उन्हें दूध के कारोबार का कोई पुराना तजुर्बा था. वे तो पेशे से एक मैकेनिकल इंजीनियर थे, जिन्होंने अमेरिका से पढ़ाई की थी और भारत इसलिए लौटे थे ताकि अपनी वजीफे की शर्त पूरी कर सकें और फिर अपना रास्ता पकड़ लें.
कुरियन का मॉडल ऐसा था, जिसमें मुनाफे का बड़ा हिस्सा बिचौलियों के बजाय किसानों तक पहुंचता था. उन्होंने साबित किया कि सही नेतृत्व, मजबूत सहकारी व्यवस्था और किसानों की भागीदारी से गांवों की अर्थव्यवस्था बदली जा सकती है. डॉ. कुरियन की विरासत आज भी भारत की ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था और श्वेत क्रांति की सबसे बड़ी पहचान है. 1940 के दशक के आखिर में उन्हें गुजरात के आणंद में एक सरकारी क्रीमरी में काम पर लगाया गया. शुरुआत में उनका मन वहां बिल्कुल नहीं लगता था.
कुरियन को लगता था कि वे एक इंजीनियर हैं और यहां दूध और मक्खन के बीच फंस गए हैं. लेकिन धीरे-धीरे उन्होंने गांव के किसानों की बेबसी को करीब से देखा. किसान सुबह-शाम मेहनत करते थे, पर बिचौलिये उनका सारा मुनाफा खा जाते थे. बारिश या गर्मी के मौसम में दूध खराब हो जाता था और किसानों को औने-पौने दामों पर बेचने के लिए मजबूर होना पड़ता था.
सही मायनों में बदलाव की नींव तब पड़ी जब कुरियन ने त्रिभुवनदास पटेल के साथ मिलकर किसानों को एकजुट करने की दिशा में काम किया. विचार बहुत सीधा था, लेकिन उसे जमीन पर उतारना टेढ़ी खीर थी. अगर किसान खुद अपनी सहकारी समिति बनाएं और दूध का प्रसंस्करण व बिक्री खुद संभालें, तो बीच के मुनाफाखोरों को हटाया जा सकता है.
यहीं से 'कैरा डिस्ट्रिक्ट को-ऑपरेटिव मिल्क प्रोड्यूसर्स यूनियन' की ताकत सामने आई, जिसे आज हम सब अमूल के नाम से जानते हैं. कुरियन ने कोई पारंपरिक डेयरी साम्राज्य खड़ा करने के बजाय एक ऐसा ढांचा तैयार किया, जिसमें मालिक खुद किसान थे. छोटे-छोटे गांवों से दूध इकट्ठा करना, उसकी जांच करना, ठंडा रखना और सही समय पर बाजार तक पहुंचाना यह सब एक व्यवस्था के तहत होने लगा.
सबसे बड़ी समस्या यह थी कि भैंस के दूध से पाउडर बनाना और उसे लंबे समय तक सुरक्षित रखना आसान नहीं माना जाता था. दुनिया भर में गाय के दूध से मिल्क पाउडर बनाने का चलन था, जबकि भारत में भैंस का दूध ज्यादा था. कुरियन और उनकी टीम ने इस चुनौती को स्वीकार किया और भैंस के दूध से पाउडर व कंडेंस्ड मिल्क बनाने की तकनीक को सफल कर दिखाया. एक तरह से उन्होंने उस धारणा को तोड़ दिया कि भारत में दूध का बड़े पैमाने पर औद्योगिक इस्तेमाल संभव नहीं है.
जब आणंद का मॉडल सफल हुआ, तो सवाल उठा कि क्या इसे पूरे देश में फैलाया जा सकता है? 1970 में ऑपरेशन फ्लड की शुरुआत हुई. नाम सुनकर भले ही पानी की बाढ़ का ख्याल आए, लेकिन इसका मकसद देश के कोने-कोने में दूध की उपलब्धता बढ़ाना और ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूत करना था. इस योजना की खासियत यह थी कि इसने 'रूरल-टू-अर्बन' या गांव से शहर की सीधी कड़ी जोड़ी. शहरों की मांग को गांवों के उत्पादन से इस तरह जोड़ा गया कि दोनों को फायदा मिले.
एक दौर ऐसा भी था जब भारत दूध की कमी से जूझता था और बाहरी मदद पर निर्भर रहना पड़ता था. कुरियन के काम और सहकारी मॉडल ने तस्वीर ही बदल दी. भारत धीरे-धीरे दुनिया के सबसे बड़े दूध उत्पादक देशों में शुमार हो गया. यह किसी जादू की छड़ी से नहीं हुआ, बल्कि सालों की मेहनत, जिद, नौकरशाही से टकराने की हिम्मत और जमीनी हकीकत को समझने की वजह से हुआ.
डॉ. वर्गीज कुरियन की एक बड़ी पहचान उनकी बेबाकी थी. वे गलत बात पर चुप रहने वालों में से नहीं थे. चाहे नीतियों का मामला हो या किसानों के हक की लड़ाई, उन्होंने हमेशा उसी बात को तरजीह दी जिससे गांव के आखिरी किसान का भला हो. उन्होंने कभी बड़े-बड़े दावों या दिखावे का सहारा नहीं लिया. उनका मानना था कि असली ताकत संस्थानों में होती है, किसी एक व्यक्ति के करिश्मे में नहीं. वर्गीज करोड़ों हाथों को रोजगार और करोड़ों घरों को पोषण दिया. उनकी कहानी बताती है कि बदलाव लाने के लिए हमेशा उसी क्षेत्र का विशेषज्ञ होना जरूरी नहीं है; जरूरी है समस्या को गहराई से देखना और लोगों पर भरोसा करना. 9 सितंबर 2012 को 90 वर्ष की उम्र में इस महान शख्सियत ने दुनिया को अलविदा कह दिया.

title: जिस दवा पर जिंदगी बचाने का भरोसा, वही बन रही जान की दुश्मन! पैरासिटामोल से हार्ट की दवाओं तक में गड़बड़ी
description: CDSCO की रिपोर्ट में अक्टूबर महीने में 324 दवाओं के सैंपल गुणवत्ता जांच में फेल हुए हैं. इनमें पैरासिटामोल, एंटीबायोटिक, बीपी और हार्ट की दवाएं भी शामिल हैं. नकली और मिलावटी दवाओं से मरीजों की सेहत पर गंभीर खतरा मंडरा रहा है.
author: ताहिर कामरान
content:
ZEE NEWS लगातार आपसे जुड़े मुद्दों को लगातार उठा रहा है. हमने खाने से लेकर पानी में मिलावट तक का मुद्दा उठाया. शुद्ध हवा का मुद्दा उठाया. आज बात शुद्ध दवा की होगी. अगर खराब खाना, खराब पानी और खराब हवा की वजह से आपकी तबीयत बिगड़ती है, तो आप क्या करते हैं? दवा लेते हैं, लेकिन अगर दवा ही अशुद्ध और मिलावटी हो तो आप क्या करेंगे?
देश में दवाओं की गुणवत्ता को लेकर केंद्रीय औषधि मानक नियंत्रण संगठन यानी CDSCO ने एक रिपोर्ट जारी की है. अक्टूबर महीने में जांच की गई दवाओं में से 324 दवाएं गुणवत्ता जांच में फेल हो गईं. यानी सिर्फ एक महीने में इतने सैंपल या तो खराब गुणवत्ता के पाए गए या फिर उनमें कोई मिलावट पाई गई. आज हम खराब दवाओं वाली इसी रिपोर्ट को डिकोड करने वाले हैं. आपको पता चलेगा कि वो कौन कौन सी दवाएं हैं जिनका नाम इस लिस्ट में है. इन दवाओं का उपयोग हमारे देश में कितने लोग करते हैं. साथ ही, आपको आज ये भी पता चलेगा कि खराब और नकली दवाओं का बाजार हमारे देश में कितना बड़ा है और इससे कितनी बड़ी आबादी प्रभावित हो रही है.
लेकिन सबसे पहले आपको 324 दवाओं की इस लिस्ट को बहुत गौर से देखना चाहिए. (लिस्ट देखने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें) ये लिस्ट हर उस व्यक्ति को देखनी चाहिए जो कोई न कोई दवा खाता है. ये लिस्ट हर उस व्यक्ति को देखनी चाहिए जिनके परिवार में कोई न कोई दवा का सेवन करता है. ये देखना चाहिए कि क्या आप जो दवा खा रहे हैं वो इस लिस्ट में मौजूद है या नहीं.
इस लिस्ट में कई दवाओं के नाम तो ऐसे हैं जो आप आमतौर पर सर्दी, बुखार या बदन दर्द में लेते हैं.. ब्लड प्रेशर और एसिडिटी के लिए ली जाने वाली दवाइयां भी जांच में फेल हुई हैं. इसमें पहला नाम है आईब्रूफेन एंड पैरासिटामोल सस्पेंशन. इस दवा के बारे में आप में से 90 फीसदी लोग जानते होंगे. इसे बुखार और दर्द के वक्त लिया जाता है, लेकिन इसके एक सैंपल की जांच में आईब्रूफेन की मात्रा ही तय मानकों से अलग पाई गई है.
दूसरी दवा का नाम है एजिथ्रोमाइसिन टैबलेट जो एक एंटीबायोटिक है. इसे वायरल इंफेक्शन के वक्त खाया जाता है. इस सैंपल में ब्रांड का नाम भी दर्ज है. Azithral 500. इसके एक खास बैच की जांच में पाया गया कि इसमें एजिथ्रोमाइसिन की मात्रा तय मानकों के हिसाब से नहीं पाई गई.
इसी लिस्ट में टेल्मीसर्टन दवा भी दर्ज है. जिसे ब्लड प्रेशर के मरीज खाते हैं. इसके एक सैंपल की जांच में टैबलेट का वजन ही गलत पाया गया.
अगला नाम है क्लोपी डोग्रेल एंड एस्पिरिन कैप्सूल. ये दवा हार्ट ब्लॉकेज रोकने के लिए दी जाती है. ये दवा उन मरीजों के लिए बहुत जरूरी है जिन्हें हार्ट अटैक का खतरा होता है.. लेकिन इसके सैंपल में एस्प्रिन की मात्रा ही कम पाई गई.
इस लिस्ट में एंटी एलर्जिक दवा फेक्सो फेनाडाइन हाईड्रो क्लोराइड टैबलेट भी है. इसके सैंपल की जांच में ये पाया गया है कि ये दवा तय मानकों के हिसाब से शरीर में नहीं घुल रही है.
ऑक्सीटोसिन इंजेक्शन का एक सैंपल भी इसीलिए फेल हो गया, क्योंकि ये कीटाणुओं से मुक्त नहीं पाया गया. ये दवा कितनी महत्वपूर्ण है, इसे ऐसे समझा जा सकता है कि इसे गर्भवती महिलाओं को डिलिवरी के वक्त दिया जाता है. राजस्थान के कोटा में इसी साल जून के महीने में नकली ऑक्सीटोसिन इंजेक्शन की वजह से 5 महिलाओं की मौत हो गई थी.
CDSCO की इस लिस्ट में और भी कई चीजें हैं, जिनका इस्तेमाल घर-घर में होता है. इस लिस्ट में Johnson's baby साबुन का नाम भी है. क्योंकि इसके सैंपल में धूल-मिट्टी के कण पाए गए हैं. मेडिकल यूज वाले कॉटन के कई सैंपल इसीलिए फेल हो गए क्योंकि उसमें धूल और मिट्टी के कण पाए गए. टांका देने वाले धागे का सैंपल भी इसीलिए फेल हो गया क्योंकि उसमें कलर मिलाया हुआ था.
ये सैंपल फेल तो हो गए, लेकिन एक सवाल उठता है कि ये तो सिर्फ सैंपल थे. इसी बैच की दवाइयां बाजार तक पहुंच भी चुकी होंगी. कई दवाइयां बड़े अस्पतालों की सप्लाई चेन में चली गई होंगी. लोगों ने इसे मेडिकल शॉप से खरीदकर खा भी लिया होगा. ये दवाइयां इतनी आम हैं कि ये अंदाजा लगाना मुश्किल है कि कितने लोगों ने मिलावटी दवा खाई और कितनों ने शुद्ध.
भारत में सालाना पैरासिटामोल की 500 करोड़ टैबलेट्स की बिक्री होती है.
एजिथ्रोमाइसिन की करीब 60 करोड़ डोज सालाना खपत होती है.
एक अनुमान के मुताबिक देश में करीब 3 करोड़ लोग एस्पिरिन खाते हैं.
इसीलिए, आपको ये भी जानना चाहिए कि अगर कोई व्यक्ति इस तरह के मिलावटी और अशुद्ध दवाइयों का सेवन करता है, तो इसका परिणाम क्या होगा?
खराब क्वालिटी वाली दवाओं की लिस्ट हर साल जारी होती है. आपको देखना चाहिए कि हर साल कितने सैंपल फेल होते हैं.
2020 से लेकर अब तक जारी हुई लिस्ट को जब हमने डिकोड किया, तो एक बेहद परेशान करने वाला आंकड़ा सामने आया है. पिछले पांस सालों में सबसे ज्यादा एंटीबायोटिक्स के 523 सैंपल फेल हुए हैं. इसके बाद 516 ऐसी दवाइयों के सैंपल फेल हए जो गैस्ट्रोनॉमिकल दवाओं की कैटेगरी में आते हैं. जैसे पेट दर्द और एसिडिटी की दवाएं. ये सैंपल्स किसी खास कंपनी के नहीं थे.. लगभग हर बड़ी छोटी कंपनी के सैंपल लिए जाते हैं.. और फेल होने वाले सैंपल में हर तरह के नाम होते हैं. ऐसे में सवाल तो ये उठता है कि इसे रोका क्यों नहीं जा रहा है. मामला आम आदमी की सेहत से जुड़ा हुआ है तो कोई ठोस एक्शन क्यों नहीं लिया जा रहा है.
जितनी हानिकारक नकली दवाइयां होती हैं. उतनी ही खतरनाक मिलावटी दवाइयां भी हो सकती हैं. इसीलिए ये सवाल पूछा जाना चाहिए कि मिलावटी या नकली दवाओं के सैंपल जब फेल होते हैं, तो उस दवा कंपनी पर क्या एक्शन होता है.. अभी तक कितनी कंपनियों के खिलाफ एक्शन लिया गया है.
यानी मिलावटी और नकली दवा बेचने वालों के खिलाफ नियम तो कड़े बनाए गए हैं, लेकिन सवाल उठता है कि इन नियमों को कितनी बार लागू कर के किसी कंपनी के खिलाफ ठोस कार्रवाई की गई है.
6 फरवरी 2026 को लोकसभा में सरकार से सवाल पूछा गया था कि 2020 से 2025 तक नकली या मिलावटी दवाएं बेचने वाली कितनी कंपनियों के लाइसेंस सस्पेंड या रद्द किए गए हैं.. जवाब में ये बताया गया कि 3,056 आपराधिक मुकदमे शुरू हुए हैं, लेकिन ये आंकड़ा कहीं उपलब्ध नहीं है कि इन मुकदमों के बाद कितनी कंपनियों पर एक्शन हुआ है. कुछ अन्य रिपोर्ट्स में ये जानकारी मिलती है कि मार्च 2023 में 18 और अगस्त 2023 में 66 कंपनियों के लाइसेंस रद्द किए गए थे.
अगर दवाइयां लोगों की बीमारी ठीक करती हैं, तो मिलावटी या नकली दवाइयां बीमार भी कर सकती हैं. ऐसे में नकली और मिलावटी दवाओं के खिलाफ एक्शन को और सख्त करने की जरूरत है. ताकि, कोई भी कंपनी दवा में मिलावट करने से पहले इसके खिलाफ होने वाली कार्रवाई के बारे में सोच कर ही कांप उठे.

title: क्या पहलगाम आतंकी हमले से पहले चीन ने की थी जासूसी? सैटेलाइट विवाद पर विदेश मंत्रालय ने तोड़ी चुप्पी
description: क्या पहलगाम आतंकी हमले से पहले चीनी सैटेलाइट्स ने संदिग्ध हलचल की थी? अंतरिक्ष निगरानी रिपोर्ट से जुड़े दावों और सैटेलाइट विवाद पर जानिए क्या है तथ्यात्मक स्थिति और विदेश मंत्रालय का रुख.
author: रवींद्र प्रताप सिंह
content:
पहलगाम आतंकी हमले से ठीक पहले चीनी सैटेलाइट की कथित जासूसी और संदिग्ध गतिविधियों को लेकर उठ रहे सवालों पर अब भारत सरकार ने अपनी चुप्पी तोड़ी है. विदेश मंत्रालय ने इस बेहद संवेदनशील मामले पर प्रतिक्रिया देते हुए साफ किया है कि सरकार को इस तरह की मीडिया रिपोर्ट्स और इनपुट्स की पूरी जानकारी है. हम ऐसी खबरों पर नजर बनाए हुए हैं और सुरक्षा के लिहाज से इस मामले में कदम उठा रहे हैं.
मंत्रालय के मुताबिक, सीमा पार या अंतरिक्ष से होने वाली ऐसी किसी भी गतिविधि पर भारतीय एजेंसियों की पैनी नजर हमेशा बनी रहती है. सरकार ने देशवासियों को आश्वस्त करते हुए कहा है कि जब भी राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा से जुड़ा ऐसा कोई मामला सामने आता है, तो उसका गंभीरता से आकलन किया जाता है और देश की संप्रभुता व सुरक्षा के लिहाज से हर जरूरी और ठोस कदम समय रहते उठाए जाते हैं. इस बयान से साफ है कि भारत किसी भी तरह की बाहरी निगरानी को हल्के में नहीं ले रहा है.
Bi-weekly Media Briefing by the Official Spokesperson (November 25, 2026) https://t.co/VCKF15IRzX
— Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) November 25, 2026
पहलगाम हमले से पहले चीनी सेटेलाइट के जरिए संभावित निगरानी की खबरों पर विदेश मंत्रालय ने साफ रुख रखा है. मंत्रालय के मुताबिक, इस तरह की रिपोर्ट्स प्रशासन की जानकारी में आई हैं. जब भी संवेदनशील गतिविधियों या निगरानी से जुड़ी कोई बात सामने आती है, तो सरकार की उस पर पैनी नजर रहती है और देश की सुरक्षा को ध्यान में रखते हुए जरूरी कदम उठाए जाते हैं. सीमा और रणनीतिक क्षेत्रों से जुड़ी हर हलचल का आकलन लगातार किया जाता है ताकि किसी भी चूक की गुंजाइश न रहे.
सौरभ दास के पासपोर्ट से जुड़े मामले में भी विदेश मंत्रालय ने स्थिति स्पष्ट की है. उनके पासपोर्ट को फिलहाल रोकने या जमा कराने के पीछे एक तय प्रक्रिया है. मंत्रालय का कहना है कि उनसे कुछ जरूरी जानकारियां मांगी गई हैं और इसके लिए उन्हें नोटिस भेजा गया है. जब तक मांगी गई जानकारी नहीं मिल जाती, तब तक उनसे पासपोर्ट जमा रखने को कहा गया है. यह कदम तय नियमों और जांच प्रक्रिया का हिस्सा बताया गया है.
दूसरी ओर, भारत और चीन के बीच सीमा से जुड़े मुद्दों पर राजनयिक और सैन्य स्तर पर संवाद जारी है. हालिया बातचीत में इस बात पर जोर दिया गया कि वास्तविक नियंत्रण रेखा यानी बॉर्डर पर स्थिति को कैसे और बेहतर ढंग से संभाला जाए. दोनों पक्षों के बीच तालमेल बढ़ाने और जमीनी स्तर पर व्यवस्था सुधारने को लेकर चर्चा हुई है, ताकि सीमा प्रबंधन अधिक प्रभावी और व्यवस्थित रह सके.

title: Delhi High Court Allows Taj Mahal Photographers To Work Beyond 65, Strikes Down ASI's Age-Based Retirement Rule
description: The Delhi High Court has struck down the ASI's 65-year retirement limit for licensed Taj Mahal photographers, allowing them to continue working subject to medical fitness requirements and other conditions.
author: Asian News International
content:
Delhi High Court Allows Taj Mahal Photographers To Work Beyond 65, Strikes Down ASI's Age-Based Retirement Rule
The Delhi High Court has struck down the ASI's 65-year retirement limit for licensed Taj Mahal photographers, allowing them to continue working subject to medical fitness requirements and other conditions.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has quashed the Archaeological Survey of India’s (ASI) policy fixing 65 years as the retirement age for licensed photographers working at the Taj Mahal, holding that the restriction is discriminatory and adversely affects their right to livelihood.
A division bench of Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Dinesh Bhatt observed that the photographers are independent professionals and not employees of the ASI. They should be allowed to continue their profession as long as their physical and mental faculties permit them to perform their duties.
The court observed that when the Supreme Court had struck down a similar age restriction for tourist guides, there was even less justification for imposing such a restriction on photographers, whose work involves considerably less physical exertion.
“These are self-employed persons, who ought to be permitted to work as long as their physical and mental faculties permit,” the bench observed.
Advertisement
The court was hearing two petitions filed by photographers challenging Clauses 9 and 9.3 of the ASI’s policy dated May 24, 2017, which prescribed medical fitness requirements after the age of 60 and fixed 65 years as the retirement age for licensed photographers working at centrally protected monuments.
The petitioners submitted that photography at the Taj Mahal was their sole source of livelihood and that several of them had been providing services at the monument for the last 30 to 40 years. They argued that the age restriction would deprive them and their families of their only source of income.
Advertisement
Opposing the petitions, the ASI argued that fixing an upper age limit was necessary to provide opportunities to younger photographers. It submitted that around 500 photographers were currently licensed to work at the Taj Mahal and that allowing older photographers to continue could restrict opportunities for younger professionals.
The authorities also raised concerns that some licensed photographers were sending nominees to the monument to provide photography services instead of performing the work themselves. They further submitted that some older photographers might not be sufficiently familiar with technological advancements in photography.
The High Court relied on the Supreme Court’s judgment in B.P. Sharma v. Union of India, in which a similar age restriction imposed on tourist guides had been struck down.
The bench noted that under Rule 8(d) of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Rules, 1959, both photographers and tourist guides are required to obtain licences from the ASI to provide services within protected monuments.
It observed that tourist guides are required to accompany visitors and move around monuments, which may involve considerable physical exertion. Photographers, however, generally remain stationed at particular locations within the monument and provide their services there.
“The reasoning adopted by the Supreme Court in B.P. Sharma would, therefore, apply with greater force to the case of the Petitioners,” the court observed.
The bench further noted that with increasing life expectancy, professionals above the age of 65 can remain physically and mentally capable of performing their work. It also observed that the experience gained by photographers from working at the monument for several decades could be an advantage for tourists and visitors.
The court clarified that the ASI was entitled to require photographers to undergo medical fitness tests and furnish certificates from registered medical practitioners.
It held that the ASI could not curtail their livelihood merely on the ground that they had crossed the age of 65, subject to their meeting the prescribed fitness requirements.
While quashing the age restriction, the High Court also addressed the ASI’s concerns regarding licensed photographers allowing nominees to work in their place.
The court directed that no licensed photographer would be permitted to allow another person to use their licence or sub-license it in any manner. If any photographer was found doing so, the licence would be liable to be withdrawn with immediate effect.
The bench further directed that photographers would be required to undertake refresher courses conducted by the ASI to upgrade their skills and ensure quality services to tourists.
If the ASI conducts any test for photographers, the petitioners would also be required to appear in and qualify the same.
The court clarified that nominees already permitted under earlier court orders could continue only in cases involving licence holders with disabilities. No such permission would be granted to nominees of licence holders without disabilities.
The ASI was also permitted to conduct physical fitness tests or medical examinations of photographers after they attain the age of 65.
Subject to these conditions, the bench quashed Clause 9.3 of the 2017 policy prescribing 65 years as the retirement age for photographers.
It directed that the licences of the petitioners, which were stated to have been renewed to date, would be renewed for the remainder of the current year and thereafter on an annual basis.

50-Year-Old Software Engineer Found Dead in Parked Car in Hyderabad
According to a police official, “A 50-year-old software engineer, Parchuri Sudhee, a native of Kondapur, was found dead in his parked car. His wife noticed him dead and informed police through 112 and filed a complaint. We have registered a case and are investigating the matter.”

title: Duliajan Triple Murder: Police Shoot Two Suspects During Escape Attempt in Assam; Two Cops Injured
description: Confirming the police firing and the injuries sustained by the accused, Dibrugarh Additional Superintendent of Police Nirmal Ghosh said, “In connection with a triple murder in Duliajan, the police opened fire on two suspects, Raju and Amir.
author: Asian News International
content:
Duliajan Triple Murder: Police Shoot Two Suspects During Escape Attempt in Assam; Two Cops Injured
Confirming the police firing and the injuries sustained by the accused, Dibrugarh Additional Superintendent of Police Nirmal Ghosh said, “In connection with a triple murder in Duliajan, the police opened fire on two suspects, Raju and Amir.
- India News
- 2 min read
Dibrugarh: Two suspects linked to a triple murder case after the pair allegedly attacked officers and attempted to flee during a night search operation, police said. The police team had taken suspects to a tea garden in the Duliajan area to trace the weapon used in the killings. During the operation, the duo allegedly overpowered the escorting personnel and tried to escape under the cover of darkness.
Confirming the police firing and the injuries sustained by the accused, Dibrugarh Additional Superintendent of Police Nirmal Ghosh said, “In connection with a triple murder in Duliajan, the police opened fire on two suspects, Raju and Amir. Both individuals sustained gunshot wounds to their legs during the police operation.”
Detailing how the escape bid unfolded at the recovery site, Ghosh stated, “A police team had taken the two suspects to the Balijan Tea Estate in Duliajan in search of the primary weapon used in the murders. Around 11:00 PM, during the search operation, the suspects allegedly overpowered the accompanying police personnel and attempted to escape by taking advantage of the darkness.”
Advertisement
The police fired multiple rounds to stop the fleeing suspects, hitting both men on their legs. Two police personnel were also hurt during the altercation and were taken to a nearby medical facility in Duliajan for treatment. Outlining the police retaliation, the medical treatment of the injured officers, and the status of the search, Ghosh added, “In response, the police fired a total of five rounds, four of which struck the suspects in their legs, Raju in his right leg and Amir in his left. Two police officers were also injured during the incident and received medical treatment at a hospital in Duliajan. The police are continuing their investigation, and efforts to recover the primary weapon used in the crime are ongoing.” Further investigation is underway.
