title: Ujani Dam Data Centre Faces Protests from Farmers and Fisherfolk
description: Farmers and fisherfolk oppose Maharashtra’s proposed AI data centre near Ujani Dam over threats to land, water, livelihoods and power supply.
author: Gautam  Nirmal Doshi
content:
“Whoever is against the construction of the AI data centre, please raise your hands,” came an announcement around 11:30 am on November 13 during a Gram Sabha held in Ranzani village in Maharashtra’s Solapur district, by the banks of the Bhima river. Every villager present, young and old, including onlooking children, raised their hands in unison. “The AI data centre and all remaining projects should be cancelled,” said many.
Villagers from Ranzani, the neighbouring Hingangaon village on the other side of Bhima, and the Bhimanagar area that surrounds the Ujani Dam, which holds the 337 square kilometre Ujani Reservoir, are all opposing the proposed construction of not only a 1.4 gigawatt (GW) hyperscale data centre but also a 2 GW floating solar power project and a 1.8 GW Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The plans for all these were finalised without consulting farmers, fishermen, and other residents.
The projects are a scaled-down version of initial plans that included a green hydrogen plant and a small modular reactor (SMR) nuclear project. After public backlash and citing feasibility concerns, District Collector S. Karthikeyan announced the cancellation of two of the five projects on November 4. The projects are public-private partnerships (PPP) between the State government’s Water Resources Department, JW Global, and The SEED Consortium Partners, with an initial projected investment of Rs.1.65 lakh crore. The 1.4 GW hyperscale data centre represents almost 70 per cent of this investment.
The projects are envisioned under the banner of making the area a “Sustainable Eco-Enterprise District” or SEED, using 568.15 hectares of land on either side of the Bhima river. It envisages the creation of 40,000 temporary jobs and 2,800 permanent jobs. With almost all local farmers and fishermen unequivocally against the project, fearing its harmful effects on the environment, the question that arises is: who is the development for?
With the mask of decarbonisation initiatives amid rising power and water-centric burdens of data centres adding to the other concerns around data centres, it begs the question why such projects are being implemented in agricultural and fishing areas where livelihoods of entire villages are at stake.
In Maharashtra, this is the second uproar against a data centre, the first being at Thane, where residents are opposing the upcoming 400-plus MW data centre in Balkum.
Speaking at a press conference on November 4, Karthikeyan announced that “not a single guntha of land of farmers will be acquired for the project”. He added: “There will be no compulsory land acquisition. Whatever land is with Maharashtra’s irrigation department, only that will be used. It will be given to the MIDC, which will then tie up with the private company.”
On the concern that some of the land proposed for the projects was farming land, Karthikeyan said: “We’re not going to evict or destroy farms and start the project. We will work out a fair compensation with the farmers.” He said that over 112 hectares (of the 586 hectares required for the project) are currently used by around 70 farmers.
Speaking to Frontline, farmers spoke of how their parents or grandparents had given up land some 50 years ago for the construction of the Ujani Dam. “My family gave up several acres for the Ujani Dam. A lot of that land is unutilised, so as per the law, shouldn’t we get it back?” said Vishwas Shahurao Deokar, a farmer from Hingangaon.
Deokar was referring to Section 101 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (or the LAPR Act, 2013), which states that “when any land acquired under this Act remains unutilised for a period of five years from the date of taking possession, the same shall be returned to the original owner or owners or their legal heirs, as the case may be, or to the land bank of the appropriate government by reversion in the manner as may be prescribed by the appropriate government”.
The land was acquired for building a dam, which is considered a public purpose. But the data centre, with the BESS and floating solar panels serving the data centre, are private ventures.
Colin Gonsalves, a senior advocate at the Supreme Court, said: “The data centre is not a public purpose. When the government acquires land for a public purpose, it must be utilised accordingly. The land vests with the government, so if they don’t use it for a dam and say they want to use it for another public purpose, like a public hospital, that would be permissible. But this data centre is not a public purpose.”
However, if the matter is escalated to the courts, there is a chance that it can be argued that the data centres are being used for a public purpose, Gonsalves added. This is because, in the Union Budget 2022-23, the government included data centres in the “Harmonised List of Infrastructure”, which treats them like national highways, airports, and power grids that have public purposes.
Also Read | A data centre mired in controversy
Even though there is no direct utilitarian benefit for farmers or fishermen, the data centres set up by private companies could be deemed to hold a public purpose, if questioned.
The farmers from Hingangaon said that they just want their land back. They wanted to know why the project could not come up on barren land and why it had to be near the Ujani Dam area. “We grow sugar cane, bananas, pomegranates, wheat, and more here. This is fertile land,” said Deokar. According to Karthikeyan, the area near the Ujani Dam was chosen because of its grid connectivity and proximity to a highway.
First phase and evictions
In August, several families in the Bhimanagar Government Colony, not far from the Ujani Dam, were served eviction notices on the grounds that they were occupying government land. The first phase of the project begins in Bhimanagar.
The families of Arifa Sikandar Pathan and Gauri Sunil Dosane (who are neighbours), with two and seven members respectively, have nowhere else to go. “They gave us notice to leave our homes in just five days. We were not told where to go, but were just told there is some area set aside within this village itself. We went to their [government’s] office and got an extension of six months,” Pathan said.
While many vacated their homes hurriedly, several such families are staying on, unsure what to do. “Soon after the notice, they shut off our water supply and electricity for 10-15 days. There’s a school here that was rebuilt less than a year ago. Where will these children go now?” said Dusane.
Vimal Gaikwad comes from Ranzani to farm on the land near the colony. “My family gave several acres for the construction of the project for barely any compensation because they were happy that the dam would benefit the entire community. And it did. But now why are they clearing trees and houses so swiftly? I have been here for over 50 years; I have all the documents about the acquisition,” she said.
A JCB earth mover stands parked near Pathan and Dusane’s homes, the modern symbol of upheaval. Adjacent lies almost an acre of cleared and deserted land. The land clearing was stopped after the public backlash. “There were many peacocks here; so many of them died when they came to cut the trees and clear the land,” said Vimal, who has been actively protesting the proposed projects.
When we reached the Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) in Indapur, along the Ujani Reservoir and near Pune’s district border with Solapur, people were leaving the bustling designated mandi where fishermen sell their freshwater catch. The reservoir has a diverse range of fish. Fisherfolk were wrapping up accounts and shutting shop. When asked, everyone Frontline spoke to was against the proposed floating solar power project.
The 2GW floating solar power plant will cover around 30 sq km, which accounts for 9 per cent of the Ujani Reservoir’s water.
Worried fisherfolk
Naseer Dawood Sheikh, a fisherman from Indapur, said: “This project will affect our livelihoods. Three generations of my family were fisherfolk. What else will we do? There are tens of thousands of us across both districts; we depend on fishing in the reservoir. And it’s not just fishermen; our entire villages depend on fish for sustenance. The government has so much land. Why don’t they take the solar plant elsewhere?”
A common concern was that, with 30 sq km cordoned off for the solar project, fishermen would be forced to fish in other areas, thus reducing everyone’s overall catch. (During his November 4 press conference, Karthikeyan claimed that fishing routes and breeding would not be affected, and that the solar project would be introduced in a phased manner.)
The fisherfolk who fish in the Ujani Reservoir have been protesting since August this year, also seeking the cancellation of a proposed private contract for fishing rights, which was cancelled in September. But the floating solar power project worries them.
Nandkumar Nagare, president of Maharashtra Rajya Machhimar Sangharsh Kruti Samiti, said: “Over 30,000 people are directly dependent on fishing; they have no other alternative. The solar power project and the data centre will increase the temperature in the surrounding land and water; besides, there will be the constant jarring noise of the data centre. People in the surrounding 4-5 villages will be forced to leave for good.”
Nagare was referring to the “data heat island effect”, a term coined by researchers. According to a paper led by Cambridge researchers, the land surface temperatures around AI data centres rise by an average of 2 degrees Celsius, with a peak limit up to 9 degrees Celsius as a result of heat dissipation. The heat can be felt up to 10 km away.
Fishermen like Kiran Mohandar Dare fear being displaced again, something his family dealt with during the construction of the Ujani Dam. “Earlier generations of my family were farmers. We had to give up our land and relocate. We switched to fishing. Now this. This project can be done elsewhere, not here.”
Water quality concerns
Next to Bhimanagar, a road running along a canal leads to its source. “All the greenery along this road will be destroyed,” said Kishore Sonawane, from Indapur, pointing to the numerous trees on either side of the road. It’s a hot November afternoon, and only one fisherman on a small boat is attempting a catch near the shore, with most others finishing before sunrise. The noise of water pumps dominates the soundscape and a faint but foul smell from the water is noticeable. This is another concern the fisherfolk share.
“The water is turning greener and it’s also dirty; we cannot use it for drinking or cooking. You can smell it,” said Pandurang Palare, a fisherman. The fishermen complained that this could be affecting the quality of fish as well. Farmers share the same concern. “We are noticing declines in our yield due to the water quality,” said Gyaneshwar Gaikwad, a farmer from Ranzani.
According to a paper published in 2023 in the Bulletin of Environment, Pharmacology, and Life Sciences, tests on water samples from 10 different locations in the Ujani Reservoir “showed horrendous physical condition issues and may lead to various diseases”.
This is primarily due to rapid urbanisation and the resultant discharge of untreated or partially treated domestic and industrial contaminants into the Mula and Mutha rivers, and the Mula-Mutha (the confluence of both rivers in Pune), which flow eastward for about 60 km before merging into the Bhima river, which flows into the Ujani Reservoir.
The paper concluded that the Ujani Reservoir’s water quality was “marred with high grade pollution. Hence, the Ujani water is not suitable for the household utilisation and also for agriculture without purification”.
“The authorities know the problems here. But no one cared to come here and help us improve the water quality all these years, and now everything is being handed over in a hurried manner to make the data centre,” farmers from Hingangaon told Frontline on November 13.
Water usage amid crisis
In his November 4 press conference, Karthikeyan also said that the total water to be utilised by the proposed facility and the adjacent campus, including the proposed residential areas, would not exceed 0.5 thousand million cubic feet (TMC), about roughly 14,150 million litres per year, which is less than 1 per cent of the reservoir’s capacity of 117 TMC.
“The floating solar power project will prevent the natural evaporation of 1.5-1.7 TMC of the reservoir’s water. Thereby, no additional water will be utilised and, in fact, there’s a net positive of 1-1.2 TMC for the reservoir,” he added.
He said that this was possible because of a newer direct-to-chip closed-loop dry cooling mechanism to be used, which reduces water consumption in a data centre compared to traditional methods of cooling through evaporation towers.
An annual usage of 14,150 million litres translates to 38-39 million litres a day, which is enough for 6.9 lakh people in rural areas or 2.8 lakh people in urban areas, as per the Central government’s benchmarks of 55 litres per capita per day (lpcd) for rural and 135 lpcd for urban populations.
Data centres need distilled or purified water for cooling purposes. However, farmers said that since the water is already polluted, the total water used will be higher than the stated 0.5 TMC. The data centre, they said, will need excess water to filter out the required 0.5 TMC for cooling and other purposes.
The Ujani Reservoir supplies water to the districts of Pune, Solapur, and Ahiliyanagar. The proposed data centre’s use of water has come under the spotlight also because this year, drought was declared in 305 of Maharashtra’s 358 talukas, including all 11 talukas in Solapur. Local news reports indicate that over 229 tankers were sent across 198 villages as of November 17, as roughly 4 lakh people faced severe water scarcity.
In late October, the Karnataka government sought the release of 7 TMC of water from the Ujani Dam for villages along the Bhima in Vijayapura district. However, that has not yet been granted. Given such concerns, farmers are vehemently opposed to a water-guzzling data centre. “We feel our villages will become like a desert. People will leave to look for different jobs,” said Sandip Maruti Mane, a farmer in Ranzani. “We have said time and time again that the entire village is against these projects; we have no option but to protest.”
Fears of energy deficit
The proposed 1,800 MW BESS stores power during surplus supply and helps meet excess demand during a supply deficit. BESS is one of the energy storage solutions being implemented across the country. Another is Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs). The Maharashtra government has ordered fast-tracked environmental clearances for 55 PSPs in the State, concentrated in and around the ecologically diverse Sahyadri range. In the last month, PSPs have come under the spotlight in Maharashtra with the proposed felling of over 32,000 trees for the construction of the Saidongar-I project in Karjat taluka. That project met with protests from villagers and opposition parties. Saidongar-I has been temporarily halted and uncertainty looms over its future as the project aims to clear 233 hectares of forest cover.
The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) projects 73.93 GW of storage capacity in the country by 2031-32. Of this, the PSPs will have a storage capacity of 26.69 GW, with BESS projects accounting for the remaining 47.24 GW.
The push for such storage solutions comes against the backdrop of rising electricity demands and increasing capacities through renewable sources, and to ensure grid stability.
For Maharashtra, specifically, it also comes against the backdrop of rising power cuts during the hotter months owing to demand surge and a lack of supply. In June this year, the Maharashtra State Load Despatch Centre reported load shedding for several hours at a stretch in places. The electricity shortfall was around 28 million units (MU), with the lack of generation accounting for 23 MU.
Farmers in Hingangaon, Ranzani, and Indapur in Pune district said that they get only six hours of electricity on their farms. “During summer, because of load shedding, there are days when we don’t get electricity at all and have to make do,” said Deokar. Some farmers said they get six hours of power every alternate day.
By the early 2030s, the State government plans to sanction 6 GW of power specifically to data centres in Maharashtra, approximately 15 per cent of the State’s entire power demand, assuming maximum demand reaches 40 GW (with current power demand being 30-32 GW and assuming a growth in demand at a CAGR of 4 per cent).
Also Read | Data centre push gets a drought reality check
Currently, connectivity amounting to 2 GW has been given to data centres, of which 200 MW is operational. A large number of data centres are being added in the State in a very short period of time, with the 1.4 GW data centre at Ujani the largest yet, and they are coming on an already burdened power grid.
“This is why we are introducing green data centres,” said Karthikeyan. “Around 50 per cent of the energy demand will be met by solar.”
But data centres work 24 hours; they require a constant power source and have to draw power from the grid itself using the existing high-voltage transmission network rather than connect directly to a solar/wind plant or microgrid. The solar panels also feed into the grid, but solar generation fluctuates.
The proposed projects guarantee 2,800 jobs and 40,000 temporary jobs, the latter primarily construction work. While Karthikeyan has listed various types of jobs ranging from IT and cybersecurity engineers to boat operators and solar panel cleaners, the farmers are doubtful about how villagers will benefit. Krishna Tate, a farmer and activist from Indapur, said: “The well-paid jobs are for AI, data, and IT engineers who will not be from these villages. People from outside will fill these vacancies.”
On November 14, Dhairyasheel Rajsinh Mohite-Patil of the Nationalist Congress Party-Sharad Pawar (NCP-SP), an MP from Madha constituency, under which the proposed projects fall, told mediapersons: “In my constituency and Indapur taluka, we have questions about the projects that remain unanswered. If we are not given an adequate response by the [District] Collector by November 26, we will hold a candlelight march on November 27 to the executive engineer’s office.”
Regardless of the government’s response, villagers are not ready to stop raising their voices against the planned projects, which were started without consulting them. “If the projects are not cancelled, we are ready to protest every day and also willing to put our lives on the line,” a group of 7-8 farmers told Frontline after the Gram Sabha in Ranzani.

title: Basava Mantapa controversy tests BJP and Congress ties with Lingayats
description: The Basavanna book controversy puts the Congress and BJP under pressure as both parties seek to retain the support of Karnataka’s Lingayat community.
author: Sujay B.M.
content:
The Karnataka Cabinet decided on Thursday, November 19, to forfeit Basava Mantapa, a Kannada book by the US-based writer Ravi Hanj, after Lingayat groups said it insulted Basavanna, the 12th-century social reformer and anti-caste crusader. Hanj was detained at Kochi airport in Keralam on Saturday, November 21, as he was about to leave the country.
The dominant Lingayat community, which considers Basavanna its ultimate leader, reacted strongly to the book, released on November 15, and to an interview Hanj gave to the YouTube channel of the Kannada daily Vishwavani. Basavanna is one of the foremost social reformers of Karnataka. In January 2024, the Congress-led State government declared him the State’s cultural icon. Police have registered FIRs against Hanj and the journalist and publisher Vishweshwar Bhat.
Days after the Cabinet decision, a notification forfeiting the book was passed. Forfeiture means that every copy of a book is declared to belong to the government, which can then seize it. Under Section 98 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, a State government can issue such a declaration by notification, stating its grounds, if a book appears to contain matter punishable under specified provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. These include promoting enmity between groups and deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings.
Once a book is declared forfeited, any police officer can seize copies wherever they are found in India, and a Magistrate can authorise a search of premises where copies are suspected to be held. The declaration can be challenged only before the High Court.
Posting on X, Home Minister Priyank Kharge accused Hanj of “distorting the history of Guru Basavanna and deeply hurting the sentiments of Kannadigas”. “He initially attempted to create the impression that he had left India for the United States. However, verification by the Home Department established that he was in a neighbouring State. He has been traced and a formal notice has been issued directing him to appear before the investigating authorities,” he added.
The book, which Frontline has accessed, accuses Basavanna of ambition and claims that “… Once Bijjala [Kalachuri king] started realising that Basavanna had placed his people in positions of power or once Basavanna opposed Bijjala, the stage of political polarisation to murder Bijjala and assume power started…”
It also claims that Basavanna died by suicide, which the Lingayat community contests. The book condemns the movement that seeks separate religion status for Lingayatism and personally attacks its leaders. In 2018, the Congress government led by Siddaramaiah recommended to the Union government that Lingayatism be granted separate religion status. The Narendra Modi-led Union government rejected the recommendation. The BJP and conservative sections had accused the Congress of “dividing” Hindu society. It also argues that untouchability was not prevalent in ancient Indian society and emerged only as a reaction to the arrival of Islamic rulers.
The book compiles articles Hanj wrote for Vishwavani, which Bhat heads. Hanj, a Kannadiga, has settled in the US and taken American citizenship. In the interview, Hanj cited a famous vachana (a Kannada devotional verse) of Basavanna, Kalabeda kolabeda husiya nudiyalu beda (Do not steal, do not murder, do not lie), as an example of Basavanna’s contradictions, accusing him of indulging in the very acts he condemned in the verse. Hanj has since apologised for his comments.
Political reactions
Criticising it at a press conference, Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil of the Congress, who is a Lingayat, said: “A man named Ravi Hanj has referred to a great vachana by Basavanna [Kala Beda Kola Beda] and has [directed it to] Basavanna himself. He is a criminal… This is not limited to one Ravi Hanj. There are many such people. It started with Kondi Manchanna in the 12th century. There have been several Kondi Manchannas over 800 years. They cannot tolerate Basavanna, the Basava Dharma and those vachanas.”
Speaking to Frontline, Congress MLA B.R. Patil, a veteran Lohiaite, or follower of the socialist leader Ram Manohar Lohia, said: “Such books are attempts by people who don’t believe in the casteless, egalitarian principles and equal society espoused by Basavanna. Whenever an opponent cannot be defeated with ideas, people resort to such personal slander and vilification. Such slanders are not confined to Basavanna but are happening with Gandhi, Ambedkar and Karl Marx as well.”
The situation is trickier for the BJP. Bhat is widely considered close to the RSS and its affiliates, and the controversy caught the party off guard. On the defensive, BJP leaders have condemned the book too. Prominent Lingayat leaders in the BJP, such as former Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa and his son, State president B.Y. Vijayendra, have expressed displeasure with the book.
Speaking to Frontline, the BJP MLA Arvind Bellad, who is Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and also a Lingayat, criticised Hanj’s comments on Basavanna. “Ravi Hanj is mad. Does anyone speak that way about Basavanna? Earlier, I have also read his articles on Vishwavani. Just because he has some literary skills, can he say whatever he wants? He is against the egalitarian principles of Basavanna that fought against untouchability. Our community [Veerashaiva Lingayats] stands on the concepts of the vachanas. Naturally the community is hurt by this controversy.”
Bellad agreed with the Congress-led State government’s decision to forfeit the book. “Such people who vitiate peace in the society must be arrested and placed before bars.” Much of civil society has condemned the book, though some scholars say banning a book is undemocratic. Others feel the line between freedom of expression and hate speech, which disturbs public tranquillity, is thin.
Fissures in the Mahasabha
The controversy has also set off a clash within the All India Veerashaiva Lingayat Mahasabha, the apex body of the Veerashaiva Lingayat community. Community leaders have criticised the Mahasabha’s State president, Shankar Bidari, a former DGP of Karnataka, and Manu Baligar, a former president of the Kannada Sahitya Parishat, for attending the book launch.
In a letter to Eshwar Khandre, the Mahasabha’s All India president and Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister, M.T. Subhash Chandra, a vice patron of the Mahasabha, urged that Bidari be suspended as State president. “Participating in the book launch of Basava Mantapa, Bidari has not only praised the anti-Basava author of the book Ravi Hanj but also congratulated him on behalf of the Mahasabha. This is a treason against the Mahasabha… Before more damage happens from such a person, I urge you to suspend Shankar Bidari,” the letter added.
Apart from the forfeiture, the letter sought legal action against Vishwavani and Bhat.
Many parts of Hanj’s book are in tune with the Hindutva ideology of the Sangh Parivar, but the BJP cannot afford to antagonise the Lingayats, its most significant support base.
Since the decline of the Janata Dal (United) in Karnataka, the BJP has drawn substantial support from the Lingayat community. The BJP has never won a simple majority on its own (113 of the 224 seats in the Karnataka Legislative Assembly). It won 110 seats in 2008 and 104 in 2018, and later assumed power through “Operation Lotus”, which drew opposition MLAs to its fold.
On both occasions, the Lingayat community was perceived as the BJP’s main support base. Yediyurappa is widely seen as the tallest Lingayat leader of the present day. Forcing him to make way for Basavaraj Bommai as Chief Minister in 2021 is widely perceived as one of the reasons for the BJP’s defeat in the 2023 Assembly election.
Though the BJP got the largest share of Lingayat votes even in 2023, a marginal shift of Lingayats towards the Congress, coupled with other developments, helped the Congress win 135 seats, with 42.88 per cent of the votes against the BJP’s 36 per cent.
The Lingayat community, dominant in north and central Karnataka with pockets of presence in the south, was believed to make up over 15 per cent of the State’s population. However, the socio-economic and educational survey report submitted in 2024 by the Backward Classes Commission under K. Jayaprakash Hegde estimated the community at 11.09 per cent. The community rejected the figure as “undercounting” of its numbers. The Siddaramaiah-led government set the report aside in June 2025.
Even at the lower estimate, the community’s social and political capital keeps it central to the State’s politics. Since Yediyurappa’s political retirement, there has been a leadership vacuum in the Lingayat community across parties. Vijayendra, though the BJP’s State president, is yet to become a universally accepted leader within the party.
The Congress is watching the situation closely and trying to win over the community. The State government’s quick action in forfeiting the book and detaining Hanj could help it make inroads. A senior Veerashaiva Lingayat Mahasabha leader told Frontline that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, though a Vokkaliga (a land-owning community dominant in south Karnataka), was trying to win over the community. “Since Shivakumar became the chief minister, he has taken decisions in favour of Lingayats. The decision to forfeit the book is a major one. He has also appointed five Lingayats as vice chancellors of various universities. He is trying to win over the support of the community. Lingayats do not insist on only supporting leaders from their caste. Even in the past, former Chief Minister Ramakrishna Hegde [Brahmin] was widely trusted and supported by Lingayats.”
The regional Janata Dal (Secular), an alliance partner of the BJP, has little stake in the contest for Lingayat votes, since it is seen as a party that rests mainly on Vokkaliga support and is confined to south Karnataka.
How the two national parties handle the controversy, and the Lingayat community, will bear on their electoral prospects in the 2028 Assembly election.

title: Why is Wall Street bleeding? $1.5 trillion-plus market value wiped out as AI bubble fears, inflation and Trump’s tariffs rattle investors
description: Wall Street is bleeding as Trump's tariff threats collide with stubborn inflation, rising interest-rate expectations and growing doubts over whether the AI boom can deliver the astronomical profits investors have priced in. | OpIndia News
author: Jinit Jain
content:
The US stock market is witnessing a generational drawdown. On Wednesday, November 25, it witnessed one of its sharpest sell-offs in recent months, with technology stocks bearing the brunt of an investor exodus. More than $1.5 trillion in market value was at risk of being wiped out from the Nasdaq-100 as a combination of renewed trade tensions, stubborn inflation, growing doubts over the artificial intelligence boom and uncertainty over Federal Reserve policy spooked investors.
The Nasdaq Composite plunged 4.15%, shedding nearly 986 points to trade at 22,747.61 during Wednesday’s session. The Nasdaq-100 fell 4.3%, while the S&P 500 declined 2.86% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.99%. The technology-led sell-off was particularly brutal, with Nvidia losing around 8.6%, Alphabet falling 5%, Amazon declining 4.9% and Microsoft shedding 3.2%.
Intriguingly, equities were not the only asset class to face the heat. Gold and Silver also came under heavy selling pressure. Spot Gold fell more than 2%, while Silver declined 3.8%, as a stronger US dollar and expectations of further interest rate hikes weighed on precious metals.
The market turmoil is being driven by several developments converging at the same time. While Trump’s fresh tariff proposals have provided the latest trigger, the underlying problems run considerably deeper.
1. Trump’s tariff war is back, and investors are getting nervous
The immediate trigger for the latest sell-off is Washington’s decision to propose fresh tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including India, China, Japan, South Korea and the European Union.
The Trump administration has proposed tariffs of up to 25% on imports from India and additional duties of up to 20% on several other economies. China faces a proposed additional 20% levy as Washington accuses Beijing of flooding international markets with cheap manufactured goods.
The measures follow an eight-month investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act into what the US describes as structural excess industrial capacity among its trading partners.
The problem for investors is that tariffs introduce another layer of uncertainty into an already complicated economic environment.
American companies depend heavily on international supply chains. Fresh import duties could increase the cost of raw materials, components and finished products, putting pressure on corporate profit margins. Businesses could either absorb these costs or pass them on to consumers, potentially creating another round of inflationary pressure.
There is also the possibility of retaliatory measures from affected trading partners. Companies operating across multiple international markets could find themselves dealing with higher costs, disrupted supply chains and unpredictable trade policies.
The tariffs have only been proposed and are not yet implemented. However, financial markets rarely wait for policies to take effect before pricing in their potential consequences.
2. Inflation refuses to cool, putting the Federal Reserve in a difficult position
Another major reason behind the market’s weakness is persistent inflation in the United States.
Data released on Wednesday showed that the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, increased 3.8% year-on-year in October, up from 3.6% in September.
Core PCE inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, climbed to 3.3% from 3.1% in September. The monthly increase was 0.3%.
This is significant because the Federal Reserve has a 2% inflation target. Inflation running considerably above that level makes it difficult for the central bank to justify cutting interest rates.
In fact, expectations have shifted towards further monetary tightening, with investors increasingly pricing in at least a 25-basis-point rate hike before the end of 2026.
The problem for Wall Street is that higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and reduce the present value of future corporate earnings. This particularly hurts technology companies whose valuations depend heavily on profits expected several years down the line.
There is another complication. The US economy grew at an annualised rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, considerably higher than the 3.5% economists had expected.
While strong economic growth is ordinarily positive for businesses, it complicates the Federal Reserve’s inflation-fighting efforts when price pressures remain elevated. The central bank has less reason to ease monetary policy when economic activity remains robust and inflation is not approaching its target.
Investors who were hoping for cheaper borrowing costs are consequently reassessing their expectations. The prospect of higher rates for longer is particularly bad news for expensive technology stocks.
3. The AI boom is facing its biggest reality check yet
Perhaps the most significant underlying reason behind Wall Street’s troubles is the growing realisation that the artificial intelligence boom may not deliver the returns investors have been expecting.
For much of the past two years, AI has been the biggest driving force behind the US stock market rally. Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and other technology giants have attracted enormous investor interest on the promise that artificial intelligence will transform businesses and generate extraordinary profits.
However, the market is increasingly questioning whether the enormous investments being made in AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.
Technology companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars building data centres, purchasing advanced processors, expanding computing capacity and securing energy supplies. This expenditure has fuelled unprecedented demand for semiconductor manufacturers and companies supplying AI infrastructure.
But building infrastructure is not the same as generating profits from it.
Investors want to know when these investments will translate into sustainable revenue and earnings. They are also questioning whether the current pace of capital expenditure is financially justified, particularly when companies are increasingly relying on borrowing to fund their expansion.
The sell-off is not limited to chip manufacturers. Companies operating data centres and providing specialised AI computing capacity are also facing pressure.
CoreWeave and Nebius, two companies exposed to the AI infrastructure boom, suffered steep share-price declines. CoreWeave’s bonds also came under significant pressure, with yields on its 2031 debt approaching 18%.
This is an important warning sign. When investors begin questioning not only the valuations of AI companies but also their ability to finance expansion, the repercussions can spread across the entire technology ecosystem.
The semiconductor index has already suffered a substantial correction, falling more than 43% from its June record high. Nvidia, the biggest symbol of the AI boom, has also been at the centre of the latest market turmoil.
This does not necessarily mean artificial intelligence is a passing fad or that demand for AI technology has disappeared. It does, however, suggest that investors are no longer willing to assign unlimited valuations to companies merely because they are associated with AI.
The market wants profitability, not just promises.
4. Excessive valuations and the unwinding of the AI trade
Another problem is that Wall Street had become heavily dependent on a relatively small group of technology companies.
A handful of mega-cap stocks, particularly those associated with artificial intelligence, account for a substantial share of the market’s value and influence major indices such as the Nasdaq-100 and S&P 500.
When these companies rally, the indices rise disproportionately. But the reverse is equally true. When investors begin selling these stocks, the damage spreads across the broader market.
The volatility surrounding Nvidia illustrates this problem.
The company witnessed a spectacular rally on Monday after Jensen Huang returned as its CEO, providing temporary relief to investors. However, the euphoria did not last. Nvidia shares subsequently reversed sharply, falling around 6% on Tuesday and another 8.6% on Wednesday.
The episode illustrates how sentiment-driven the AI trade has become. Investors are willing to aggressively buy shares on positive developments, but they are equally quick to exit when doubts resurface.
There are also concerns about the valuations attached to companies that have benefited enormously from the AI narrative without yet demonstrating that their infrastructure investments will generate commensurate returns.
When expectations become excessively high, even strong earnings or improved revenue forecasts may not be enough to satisfy investors.
The result is a market increasingly vulnerable to profit-booking and sudden corrections.
5. Regulatory uncertainty is adding another layer of pressure
The political environment is also changing the outlook for technology companies.
The Democratic Party’s gains in the November midterm elections have raised concerns among investors about potentially tougher scrutiny of the AI industry.
Regulatory restrictions, additional compliance requirements and hurdles to building large data centres could slow down infrastructure expansion.
This matters because the current AI investment cycle depends on companies being able to construct data centres rapidly, secure electricity and deploy increasingly powerful computing infrastructure.
Any regulatory intervention or delay could affect the projected returns on investments running into hundreds of billions of dollars.
Investors are consequently assessing whether the scale and speed of AI infrastructure expansion can be sustained under a potentially more challenging regulatory environment.
6. Even Gold and Silver are falling as investors seek liquidity
The simultaneous decline in Gold and Silver is another interesting feature of the current market turmoil.
Gold is traditionally considered a safe-haven asset, but it is not immune to selling pressure when investors anticipate higher interest rates and a stronger dollar.
The US inflation numbers have reinforced expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. Higher interest rates make non-yielding assets such as Gold less attractive compared with interest-bearing investments.
There is also another possible explanation. During sharp market corrections, investors facing losses in equities may sell profitable or liquid positions in other asset classes to meet margin calls and raise cash.
Silver has faced additional pressure because of its industrial demand exposure.
The decline in precious metals alongside equities therefore reflects more than just a conventional flight away from risk. It also highlights how aggressively investors are reassessing monetary policy expectations and liquidity requirements.
Is this the beginning of a bigger market correction?
The latest sell-off is not an isolated event caused exclusively by Trump’s tariff announcement. Wall Street has been struggling for several weeks as investors reassess technology valuations, inflation expectations and the sustainability of the AI investment cycle.
The Nasdaq-100 briefly touched the threshold of 20% below its October 6 record closing high on Wednesday. A closing level at that threshold would confirm a bear market in the index.
The combination of sticky inflation, potentially higher interest rates, renewed trade tensions and doubts over AI profitability has created an uncomfortable environment for investors.
What makes the situation particularly interesting is that none of these developments, individually, necessarily signals the end of the US economic or technology growth story.
The US economy is still expanding, companies continue to invest heavily in artificial intelligence, and demand for advanced computing infrastructure remains substantial.
However, financial markets operate on expectations. When investors begin questioning whether those expectations have become unrealistic, valuations can correct sharply even when the underlying businesses continue to grow.
That is precisely what Wall Street appears to be experiencing right now.
The AI boom is here to stay. The chips used to power the AI boom are selling at a record pace. All metrics suggest the AI is yet to reach its peak. But the recent correction in the markets, particularly the slump in Anthropic shares, suggest we are well past the time when AI companies got a free pass in commanding unrealistic valuations. We are now, perhaps, entering from the realm of imagination to reality.

title: 15 दिसंबर से पहले बुलाया जा सकता है संसद सत्र, पीएम मोदी ने मंत्रियों को दी विदेश यात्रा न करने की सलाह
description: सूत्रों ने समाचार एजेंसी पीटीआई को बताया कि प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने 15 दिसंबर से पहले संसद का सत्र बुलाने का संकेत दिया।
author: जनसत्ता न्यूज डेस्क
content:
प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने अपने मंत्रिमंडल के सहयोगियों को 15 दिसंबर से पहले संसद के अगले सत्र की तैयारियां पूरी करने का सुझाव दिया है। उन्होंने मंत्रियों को सत्र से पहले विदेश यात्रा नहीं करने की सलाह भी दी है। इससे संकेत मिलता है कि सरकार चाहती है कि मंत्री इस दौरान उपलब्ध रहें। मामले की जानकारी रखने वाले सूत्रों ने बताया कि बुधवार को पीएम मोदी की अध्यक्षता में हुई केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल की बैठक में संसद के अगले सत्र का मुद्दा भी उठा।
सूत्रों ने समाचार एजेंसी पीटीआई को बताया कि प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने 15 दिसंबर से पहले संसद का सत्र बुलाने का संकेत दिया। उन्होंने कहा कि संसदीय मामलों की मंत्रिमंडलीय समिति सत्र शुरू होने की तारीख और उसकी अवधि को अंतिम रूप देगी। पीएम मोदी ने सत्र की तैयारियों की जरूरत पर जोर देते हुए मंत्रियों से अपने-अपने मंत्रालयों को आगामी सत्र के लिए तैयार रखने को कहा। बुधवार रात तक संसद का मानसून खत्म नहीं हुआ है। दोनों सदनों की बैठक 13 अगस्त को अनिश्चितकाल के लिए स्थगित किए जाने के 103 दिन बाद भी सत्र के खत्म होने की घोषणा नहीं की गई है।
विपक्षी दलों का क्या है रुख?
संसद का शीतकालीन सत्र बुलाने में देरी को लेकर विपक्ष के लगातार सवालों के बीच इन घटनाक्रमों को महत्वपूर्ण माना जा रहा है। विपक्षी दलों ने कहा है कि मानसून सत्र स्थगित हुए 100 से अधिक दिन बीत चुके हैं, लेकिन अब तक सदन का सत्र खत्म नहीं किया गया है। इस देरी से संसद का विशेष सत्र बुलाए जाने की अटकलें तेज हो गई हैं। यह चर्चा खास तौर पर लोकसभा और विधानसभा क्षेत्रों के प्रस्तावित परिसीमन के संदर्भ में हो रही है।
संसद का अगला सत्र 15 दिसंबर से पहले होने की संभावना के बीच सबकी नजर इस बात पर है कि क्या सरकार परिसीमन से जुड़े महिला आरक्षण विधेयक को पेश करेगी। हालांकि, इस महत्वपूर्ण संविधान संशोधन विधेयक को पारित कराने के लिए जरूरी संख्या जुटाना सरकार के लिए चुनौतीपूर्ण हो सकता है। वर्तमान 543 सदस्यीय लोकसभा में इस विधेयक को पारित कराने के लिए दो-तिहाई बहुमत यानी 361 सदस्यों के समर्थन की आवश्यकता होगी। तीन सीट रिक्त होने के कारण लोकसभा में फिलहाल 540 सदस्य हैं। सत्तारूढ़ एनडीए गठबंधन के पास 320 सदस्य हैं और दो-तिहाई बहुमत का आंकड़ा पार करने के लिए उसे विपक्षी दलों के समर्थन की जरूरत होगी।
NDA के पास कितना नंबर?
अप्रैल में लोकसभा में विधेयक के गिर जाने के बाद से राजनीतिक समीकरण बदल गए हैं और 26 सांसद विपक्षी खेमे से अलग हो गए हैं। तृणमूल कांग्रेस के 20 बागी सांसदों ने पार्टी से अलग होकर नेशनलिस्ट सिटीजन्स पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया (NPCI) में विलय कर लिया और राजग को समर्थन देने का भरोसा दिया। वहीं, शिवसेना (यूबीटी) के छह सांसद एकनाथ शिंदे के नेतृत्व वाली शिवसेना में शामिल हो गए। इन घटनाक्रमों से सरकार की स्थिति मजबूत हुई है, लेकिन इसके बावजूद उसे अतिरिक्त समर्थन की जरूरत होगी।
लोकसभा में 22 सदस्यों वाली डीएमके और आठ सदस्यों वाली राष्ट्रवादी कांग्रेस पार्टी (शरदचंद्र पवार) बदलते राजनीतिक समीकरणों में अहम भूमिका निभा सकती हैं। राजनीतिक चुनौती केवल संख्या जुटाने तक सीमित नहीं है। विपक्षी दलों ने मतदाता सूचियों के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) के खिलाफ अपना अभियान तेज कर दिया है और मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग की है। ऐसे में विपक्षी दल संसद में भी अपना विरोध जारी रख सकते हैं, जिससे आगामी सत्र में फिर हंगामे के आसार हैं।
सत्तारूढ़ गठबंधन के एक सांसद ने कहा कि जब तक सदन सुचारू रूप से नहीं चलेगा, तब तक संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पर चर्चा और मतदान संभव नहीं होगा। मौजूदा सत्र को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए कम से कम दो दिन पहले सूचना देना जरूरी है, जबकि नया सत्र बुलाने के लिए कम से कम 14 दिन पहले सूचना देनी होती है। सरकार ऐसे एक फार्मूले पर विचार कर रही है, जिसके तहत परिसीमन के प्रभावों को लेकर, खासकर दक्षिणी राज्यों की चिंताओं को दूर करने के लिए, सभी राज्यों में लोकसभा सीट की संख्या 50 प्रतिशत बढ़ाई जाएगी। प्रस्तावित रूपरेखा में 1971 की जनगणना के आधार पर राज्यों के बीच सीट का मौजूदा अनुपात भी बरकरार रखने की बात है, हालांकि इस पर अभी कोई अंतिम निर्णय नहीं लिया गया है।
यह भी पढ़ें: ‘जब पासपोर्ट के लिए आवेदन करते हैं, तो…’, सौरव दास को UK जाने से रोके जाने पर विदेश मंत्रालय ने दिया जवाब
कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के सह-संयोजक और प्रवक्ता सौरव दास को ब्रिटेन जाने से रोके जाने को लेकर विदेश मंत्रालय ने अपना जवाब दिया है। विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता रणधीर जायसवाल ने कहा, “कानून लागू करने वाली एजेंसियों से मिली रिपोर्ट के आधार पर, RPO चेन्नई ने 23 नवंबर 2026 को सौरव दास को एक ‘शो-कॉज नोटिस’ (कारण बताओ नोटिस) जारी किया है।” पूरी खबर पढ़ने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें

title: ‘इमरान मसूद से बड़ी है कांग्रेस…’, सपा सांसद इकरा हसन बोलीं- मैं उनके प्रति सहानुभूति रखती हूं
description: कांग्रेस का कहना है कि वह यूपी की 403 सीटों में से 100 सीटों से कम पर समझौता नहीं करेगी, जबकि सपा का कहना है कि सीट समझौता केवल जीत की संभावना के आधार पर होना चाहिए।
author: असद रहमान
content:
उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा चुनावों के लिए कांग्रेस और समाजवादी पार्टी के बीच सीट बंटवारे को लेकर खींचतान मची हुई है। दोनों सहयोगी दलों के बीच तीखी नोकझोंक देखने को मिली है। मंगलवार रात को इन वार्ताओं के बीच एसपी द्वारा पांच उम्मीदवारों के नाम घोषित किए जाने पर यूपी कांग्रेस के कार्यकारी अध्यक्ष इमरान मसूद ने तीखी प्रतिक्रिया दी। कांग्रेस का कहना है कि वह यूपी की 403 सीटों में से 100 सीटों से कम पर समझौता नहीं करेगी, जबकि सपा का कहना है कि सीट समझौता केवल जीत की संभावना के आधार पर होना चाहिए।
द इंडियन एक्सप्रेस को दिए एक इंटरव्यू में 32 वर्षीय सपा सांसद चौधरी इकरा हसन ने इन वार्ताओं से जुड़े कई मुद्दों पर बात की, जिनमें कांग्रेस के लिए उनकी पार्टी का फॉर्मूला और इमरान मसूद की टिप्पणियां शामिल हैं। इकरा यूपी की कैराना लोकसभा सीट से सांसद हैं।
सवाल: कांग्रेस के साथ सीट बंटवारे की वार्ता अब तक कैसी रही है? कांग्रेस ने आरोप लगाया है कि सपा ने मीडिया को जानकारी लीक की है।
जवाब: उनके पास इस बात का कोई पुख्ता सबूत नहीं है कि हमने कोई सूची लीक की है। सबसे पहले उन्होंने ही 181 सीटों की अपनी सूची लीक की, जो उन्होंने हमें दी थी। फिर सोमवार को उन्होंने 131 सीटों की सूची लीक की, और साथ ही उन 26 सीटों की सूची भी लीक की जो हम उन्हें देने को तैयार थे। मेरी समझ से कांग्रेस में ऐसे लोग ज्यादा हैं जिन्हें सार्वजनिक बयान देना पसंद है। दूसरी ओर, हम एक बहुत ही अनुशासित पार्टी हैं और हमारा नेतृत्व हमें अनावश्यक बयानबाजी करने से रोकता है।
सवाल: क्या आप बता सकती हैं कि कांग्रेस क्या मांग कर रही है?
जवाब: सबसे पहली बात जो हमने उनसे कही वह यह थी कि जिन सीटों पर हमारे मौजूदा विधायक हैं, उन पर कोई बातचीत नहीं होगी। उनकी पहली मांग यह थी कि हम 2022 के विधानसभा चुनावों को इन चुनावों का मापदंड न मानें। हमने इसे स्वीकार कर लिया। हम 2024 के लोकसभा चुनावों और उनके प्रदर्शन के आधार पर सीटों का विश्लेषण करने के लिए तैयार हैं। इसे ध्यान में रखते हुए, हमारी उनसे यही अपील है कि 2022 के चुनाव सबसे हालिया विधानसभा चुनाव थे और जब तक हम 2022 के नतीजों का विश्लेषण नहीं करते और यह नहीं समझते कि 2022 में हम इतनी सीटें क्यों हारे, तब तक हम उन सीटों को दोबारा नहीं जीत पाएंगे और सरकार नहीं बना पाएंगे। हमारे और उनके लिए यह जरूरी है कि हम 2022 के चुनावों पर आत्ममंथन करें।
सवाल: मंगलवार रात को SP ने UP चुनावों के लिए पांच उम्मीदवारों की एक सूची जारी की। कांग्रेस का कहना है कि SP ने उनसे सलाह लिए बिना एकतरफा तरीके से ऐसा किया। इस पर आपकी क्या प्रतिक्रिया है?
जवाब: यह एकतरफा नहीं था। सबसे पहले, हमने उन्हें 26 सीटों की एक सूची दी, जो हम उन्हें देने के लिए तैयार थे। उसके बाद ही हमने अपने पांच उम्मीदवारों की सूची जारी की। ये वे सीटें थीं, जहां हम बड़े अंतर से जीते हैं और जहां हमारे मौजूदा विधायक हैं। हमने उन्हें साफ बता दिया है कि जिन सीटों पर हमारे मौजूदा विधायक हैं, वहां हम कोई समझौता नहीं करेंगे। हम कांग्रेस का स्वागत करते हैं कि वे हमारे साथ बैठें और सभी सीटों पर चर्चा करें। हमने कोई ऊपरी या निचली सीमा तय नहीं की है। उन्हें बस हमें यह यकीन दिलाना होगा कि वे जो सीटें मांग रहे हैं, उन पर वे जीत हासिल कर सकते हैं।
सवाल: इमरान मसूद, जो सीट बंटवारे की बातचीत के लिए कांग्रेस की टीम का हिस्सा हैं, वह नाराज हैं और कह रहे हैं कि हम भिखारी नहीं हैं। उनके इस बयान को आप कैसे देखते हैं?
जवाब: मुझे लगता है कि कांग्रेस पार्टी इमरान मसूद से बड़ी है। गठबंधन भी इमरान मसूद से बड़ा है। मैं उनके प्रति सहानुभूति रखती हूं, क्योंकि एक नेता के तौर पर अगर मुझे अपने निर्वाचन क्षेत्र से कुछ सीटें छोड़नी पड़ें, तो इससे अगले चुनाव के लिए मेरे समीकरण बिगड़ जाते हैं। लेकिन कोई भी गठबंधन किसी व्यक्ति के अहंकार और उसकी महत्वाकांक्षाओं से बड़ा होता है। यह पहली बार नहीं है जब उन्होंने (मसूद ने) गैर-जिम्मेदाराना बयान दिए हैं। वे एक साल से भी ज्यादा समय से ऐसा कर रहे हैं। कांग्रेस को अपने सदस्यों को अनुशासित करने की जरूरत है, और अभी बातचीत पूरी भी नहीं हुई है। सिर्फ इसलिए कि किसी एक व्यक्ति का अहंकार आहत हुआ है, इसका मतलब यह नहीं है कि गठबंधन कमजोर हो गया है।
सवाल: कांग्रेस के उत्तर प्रदेश प्रभारी राजेंद्र पाल गौतम ने कहा है कि कांग्रेस 100 सीटों से कम पर समझौता नहीं करेगी। क्या यह संभव है?
जवाब: हमें सीटों की कोई ऊपरी या निचली सीमा तय करने का निर्देश नहीं दिया गया है। हम चर्चा के लिए तैयार हैं। एकमात्र शर्त यह है कि हम इस चुनाव को लेकर बेहद गंभीर हैं। यह हमारे लिए करो या मरो की स्थिति है। हो सकता है कांग्रेस 2029 के लोकसभा चुनावों पर नजर रख रही हो। लेकिन 2029 के चुनावों का रास्ता इन उत्तर प्रदेश चुनावों से ही तय होगा। हमने केंद्र स्तर पर सभी मुद्दों पर कांग्रेस का समर्थन किया है। हम उनके सबसे बड़े सहयोगी हैं। हमने उन मुद्दों पर भी उनका साथ दिया है जो हमारे लिए कम और उनके लिए ज्यादा मायने रखते हैं। और अब जब हमारे लिए दांव ऊंचे हैं, तो हम उनसे इस विधानसभा चुनाव के लिए भी इसी तरह की प्रतिबद्धता और गंभीरता की उम्मीद करते हैं। हम उन्हें सीटें नहीं दे सकते ताकि वे यहां अपना कैडर बना सकें। यह चुनाव हमारे लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है।

title: ‘सहमत या असहमत होने का डेटा नहीं’, सीएम योगी के वोटर लिस्ट से ‘हिंदुओं के नाम कटने’ के दावे पर बोले यूपी के मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त
description: उत्तर प्रदेश के मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी नवदीप रिणवा ने इंडियन एक्सप्रेस हिंदी से बात की।
author: जनसत्ता न्यूज डेस्क
content:
उत्तर प्रदेश में विधानसभा चुनाव की तैयारी चल रही है। स्पेशल इंटेंसिव रिवीजन (SIR) के बाद ड्राफ्ट वोटर लिस्ट भी जारी हो गई है। हालांकि अभी भी लोगों को आपत्तियां दर्ज कराने का समय दिया गया है। इस बीच उत्तर प्रदेश के मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी नवदीप रिणवा ने इंडियन एक्सप्रेस हिंदी से बात की। उन्होंने मुख्यमंत्री योगी आदित्यनाथ के उस दावे पर भी जवाब दिया, जिसमें उन्होंने कहा था कि 1 करोड़ 27 लाख हिंदुओं के नाम मतदाता सूची से कट गए हैं। पढ़िए पूरी बातचीत
सवाल: कौन सही है? उत्तर प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्री योगी आदित्यनाथ या उत्तर प्रदेश का चुनाव आयोग? क्या राज्य चुनाव आयोग ने मुख्यमंत्री को धर्म-वार आंकड़े दिए हैं?
जवाब: हमारे पास धर्म को लेकर ऐसा कोई आंकड़ा नहीं है। आपने पूछा कि क्या मुख्यमंत्री सच बोल रहे हैं? उत्तर प्रदेश चुनाव आयोग की ओर से मैंने कहा है कि उत्तर प्रदेश में लगभग 25 लाख लोग मतदाता सूची में शामिल होने के योग्य हैं, लेकिन उनके नाम सूची में नहीं हैं। लेकिन मैं यह नहीं बता सकता कि उनमें से कितने हिंदू हैं, कितने मुसलमान हैं, कितने सिख हैं, कितने ईसाई हैं या वे किस जाति से हैं। क्योंकि हमारे पास जो डेटाबेस है, उसका विश्लेषण लिंग, आयु आदि के आधार पर किया जा सकता है, लेकिन हमारे पास धर्म या जाति के आंकड़े नहीं हैं। मतदाता सूची में शामिल होने के लिए भरे जाने वाले फॉर्म 6 में धर्म या जाति का कोई कॉलम नहीं है। आप कहते हैं कि उन्होंने (मुख्यमंत्री ने) हम पर आरोप लगाया। मैंने उनकी बात सुनी। मुझे नहीं लगता कि उन्होंने चुनाव आयोग पर आरोप लगाया। उन्होंने नाम हटाने की बात नहीं की।
सवाल: सीएम ने पूछा कि वे नाम कैसे गायब हुए और इसके पीछे कौन है। वह आपराधिक साजिश की ओर इशारा कर रहा है।
जवाब: नहीं, नहीं… वे 2.5 करोड़ नाम इसलिए गायब हैं क्योंकि किसी व्यक्ति का नाम मतदाता सूची में तभी जोड़ा जा सकता है जब वह फॉर्म भरकर और अपने हस्ताक्षर या अंगूठे का निशान लगाकर पहला कदम उठाए। यदि व्यक्ति यह कदम नहीं उठाता है, तो भले ही हमें पता हो कि कितने लोग मतदाता सूची से बाहर हैं, हम किसी का नाम जबरदस्ती नहीं जोड़ सकते। हमारा प्रयास है कि चल रहे SSR के दौरान प्रत्येक व्यक्ति तक पहुंचे और उन्हें बताएं कि वे अपना नाम मतदाता सूची में जुड़वा सकते हैं। इसके लिए बहुत अधिक दस्तावेज़ों की आवश्यकता नहीं होगी। 99.99% लोगों के पास आधार कार्ड है। आधार कार्ड पर जन्मतिथि और पता पर्याप्त प्रमाण हैं।
सवाल: संभव है कि किसी राजनीतिक दल के सक्रिय एजेंटों ने मतदाता सूची से नाम हटवा दिए हों?
जवाब: हमें ऐसी शिकायत सबसे पहले 31 जनवरी को मिली थी। 8 फरवरी को हमने एक प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस आयोजित की और आंकड़े साझा किए। हाल ही में एक समाचार पोर्टल ने हमारी वेबसाइट पर जारी किए गए आंकड़ों का विश्लेषण किया और पाया कि इन प्रयासों के कारण मतदाता सूची से 114-115 से अधिक नाम नहीं हटाए गए थे। फॉर्म 6 भरवाने के बाद उनके नाम अब वापस सूची में शामिल कर दिए गए हैं। संबंधित अधिकारियों को कारण बताओ नोटिस जारी कर दिए गए हैं।
सवाल: मुख्यमंत्री कुछ ऐसे दावे कर रहे हैं जिनसे आप सहमत नहीं हैं। क्या राज्य चुनाव आयोग ने मुख्यमंत्री को पत्र लिखकर उनके दावे का आधार पूछा है, क्योंकि उनकी टिप्पणियां चुनाव आयोग की छवि को धूमिल करती हैं?
जवाब: मुझे लगता है कि यह गलत व्याख्या है। मैं कह रहा हूं कि मेरे पास मुख्यमंत्री के बयान से सहमत या असहमत होने के लिए पर्याप्त आंकड़े नहीं हैं। मुख्यमंत्री टिप्पणी कर सकते हैं, अखिलेश यादव टिप्पणी कर सकते हैं, आप भी कर सकते हैं, क्योंकि भारत एक लोकतंत्र है। मुझे नहीं लगता कि वे चुनाव आयोग पर सवाल उठा रहे हैं। इसके लिए जिम्मेदार वे लोग हो सकते हैं जिन्होंने फॉर्म नहीं भरा या किसी राजनीतिक दल के सदस्य हो सकते हैं।
सवाल: अगर मुख्यमंत्री योगी आदित्यनाथ चाहे और बहुमत वाली सरकार सत्ता में है, तो क्या वे ऐसा कानून ला सकते हैं कि उत्तर प्रदेश में पंचायत और नगरपालिका चुनावों में भारतीय निर्वाचन आयोग की मतदाता सूची का इस्तेमाल किया जाए?
जवाब: विधानसभा के पास यह अधिकार है।
सवाल: क्या कोई दबाव है? आप एक सेवारत आईएएस अधिकारी हैं। क्या आपको लगता है कि आप नैतिक रुख अपना रहे हैं, लेकिन इस कार्यकाल के समाप्त होने के बाद मुख्यमंत्री ही आपकी अगली पोस्टिंग तय करेंगे?

title: Comedian Yash Maheshwari booked over Chhath remarks
description: Stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari has been booked in Patna for allegedly making indecent remarks about women observing Chhath Puja in Bihar. The case was registered after his 'Morally Questionable' video went viral, leading to a public apology from Maheshwari.
author: Senjo M R
content:
Stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari faces legal action in Patna after his "Morally Questionable" video, containing alleged indecent remarks about women observing Chhath Puja, sparked widespread controversy and led to a police case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and IT Act.
Key Points
- A case was registered against stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari in Patna on Tuesday for alleged indecent remarks about women observing Chhath.
- The controversy stemmed from his YouTube video, 'Morally Questionable', where he purportedly made sexually explicit comments regarding women's vermilion application during Chhath Puja.
- Police stated the remarks could harm women's dignity, disrupt social harmony, and cause law-and-order issues.
- The FIR was lodged under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Information Technology Act.
- Maheshwari has since issued a public apology, admitting that his remarks were inappropriate.
A case was registered against stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari in Patna over his alleged indecent remarks about women observing Chhath in Bihar, the police said on Wednesday.
Controversial Remarks Spark Legal Action
The case was lodged at the Cyber Police Station on Tuesday, according to a statement.
The alleged remarks could hurt the dignity of women, disturb social harmony among communities and trigger law-and-order problems, the statement said.
The FIR has been registered under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Information Technology Act, it added.
The controversy erupted after his stand-up comedy video, titled 'Morally Questionable', on YouTube went viral. In the video, Maheshwari purportedly made sexually explicit remarks about women in Bihar applying long streaks of vermilion on their foreheads during Chhath Puja.
Facing backlash, Maheshwari issued a public apology, admitting that his remarks were inappropriate.

title: Bisleri row: FSSAI launches nationwide packaged water quality checks
description: India's food regulator, FSSAI, has initiated a nationwide collection and testing drive for packaged drinking water samples, with results expected in one to two months. This move follows the sanctioning of prosecution against Bisleri International after one of its samples failed quality tests. FSSAI asserts the drive is part of its broader consumer safety efforts and aims to ensure compliance rather than create panic among consumers.
author: Senjo M R
content:
India's food safety watchdog, FSSAI, has launched a comprehensive nationwide drive to test packaged drinking water quality, intensifying scrutiny across the country following a recent prosecution sanction against Bisleri International for unsafe samples.
Key Points
- FSSAI is conducting a nationwide drive to collect and test packaged drinking water samples, with results anticipated in one to two months.
- The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a sample of its packaged drinking water was found unsafe due to non-compliant bromate limits and polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
- FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani stated on Wednesday that the enforcement activities are aimed at ensuring compliance and safeguarding consumer interests, not creating panic.
- The current drive is part of FSSAI's ongoing efforts, which in the last year have covered dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, and various beverages.
- FSSAI has urged food companies to comply with regulations, set up in-house testing, and avoid misleading claims on labels and advertisements.
Food regulator FSSAI is collecting packaged drinking water samples across the country, and their lab testing for quality will be completed in one to two months, its CEO Rajit Punhani said on Wednesday, while asserting that enforcement activities are to ensure compliance and not create panic.
Nationwide Quality Check Underway
He said the regulator, in the past year, has undertaken enforcement activities for many food as well as beverage products, and added that it would soon start inspection of 'packaging materials' used for food items.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test. The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International.
According to sources, the FSSAI has written to state food commissioners and its regional directors to step up surveillance, inspection and sampling of 'Packaged Drinking Water and Mineral Water'. It also asked them to take action against companies in case of non-compliance.
When asked about its enforcement drive against packaged drinking water, Punhani said, "We are in the process. The process has started. We are doing it all over the country."
On the timeline for results, he said, "It's a very big country. So I think it will take at least a month or two."
The CEO said the drive on packaged drinking water is not for any particular reason but part of the FSSAI efforts to safeguard consumers' interests by ensuring safe food.
"There is no particular reason. If you notice, in the last year, we have taken up, one by one, a lot of things. We have done dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, and sugary drinks. Water is also part of that process," he told reporters on the sidelines of a CII event.
Punhani highlighted that FSSAI has taken action against misleading advertisements as well as claims on labelling of food products.
Bisleri Prosecution Details Emerge
Asked about when the regulator will start legal process against Bisleri International, Punhani said it is a "normal routine thing, and it will happen".
On Sunday, through a social media post, FSSAI informed that it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water".
A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis.
"The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator had said.
Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added.
The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law.
On Monday, Bisleri International asserted that its packaged drinking water is "safe" for consumption, and it will cooperate with the food regulator to address the issue.
FSSAI Urges Industry Compliance
Sending out a strong message, the FSSAI CEO said the regulator's enforcement actions against companies are not meant to spread panic but to ensure compliance with the law.
He asked food companies to fully comply with FSSAI regulations and suggested they set up in-house testing mechanisms to ensure high product quality.
He told Food Business Operators (FBOs) and e-commerce companies to ensure there are no misleading claims on product labels and no misleading advertisements.
In its letter to state food commissioners,the FSSAI said that the details of inspections, samples lifted and corresponding test reports should be recorded in the Food Safety Compliance System (FoSCoS) to facilitate effective monitoring and periodic review.
Regulatory Framework for Packaged Water
In November 2024, FSSAI classified packaged drinking water and mineral water under 'High-Risk Food Categories'. This order was issued after omitting the mandatory Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) certification requirement for 'packaged drinking water and mineral water'.
FSSAI prescribed a testing scheme for 'packaged drinking water and mineral water' in December 2025.

title: Police Probe Firing Incident In North Delhi's Lahori Gate
description: A 20-year-old man was injured in north Delhi's Lahori Gate area after being hit by a bullet during a firing incident that followed an altercation between a group of boys. The victim is stable and undergoing treatment, while police are investigating the cause of the dispute and working to identify those involved.
author: Text Feed
content:
A 20-year-old man was injured in a firing incident in north Delhi's Lahori Gate area on Wednesday night following a group altercation, prompting a police investigation into the unknown motive and unidentified shooter.
Key Points
- A 20-year-old man sustained a bullet injury to his toe during a firing incident in north Delhi's Lahori Gate area on Wednesday night.
- The incident occurred following an altercation between a group of boys, though the reason for the dispute remains unknown.
- The injured man is currently undergoing treatment at LNJP Hospital and is reported to be in stable condition.
- Police are actively investigating the incident, examining CCTV footage, questioning locals, and have called a forensic team to collect evidence.
A 20-year-old man was injured after a bullet hit his toe during a firing incident following an altercation between a group of boys in north Delhi's Lahori Gate area, police said.
Investigation Underway In Lahori Gate
The man was rushed to Lok Nayak Jai Prakash (LNJP) Hospital, where he is undergoing treatment. His condition is stable, police added.
According to preliminary investigation, police received a PCR call regarding the firing in Fatehpuri on Wednesday night. A police team rushed to the spot and found that an altercation broke out between a group of boys, during which a round was fired, and a person sustained injuries.
Police are yet to ascertain the reason behind the altercation and identify the person who fired the shot.
Teams are working to identify those involved, while CCTV footage from the area is being examined and locals are being questioned, police said.
A forensic team was also called to the spot to collect evidence. Further investigation is underway.

title: Farmers To Stage Protest At Sanchi Dairy HQ On Nov 26 In Indore
description: Farmers and labourers under the Samyukt Kisan Morcha will stage a protest at Sanchi Dairy headquarters in Indore on November 26. Their demands include a legal MSP guarantee, complete loan waiver, higher milk prices, electricity bill waivers and drought-hit status for Indore district. Protesters will also demand measures to prevent crop damage by wild animals.
author: Staff Reporter
content:
Indore (Madhya Pradesh): Farmers and labourers under the banner of the Samyukt Kisan Morcha will stage a sit-in protest at the Sanchi Milk Dairy headquarters in Talawali Chanda on Nov 26 at 11 am, as part of a nationwide agitation to press for their demands.
The protest will raise several national-level demands, including a law guaranteeing minimum support price (MSP), fixing crop prices based on the C2 cost of production recommended by the Swaminathan Commission, complete loan waiver for farmers and repeal of all four labour codes.
The protesters will also highlight issues concerning farmers in Indore district. Their local demands include payment of Rs 12 per fat for milk supplied to Sanchi Dairy, a bonus of Rs 5 per litre as announced by the chief minister, declaring Indore district drought-hit and waiving farmers' electricity bills.
They will also seek measures to prevent crop damage caused by wild 'nilgai' (blue bulls) and wild boars.
Farmer leaders said rising input costs, inadequate crop prices, natural challenges and damage caused by wild animals had worsened farmers' difficulties. Representatives of various farmers' and labourers' organisations, including Ram Swaroop Mantri, Bablu Jadhav, Chandan Singh Barwalia and Arun Chauhan, will participate in the protest. They have appealed to farmers and labourers to join the demonstration in large numbers.

title: E-Attendance: Deos Warn Of Salary Cuts Despite DPI Assurance Against Withholding Pay In Bhopal
description: Government school teachers and employees face confusion over e-attendance after district and block officials in Shivpuri and Bhopal’s Phanda block threatened to withhold salaries for non-compliance, contradicting Department of Public Instruction assurances against pay cuts. Cluster principals were ordered to verify digital records on IFMIS.
author: Staff Reporter
content:
Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): Government school teachers and employees are facing confusion over e-attendance, with district-level education officials issuing warnings of salary withholding for failure to mark attendance digitally, even as the Department of Public Instruction (DPI) has reportedly instructed that salaries should not be withheld on this ground.
Despite the state-level directions, orders issued by district and block education offices have created uncertainty among employees over whether their salaries can be stopped for failing to record 100% e-attendance.
The issue has come into focus following a video conference held by senior officials on Nov 23, after which district authorities began issuing instructions to ensure complete implementation of the digital attendance system.
The officials have directed cluster principals to review attendance daily, verify records and ensure necessary corrections in the Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) software before forwarding salary-related details. Principals have been asked to submit monthly certificates confirming that salary payments have been properly verified.
In Shivpuri, the district education officer (DEO) issued a warning letter to all block education officers (BEOs), stating that salaries of government employees who fail to ensure 100% e-attendance will be withheld and that the employees concerned will be responsible for the action.
Similarly, in Bhopal s Phanda development block, the block education officer issued directions to all cluster principals to process employees salaries on the basis of verified e-attendance. The order instructed principals not to recommend salary withdrawal for employees who had not registered their e-attendance. It further directed that cases requiring salary withholding must be reported to the BEO office.

title: Mumbai Crime Branch Busts Alleged Cyber Fraud Bank Account Racket In Dharavi; 2 Arrested
description: Mumbai Crime Branch Unit 8 arrested two people after raiding a Dharavi premises allegedly used to procure and activate bank accounts and SIM cards for online gaming and cyber fraud. Police seized ATM cards, SIM cards, banking documents, identity papers and account records. Investigation is ongoing.
author: Poonam Apraj
content:
Mumbai, November 25, 2026: The Mumbai Crime Branch's Unit 8 has busted an alleged bank account racket being operated from Dharavi, where bank accounts and SIM cards were allegedly procured, activated and supplied for use in online gaming and cyber fraud. Two accused have been arrested in connection with the case. The accused have been identified as Wasim Javed Khan and Sagar.
Acting on a tip-off received by Police Inspector Sawant, a team from Unit 8 conducted a raid at Room No. 1, ground floor, Nehru Society Old Building, near V.M. Thevar Marg, Thevar Nagar, Dharavi, on November 14. The main accused, Wasim Javed Khan (36), was found inside the premises along with his wife, Rubina Khan.
Police Recover ATM Cards And SIMs
During a search of the house, the police recovered 33 ATM cards belonging to different banks, 23 ATM cards with SIM cards attached to them, 32 loose SIM cards and two memory cards.
The police also seized a mobile phone, three bank passbooks, three cheque books, loose cheques, six bank letters, photocopies of identity documents belonging to 12 individuals, a bank account-opening form, and a notebook and diary containing details of bank accounts.
According to the police, the accused allegedly procured details of newly opened savings and current accounts in different banks in Mumbai, along with SIM cards.
These SIM cards were allegedly used to activate the bank accounts before the accounts were handed over to other persons for further use. The police suspect that these bank accounts were subsequently used for online gaming activities and cyber fraud.
Banking Documents Seized
The seizure included ATM cards and banking documents belonging to several banks, including CSB Bank, DCB Bank and Bombay Mercantile Co-operative Bank, among others.
The police have alleged that Wasim Javed Khan and another accused, identified as Sagar, conspired to procure bank accounts and SIM cards from different individuals and make them available for online gaming and cyber fraud activities.
Also Watch:
Based on a complaint filed by Unit 8, a case has been registered at Dharavi Police Station under Sections 318(4) (cheating) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Further investigation is underway.

Latur News in Marathi: लातूर जिल्हा महाराष्ट्र राज्यातील मराठवाडा विभागातील एक जिल्हा आहे (Latur News). लातूर शहर हे जिल्ह्याचे मुख्यालय असून महाराष्ट्र राज्यातील १६ व्या क्रमांकाचे मोठे शहर आहे. लातूरचा प्राचीन इतिहास आहे (Latest Latur News). हे राष्ट्रकूटांचे घर होते आणि ते अशोकच्या साम्राज्याचा भाग होते. शतकानुशतके सातवाहन, शक, चालुक्य, देवगिरीचे यादव, दिल्लीच्या सुलतान, दक्षिण भारतातील बहामनी शासक, आदिल शाही आणि मुघल यांच्याद्वारे शासन केले (Latur Crime). १९व्या शतकात ते हैदराबादच्या स्वतंत्र संस्थानाच्या राज्याचे भाग बनले. पूर्वी १९०५ मध्ये नळदुर्ग तहसील म्हणून ओळखले जाणारे हे आसपासच्या परिसरात विलीन झाले आणि त्यांचे नाव लातूर तहसील असे करण्यात आले नंतर ते उस्मानाबाद जिल्ह्याचे भाग बनले. स्वातंत्र्य मिळाल्यानंतर हैदराबादचा विलय, उस्मानाबाद हा बॉम्बे प्रांतचा हिस्सा बनला. १९६० मध्ये महाराष्ट्र निर्माण झाल्याने ते एक जिल्हा बनले. १५ ऑगस्ट १९८२ रोजी लातूरला उस्मानाबादपासून वेगळे केले व लातूर जिल्हा स्वतंत्र करण्यात आला. लातूरचा संपूर्ण जिल्हा बालाघाट पठारावर आहे. मांजरा ही जिल्ह्यातील प्रमुख नदी आहे, जी बालाघाट पठारावरील उपनद्यांसह (तेरना, तावरजा आणि घर्नी) वाहते.

title: नांदेड
description: Nanded Marathi News: मराठवाड्यातील नांदेड हे ऐतिहासिक ठिकाण आहे (Nanded News) . हे गोदावरी नदीच्या उत्तरेस वसलेले आहे. हे शीख गुरुद्वारासाठी प्रसिद्ध आहे. नांदेड हे पुरातन वास्तू असलेले शहर आहे (Latest Nanded News). असे म्हटले जाते की पौराणिक दिवसात पांडव नांदेड जिल्ह्यातून प्रवास करत असत ( Nanded Crime News). नंदांनी नांदेडवर पिढ्यान्पिढ्या राज्य केले. नांदेड हे मराठवाड्यातील दुसरे मोठे शहर. शैक्षणिक हब अशी देखील नांदेड शहराची ओळख आहे. छत्रपती संभाजीनगरनंतर नांदेड हे रोजगारासाठी महत्वाचे शहर आहे. नांदेडचा उल्लेख ‘लीलाचरित्र’ या महिम्भट्टाने लिहिलेला ग्रंथ आढळतो (Nanded Weather). यात शहरातील नरसिंहच्या मूर्तीचे वर्णन आहे. नांदेड पूर्वी “नंदीतट” म्हणून ओळखले जात असे वाशिम येथे सापडलेल्या तांब्याच्या प्लेटद्वारे याची पुष्टी केली जाते.

description: बीबीसी संवाददाता मोहन लाल शर्मा ने बात की राजीव गांधी हत्याकांड की प्रत्यक्षदर्शी नीना गोपाल, हत्याकांड की जांच करने वाले पूर्व आईपीएस अधिकारी आमोद कंठ और इस घटना की जांच पर किताब लिखने वाले लेखक-पत्रकार अनिरुद्ध मित्रा से.
author: BBC News हिंदी
content:
एक कैमरे ने कैसे खोला राजीव गांधी हत्याकांड का राज़
सोनिया गांधी की किताब 'बिलॉन्गिंग्स: अ जर्नी ऑफ लव' के बहाने इस बार बात भारतीय राजनीति की उस घटना की, जिसने देश की राजनीति और सोनिया गांधी की जिंदगी हमेशा के लिए बदल दी पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री राजीव गांधी की हत्या.
21 मई 1991 को श्रीपेरंबदूर में राजीव गांधी की हत्या की साजिश कैसे रची गई? हमलावर कौन थे? जांच एजेंसियां 90 दिनों के भीतर हत्यारों और उनके नेटवर्क तक कैसे पहुंचीं? और क्या इस साजिश की सभी परतें कभी सामने आ पाईं?
बीबीसी संवाददाता मोहन लाल शर्मा ने बात की राजीव गांधी हत्याकांड की प्रत्यक्षदर्शी नीना गोपाल, हत्याकांड की जांच करने वाले पूर्व आईपीएस अधिकारी आमोद कंठ और इस घटना की जांच पर किताब लिखने वाले लेखक-पत्रकार अनिरुद्ध मित्रा से.
